sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 1.5 Summary 1.5 Summary This chapter began with covering what QM is and the importance of QM integration with logistics and areas of supply chain management. The QM master data objects are important during processes relevant for ensuring product quality. We continued with the business processes within QM, starting with quality engineering. Then, we also quickly showed you how QM relates to the rest of the SAP S/4HANA landscape, as it’s important to understand the enterprise structure of various SAP S/4HANA systems that you’ll use throughout the book. Setting up the correct and complete enterprise struc- ture is one of the key success factors for ensuring effective reporting that eventually helps in making important and strategic business decisions. The chapter also covered how SAP S/4HANA supports the ISO 9001 certification process. In the next chapter, we begin our journey in the QM area with a look at quality plan- ning. Internal audit: An audit pro- gram must be planned— criteria, scope, frequency, and methods must be defined— and records must be main- tained. Audit management is directly supported by the SAP S/4HANA system. You can also use the quality notification to document and trace audits. Improvements (corrective and preventive action): Corrective measures must evaluate errors, including customer complaints. You’ll find the direct implementation of these requirements in the QM and PP areas in particu- lar. You can create, trace, and determine causes, prevent recurring errors, initiate mea- sures, record results, and evaluate measures. Preventive measures must determine possible errors and causes, prevent the occurrence of errors, initiate actions, record results, and evaluate actions; corrective and preven- tive actions work directly through error recording for the inspection results and the use decision. You can use your own action catalogs or initiate individual measures or actions using free texts and quality notifications, and you can trace and monitor these over time. All information and quality records are available from in-process and final inspec- tions involving production. You can record customer com- plaints, initiate corresponding actions, and further trace them via the quality notification. The SAP S/4HANA system can provide information at any time on all actions, steps, and their processing status, as well as provide information for a QM evaluation. Standard ISO 9001 Requirement Implementation Option in SAP S/4HANA Table 1.2 How SAP S/4HANA Supports the ISO 9001 Certification (Cont.) ©
sections.he: הפרק פתח במהות QM ובחשיבות האינטגרציה עם הלוגיסטיקה ושרשרת האספקה. אובייקטי נתוני האב חשובים בתהליכים להבטחת איכות. המשכנו בתהליכי QM, החל מהנדסת איכות, ובקשר של QM לשאר ה-S/4HANA landscape (חשוב להבין את המבנה הארגוני של המערכות בספר). הקמת מבנה ארגוני נכון ומלא — גורם הצלחה מרכזי לדיווח יעיל ולהחלטות אסטרטגיות. הפרק כיסה גם כיצד S/4HANA תומך בהסמכת ISO 9001. הפרק הבא — תכנון איכות (quality planning).

sections.title: Quality Management View in Material Master
sections.en: 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Let’s now delve into discussing and maintaining the important master data of Table 2.1. 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master When a company decides to implement QM to integrate its business processes with logistics and the supply chain and to bring about improvements to business processes, one of the very first master data maintenance tasks required is maintaining the Quality management view of the material master. The material master record in the SAP system is a complex and central entity, the pur- pose of which is to control business and logistical processes. For the sake of clarity and visibility, the system divides the material master record into different views. Maintain- ing master data is a combined and collective responsibility of various departments or persons. There is also the Quality management view (see Figure 2.1) of the material master. If this view of the material isn’t available initially, the person responsible for the material master record can add it later at any time. This has no effect on any part of the logistics process (e.g., inventory management, procurement, production). The functions for inspection-lot creation, stock posting, and—in particular—QM procure- ment control are activated later, when the Quality management view is maintained further. You set up an inspection type in the Quality management view of the material master, which acts as a control function for all subsequent activities. An inspection type is the basic identifier for the different types of inspections available in the SAP system. To add an inspection type to a material master, use Transaction MM02 or follow menu path SAP  Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Material  Change  Immediately. In the screen that appears, enter Material “RM17” and Plant “1710”, and then click Quality Management to go to the Quality management view, as shown in Figure 2.1. Material specification QM/MM Material master record Quality info record: procure- ment QM/MM Procurement Quality info record: sales QM/SAP S/4HANA Sales Sales General Master Data Area(s) Use in QM Table 2.1 Master Data of QM and Its Use in Other Logistics Areas (Cont.) 2 Quality Planning 60 Figure 2.1 Quality Management View of Material Master Tips and Tricks If the Quality management view hasn’t been previously maintained, use Transaction MM01 to create the Quality management view of the material master first. Figure 2.1 shows the Quality management view of material RM17 for plant 1710, which includes the following important fields:  QM Material Auth. (authorization) helps to control who is authorized to perform inspection-related tasks on this material. This field also controls the digital signature in SAP, which is discussed in Chapter 3.  GR Processing Time is the average number of working days it takes it to process an inspection lot. The system uses this information during material requirements planning (MRP) to take the inspection duration into account while planning pro- curement, production, or availability of a material.  A Catalog Profile consists of defects and defect locations and is available during quality notification creation (see Chapter 12 for more details).  Material Status is the control function that allows or disallows the functions or busi- ness processes possible for this material. For example, a control function such as a material may be blocked from procurement, or the material may be obsolete.  Inspection Interval denotes the frequency with which a batch-managed material under- goes recurring (repeat) inspection. Recurring inspection is discussed in Chapter 9. © 61 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master The control functions in the Procurement Data area are covered in Chapter 4. Click on the Insp. Setup button in Figure 2.1 to go to Figure 2.2, which shows the initial screen of Inspection Setup Data. Because no inspection type existed when you first clicked on the Insp. Setup button, you’ll find a blank screen. You can incorporate or set up a new inspection type with the Inspection Types button shown in Figure 2.2. Inspection type 01 is relevant for the quality inspection of raw material (or other procured materials) on goods receipt against a purchase order. It’s important to note that assignment of an inspection type to a material is plant-specific. You can assign more than one inspection type to a material. For example, a batch-man- aged finished good with a shelf-life expiration date is inspected on its production com- pletion (known as goods receipt inspection against production order), but then the same finished good also undergoes periodic inspection if it remains unsold and its batch’s shelf life is about to expire (known as recurring inspection). Figure 2.2 Inspection Setup Data 2 Quality Planning 62 Consider another example: the company’s business process requires inspection of a raw material at the supplier’s premises for compliance with important quality parameters prior to its delivery into the company’s warehouse (known as source inspection). The same raw material will again go through another round of quality inspection when the goods reach the company’s warehouse (known as goods receipt inspection against the purchase order). This requires activation of two different inspection types. The first inspection type is for inspection at the supplier premises, and the second inspection type is for inspection at the company’s premises. When you want to activate a specific inspection type, you need to ensure that the Active checkbox is selected. Due to changes in the business process, if a particular inspection type is no longer needed, simply dese- lecting the Active checkbox deactivates it. This is the easiest way to deactivate an inspec- tion type at any time. You can also delete the entire inspection type, if needed. Based on your business needs and at any point in time, you can add a new inspection type or make changes to control indicators of an already existing inspection type in Inspection Setup. Warning On deactivating or deleting an inspection type, you first have to ensure that there is no quality stock. Now, click Insp. type det. (inspection type details; the right button [the magnifying glass]) to view the details of the fields and other options available for inspection type 01. Table 2.2 explains some of the important fields of Figure 2.2. Control Indicator Effects Post to Insp. Stock Posts a goods movement to the inspection stock for the material. Only in the QM area, within the scope of the usage decision, can you release anything out of quality inspection stock. In an exceptional case, the movement type itself enables the system to determine whether to post the quantity to inspection stock. Insp. with Mat Spec. With this indicator set, you can use a material specifica- tion to carry out an inspection. An inspection that uses a material specification can be in addition to, or even replace, an inspection that uses a routing or a master rec- ipe. You need to completely maintain a material specifica- tion for the material to carry out an inspection. Refer to Section 2.12 on how to set up a material specification. Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup © 63 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Insp. with Task List With this indicator set, the system requires a task list for an inspection with the inspection lot. The decision on whether a routing or a master recipe is required is made during inspection data maintenance in the material mas- ter record. The system can only determine the sample size after assignment of the task list to the inspection lot. In Chapter 3, you’ll see that when the system is unable to find and assign a task list to an inspection lot, it’s unable to calculate the sample size. Insp. by Configuration If this indicator is set, the system takes configurations from the sales order or production order into account in inspection-lot creation. Automatic Assignment The system tries to automatically assign a routing, an inspection plan, or a material specification to the inspec- tion lot. Inspect Charcs If you want characteristic-based results recording, you have to use a routing, an inspection plan, or a material specification for the inspection. Characteristic-based results recording is a prerequisite for characteristic-based dynamic modification. You can select a dynamic modifi- cation level in an inspection plan. Smpl. Procedure A procedure to determine the size of the sample in an inspection. The sampling procedure also defines the valu- ation type used for results recording (attributive, variable, manual, etc.). This field is of significance only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing, master recipe, or material specifica- tion. If you enter a sampling procedure here, the system calculates the total sample size from the lot size. Select a sampling procedure that uses a valuation mode without valuation parameters. In the case of an inspection without a routing, master rec- ipe, or material specification, you have the following options to determine the inspection scope for a specific material:  100% inspection  Specify a percentage  Specify a sampling procedure without valuation parameters Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) 2 Quality Planning 64 100% Inspection There are two possible business scenarios that you need to consider while setting up this indicator:  Inspect without routing, master recipe, or material specification The system creates the sample size as equal to the cre- ated lot.  Inspect with routing, master recipe, or material speci- fication The sample size of the created lot is the same as the lot size. The sampling procedure set down in the inspection plan or specification isn’t taken into account in the sample determination process for the inspection characteristics. Instead, the system uses sample determination rules, which are preset in the configuration. The sample size of the created charac- teristics depends on whether the base unit of measure has decimal places. If the base unit of measure does have decimal places, the sample size of the character- istic is always 1; if the base unit of measure doesn’t have decimal places, 100% of the lot size should be inspected in sample units of measure (rounded up) for the characteristic. Here, the dependencies are that if in addition to either 100% inspection, Inspect with Task List, or Insp. by Config- uration indicators, you also set the Skips Allowed charac- teristic, nothing changes in the sample calculation. However, the system does check whether the characteris- tic is to be inspected or not. Inspection % This field is of significance only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing, master recipe, task list, or material specification. In this case, the system calculates the over- all sample size using this percentage value from the inspection lot size. Manual Sample Calc. Set this indicator if you want to manually trigger the sam- ple calculation for the inspection lot. Manual Sample Entry If this checkbox is selected, then you need to manually enter the sample size for the inspection of this inspection lot. This characteristic is only taken into account in inspections that don’t use a routing, task list, or material specification. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) © 65 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Dyn. Mod. Rule This is for the dynamic modification rule. It contains defi- nitions of the inspection levels and the conditions that cause inspection levels to change. This field is significant only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing or mate- rial specification. If you enter a dynamic modification rule here, a quality level for the material, plant, and inspection type is set, and when the quality level is created automat- ically, the system calculates the dynamic modification cri- teria for the inspection-lot origin. If, in addition to the sample size, you control using a sampling procedure, the system checks whether the combination of dynamic modification rule and sampling procedure is permitted (permitted relationships). Refer to Chapter 3, which cov- ers the dynamic modification rule in detail. Skips Allowed If you set this indicator, then the system allows skipping results recording for inspection characteristics when it calculates the sample size of the lot. The characteristic takes effect in the inspection lot if it’s set in the QM inspection data of the material for the inspection type in question. If the characteristic isn’t set in the dynamic modification process, the system selects the next nonskip inspection level instead of a skip level. If all the characteristics to be inspected in an inspection lot have the Skip status, it results in a skip inspection lot. In the case of a skip lot, if both skips and automatic usage decision are allowed, inspection-lot processing is carried out without any user intervention. A time delay can be set for this in the configuration. This triggers unrestricted stock at the goods receipt stage because the lot quantity is immediately posted to unrestricted-use stock. In the QM control function in procurement (quality infor- mation record), you can make a setting that skips the goods receipt inspections. You can also specify for the material in the inspection data that an inspection is to be carried out only for the first goods receipt per order or production order. To prevent individual characteristics from being skipped, proceed as follows:  Assign characteristic weightings to the characteristics to prevent skips.  Assign sampling procedures to the characteristics that don’t permit stage changes. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) 2 Quality Planning 66 Automatic UD If you set this indicator, the system can automatically make usage decisions for inspection lots. The inspection lots have to fulfill the following conditions:  All characteristics are completed.  No characteristic has been rejected.  No defects have been recorded, and no quality notifi- cation has been created. The lead time set in configuration must have expired. Inspection lots with the status Skip Lot can also be con- sidered here. If an automatic usage decision can’t be made, you’ll have to make it manually. The system records an automatic usage decision in the long text that accompanies the usage decision. Chapter 3 shows you how to make automatic usage deci- sions for skipped inspection lots. Avg. Insp. Duration Specifies the average duration, in days, of the inspection for every inspection type. If the start date of the inspec- tion is entered during inspection-lot creation, the system calculates the end date using the average inspection time entered in this field. Conversely, if the end date of the inspection is entered during inspection-lot creation, the system calculates the start date using the average inspec- tion time entered in this field. Q-Score Procedure The coded ID of the procedure that the system uses to cal- culate the quality score. You can maintain one quality score procedure per inspection type in the material mas- ter record. The system transfers the information main- tained in this field to the inspection lot record on inspection lot creation. In the simplest procedure, the quality score is taken from the code for the usage decision. In another procedure, the quality score is calculated on the basis of the scrap share in the inspected characteristics. Allowed Scrap Share Some quality score procedures require an allowed scrap share to calculate the quality score. In normal cases, the scrap share is set to be half the acceptable quality level (AQL) value. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) © 67 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Control Lot Creation This control applies to goods receipt for inspection lot ori- gins 01, 04, 05, and 08. You can make the following settings:  <Space>: One inspection lot per goods receipt docu- ment item. In other words, one inspection lot is cre- ated for each goods receipt document item.  X: One inspection lot per purchase order item or order item and batch. If you set this value, the system cre- ates an inspection lot only for the first goods receipt for each purchase order item or production order, or, if the material is managed in batches, only for the first goods receipt per purchase order item or production order and batch. This setting is restricted to the inspec- tion lot origins For Purchase Order (Inspection Lot Ori- gin 01) and For Production Order (Inspection Lot Origin 04).  1: One inspection lot per material document, material, and batch. If you set this value, the system opens only one inspection lot per material and batch (in the case of batch management) for a material document (i.e., within a goods receipt transaction). This can occur if several purchase orders or several partial deliveries of the same material are processed within one goods receipt transaction.  2: One inspection lot per material and batch. If you set this value, the system opens only one inspection lot per material and batch (in the case of batch manage- ment). This setting is useful only for materials that require batch management. In the case of X, 1, and 2, if the stock of the inspection lot that was created with the first goods receipt isn’t com- pletely discharged or its usage decision made when fur- ther partial deliveries are received, these goods receipt quantities are added to this stock. In the case of 1 and 2, if Skip Lot is set, there is no direct change of the stock type from In Quality Inspection to Unrestricted Use. Instead, a transfer posting takes place as part of an automatic usage decision with a time delay. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) 2 Quality Planning 68 Tips and Tricks When you’re maintaining the control indicator of the inspection data, we recommend that you use the predefined and default configuration settings for each inspection type. This is important because different entries for the same inspection type cause different materials to be used or cause difficulties with the inspection-lot generation process. If a special inspection lot control process is required on the material level for the same inspection type, this must be carefully documented in each individual case. For more information, see Chapter 3, which covers the configuration details of main- taining default values for inspection types. Table 2.3 contains a selective list of inspection types of respective inspection origins that we cover in various chapters of this book. The last column is the number of the chapter in which you’ll find detailed configuration, master data setup, requirements, or business processes that use the specific inspection type. Individual QM order This characteristic specifies that you need to create an individual QM order with an account assignment when the system creates an inspection lot for this inspection type. If you set this characteristic, you’re specifying that an individual QM order should be opened for this combi- nation of material and inspection type. If the field for the QM order is filled and the characteristic for individual QM orders is set, this field is taken into account only if the system is unable to create an individ- ual QM order due to a missing account assignment in the inspection lot. A prerequisite for creating an individual QM order is that the inspection lot contains an allocation provision such as sales order, cost center, or plant. QM Order A number that uniquely identifies the QM order to which the costs are to be charged. The QM order specified in the material master record in the inspection data is used as a template for inspection-lot creation if an individual QM order hasn’t been created for the inspection lot. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) © 69 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Inspection Origin Inspection Type Task List Usage Inspection Type Description Chapter 01 01 5 Incoming inspection for goods receipt for purchase order 4 01 0101 501 Model inspection for goods receipt for purchase order 4 01 0102 502 Goods receipt inspection, pilot run 4 01 0130 53 Goods receipt inspection at goods receipt from external processing 4 02 02 6 Goods issue inspection 5 03 03 1 In-process inspection for pro- duction order 5 04 04 5 Final inspection for goods receipt from production 5 05 05 5 Inspection for other goods receipts 4 06 06 6 Inspection for customer returns 6 07 07 3 Audit inspection 14 08 08 5 Stock-transfer inspection 4 08 0800 9 Inspection lot with inspection stock at QM activation 4 09 09 9 Recurring inspection 4 10 10 6 Inspection for delivery to cus- tomer (with order) 6 11 11 6 Inspection for delivery to cus- tomer (without order) 6 12 12 6 General inspection for delivery 6 13 13 1 In-process inspection for run schedule header 6 14 14 4 Plant maintenance inspection 7 15 15 9 Inspection of physical samples 10 16 16 9 Inspection of storage condi- tions (stability studies) 15 Table 2.3 Inspection Types 2 Quality Planning 70 Note In project discussions, requests are often made to create new inspection types to meet specific business needs, such as inspection types that reflect different strategies for incoming inspections for fundamentally different materials. Even if you configure new or extra inspection types, the problem still remains. This is because the inspection ori- gins to which you have to assign the inspection type are preconfigured and delivered. You therefore have no choice but to individually change the relevant control indicators under Inspection Data in the Quality management view of the material. In such a case, the only configuration tasks are to customize the short name of the inspection type and the global control indicator for each existing inspection type. For this reason, we don’t recommend that you create new inspection types to meet this business need. Chapter 3 shows how you can configure a new inspection type and use it in business processes.
sections.he:
אחת ממשימות נתוני האב הראשונות ביישום QM היא תחזוקת תצוגת Quality management של אב החומר.
רשומת אב החומר היא ישות מורכבת ומרכזית לבקרת תהליכים עסקיים ולוגיסטיים. המערכת מחלקת אותה לתצוגות. תחזוקה היא אחריות משותפת של מחלקות. תצוגת Quality management (Figure 2.1) — אם אינה זמינה בתחילה, ניתן להוסיפה בכל עת ללא השפעה על הלוגיסטיקה. פונקציות יצירת inspection lot, רישום מלאי, ובפרט בקרת רכש QM — מופעלות מאוחר, בתחזוקת התצוגה.
מגדירים inspection type בתצוגה — פונקציית בקרה לכל הפעילויות. ה-inspection type הוא המזהה הבסיסי לסוגי הבדיקות.
להוספה: Transaction MM02 או SAP • Logistics • Materials Management • Material Master • Material • Change • Immediately. הזינו Material "RM17", ‏Plant "1710", ובחרו Quality Management (Figure 2.1).
(טבלה 2.1 — נתוני אב QM: ‏Material specification [QM/MM, אב החומר]; ‏Quality info record: procurement [QM/MM, רכש]; ‏Quality info record: sales [QM/Sales, מכירות].)
**Tips and Tricks:** אם התצוגה לא תוחזקה, השתמשו ב-Transaction MM01 ליצירתה.
שדות חשובים (Figure 2.1):
• **QM Material Auth.:** מי מורשה לבצע בדיקות; שולט גם בחתימה הדיגיטלית (פרק 3).
• **GR Processing Time:** מספר ימי העבודה הממוצע לעיבוד inspection lot; ‏MRP משקלל אותו.
• **Catalog Profile:** פגמים ומיקומי-פגם, זמין ביצירת quality notification (פרק 12).
• **Material Status:** מתיר/אוסר פונקציות (למשל חסום מרכש, מיושן).
• **Inspection Interval:** תדירות הבדיקה החוזרת (recurring) לחומר מנוהל-אצווה (פרק 9).
(בקרות אזור Procurement Data — פרק 4.)
בחרו Insp. Setup (Figure 2.2 — מסך ריק כי אין inspection type). הוסיפו ב-Inspection Types. סוג 01 רלוונטי לבדיקת גלם (או נרכש אחר) ב-goods receipt מול הזמנת רכש. ההקצאה ספציפית-מפעל. ניתן מספר סוגים לחומר. למשל, גמור מנוהל-אצווה עם תפוגה — נבדק בהשלמת ייצור (GR מול הזמנת ייצור), ואז recurring בהתקרב התפוגה.
דוגמה נוספת: בדיקת גלם אצל הספק (source inspection) ואז שוב במחסן (GR מול הזמנת רכש) — שני סוגים. להפעלה, סמנו Active; להשבתה, בטלו את הסימון; ניתן גם למחוק.
**אזהרה:** בהשבתה/מחיקה, ודאו תחילה שאין quality stock.
בחרו Insp. type det. (זכוכית מגדלת) לפרטי סוג 01.

טבלה 2.2 — הקמת inspection types (מחווני בקרה | השפעות):
| **Post to Insp. Stock** | רושם תנועה ל-inspection stock; שחרור רק ב-QM דרך usage decision (או שסוג התנועה קובע). |
| **Insp. with Mat Spec.** | שימוש ב-material specification לבדיקה (בנוסף או במקום routing/master recipe). יש לתחזק במלואו (2.12). |
| **Insp. with Task List** | המערכת דורשת task list ל-lot. ההחלטה (routing או master recipe) בתחזוקת נתוני הבדיקה. גודל הדגימה נקבע רק לאחר הקצאת ה-task list. |
| **Insp. by Configuration** | המערכת שוקלת תצורות מהזמנת מכירה/ייצור ביצירת ה-lot. |
| **Automatic Assignment** | המערכת מנסה להקצות אוטומטית routing/inspection plan/material specification. |
| **Inspect Charcs** | לרישום תוצאות מבוסס-מאפיין נדרש routing/inspection plan/material specification — תנאי מוקדם ל-dynamic modification מבוסס-מאפיין. |
| **Smpl. Procedure** | נוהל לקביעת גודל הדגימה; מגדיר גם valuation type (attributive/variable/manual). משמעותי רק בבדיקה ללא routing/master recipe/material specification. אפשרויות היקף: 100% inspection; אחוז; sampling procedure ללא valuation parameters. |
| **100% Inspection** | ללא routing/recipe/spec — גודל הדגימה = ה-lot. עם routing/recipe/spec — גודל הדגימה = ה-lot, אך ה-sampling procedure בתוכנית אינו נשקל; המערכת משתמשת בכללי דגימה מהתצורה (תלוי במקומות עשרוניים של יחידת הבסיס: עם עשרוניים — דגימה 1; ללא — 100% מעוגל). |
| **Inspection %** | משמעותי רק ללא routing/recipe/task list/spec — המערכת מחשבת את הדגימה לפי אחוז מ-lot. |
| **Manual Sample Calc.** | הפעלה ידנית של חישוב הדגימה. |
| **Manual Sample Entry** | הזנה ידנית של גודל הדגימה (רק ללא routing/task list/spec). |
| **Dyn. Mod. Rule** | כלל dynamic modification — רמות בדיקה ותנאי המעבר. משמעותי רק ללא routing/spec (פרק 3). |
| **Skips Allowed** | מאפשר דילוג על רישום תוצאות בחישוב הדגימה. אם כל המאפיינים בדילוג → skip inspection lot. עם automatic UD → עיבוד ללא התערבות (delay בתצורה), והכמות ל-unrestricted ב-GR. |
| **Automatic UD** | usage decision אוטומטי אם: כל המאפיינים הושלמו; אף אחד לא נדחה; אין פגמים/notification; ה-lead time פג. אחרת — ידני. |
| **Avg. Insp. Duration** | משך הבדיקה הממוצע (ימים) — המערכת מחשבת תאריך סיום/התחלה. |
| **Q-Score Procedure** | נוהל חישוב ה-quality score (מקוד ה-usage decision, או לפי scrap share). |
| **Allowed Scrap Share** | חלק פסולת מותר לחישוב ה-score (בד"כ חצי מערך ה-AQL). |
| **Control Lot Creation** | ל-origins 01/04/05/08: רווח = lot אחד לפריט מסמך GR; ‏X = lot אחד לפריט הזמנה+אצווה (ל-origins 01, 04); ‏1 = lot אחד למסמך חומר/חומר/אצווה; ‏2 = lot אחד לחומר/אצווה. ב-X/1/2, מנות חלקיות מתווספות; ב-1/2 עם Skip Lot — transfer posting ב-automatic UD עם delay. |
| **Individual QM order** | יצירת QM order נפרד עם הקצאת חשבון ביצירת ה-lot. תנאי — הקצאה (הזמנת מכירה/מרכז עלות/מפעל). |
| **QM Order** | מספר ה-QM order לחיוב העלויות; משמש תבנית אם לא נוצר individual. |

**Tips and Tricks:** השתמשו בהגדרות ברירת המחדל לכל סוג; תיעוד מוקפד לתהליך מיוחד (פרק 3).

sections.title: Master Record
sections.en: 2.2 Master Record This section covers the important QM master record, as well as other logistics areas needed in the SAP S/4HANA system to run business processes.
sections.he: סעיף זה מכסה את רשומת אב ה-QM החשובה ואת תחומי הלוגיסטיקה הנדרשים.

sections.title: Change Master Record
sections.en: 2.2.1 Change Master Record To manage the different versions of a drawing that belongs to a material master record, an inspection plan, or an inspection method, for example, it may be a good idea to also assign a version to every material. You can link every version of the material master record with a change master record. A change master record brings far greater control 16 1601 9 Initial test (stability study) 15 16 1602 9 Manual inspection lot for stor- age conditions 15 17 17 9 EWM inspection 8 17 1701 9 EWM: goods receipt inspection for purchase order 8 89 89 3 Other inspection 3 89 8914 4 Inspection checklists 7 Inspection Origin Inspection Type Task List Usage Inspection Type Description Chapter Table 2.3 Inspection Types (Cont.) © 71 2.2 Master Record and visibility to changes made to the QM master record, such as an inspection method or an inspection plan. Note See Chapter 13, which contains an example of using a change number to manage changes to an inspection plan.
sections.he:
לניהול גרסאות של שרטוט השייך לאב חומר, inspection plan, או inspection method — כדאי להקצות version לכל חומר. ניתן לקשר כל גרסה ל-change master record. ה-change master record מספק בקרה ונראות גדולות לשינויים ברשומת אב ה-QM (inspection method/plan).
**הערה:** ראו פרק 13 לדוגמה לשימוש ב-change number לניהול שינויים ב-inspection plan.

sections.title: Business Partner Master Record
sections.en: 2.2.2 Business Partner Master Record The supplier master record contains all the necessary information about a supplier from the purchasing and accounting points of view. In addition, the buyer can set a lock under the Lock Data option for quality reasons. This lock contains the same list entries as those in the quality info record for delivery control on the material supplier level. The details of the contact persons for purchasing and QM are stored in the part- ner data of the supplier master. The customer master record, on the other hand, contains all the necessary information about a customer from the point of view of sales and accounting. The buyer can also set a lock, if necessary, for quality reasons. This master record also contains partner data, such as the contact person in the customer’s company. It can be useful to maintain the details of a contact person responsible for quality matters.
sections.he:
רשומת אב הספק מכילה את כל המידע מנקודת מבט הרכש והחשבונאות. הקונה יכול לקבוע נעילה ב-Lock Data מסיבות איכות (אותן כניסות כמו ב-quality info record לבקרת משלוח ברמת חומר-ספק). פרטי אנשי הקשר לרכש ול-QM ב-partner data.
רשומת אב הלקוח מכילה את המידע מנקודת מבט המכירה והחשבונאות. הקונה יכול לקבוע נעילה מסיבות איכות. מכילה partner data (איש קשר בחברת הלקוח) — כדאי לתחזק אחראי לענייני איכות.

sections.title: Batch Master
sections.en: 2.2.3 Batch Master If the company maintains an externally procured material or an in-house material through batch management, the system creates a batch master record using Transac- tion MSC1N or menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Batch  Create. With the relevant configuration settings in place, the system can automatically assign a batch number, or a user can do so manually for goods movements or for pro- cess or production orders. If batch management is active for a material, the system requires a batch number during inspections and can also assign the inspection lot data to the batches. An important consideration for process industries is that it’s a requirement to separate various batches of a material according to their different properties. To this end, batches are divided into different classes, which are defined in advance in the batch characteristics. If during the inspection a batch fulfills the specification of a batch char- acteristic, it’s assigned to the relevant batch class. If a material with the required prop- erties is subsequently used for further processing or for a sales order, the batch classification finds the appropriate material. You also need the batch master record for order processing in production planning for process industries (PP-PI). 2 Quality Planning 72 Figure 2.3 shows the Basic Data 1 tab of batch 6 of material RM17, plant 1710, and storage location 0001. The system automatically fills in the date of manufacture, shelf-life expiration date/best-before date (SLED/BBD), and next inspection date while running relevant business processes. Figure 2.3 Batch Master Note See Chapter 9 on batch management, which also covers the master data requirements, as well as the business processes that either fill up or automatically update the various fields that you see in Figure 2.3.
sections.he:
אם החברה מנהלת חומר (נרכש או פנימי) באצוות, המערכת יוצרת batch master record ב-Transaction MSC1N או Logistics • Materials Management • Material Master • Batch • Create. עם התצורה, המספר מוקצה אוטומטית או ידנית. אם batch management פעיל, המערכת דורשת מספר אצווה בבדיקות ויכולה להקצות את נתוני ה-inspection lot לאצוות.
בתעשיות תהליכיות, חובה להפריד אצוות לפי תכונות — באמצעות classes המוגדרים ב-batch characteristics. אם בבדיקה אצווה ממלאת מפרט מאפיין, היא מוקצית ל-class. בשימוש עוקב/הזמנת מכירה, ה-classification מוצא את האצווה המתאימה. ה-batch master נדרש גם לעיבוד הזמנות ב-PP-PI.
Figure 2.3 — לשונית Basic Data 1 של אצווה 6 (חומר RM17, מפעל 1710, מיקום 0001). המערכת ממלאת אוטומטית date of manufacture, ‏SLED/BBD, ו-next inspection date.
**הערה:** ראו פרק 9 (batch management).

sections.title: Production Resources and Tools
sections.en: 2.2.4 Production Resources and Tools All the resources required for production, such as documents, operating supplies, test equipment, tools, equipment, and so on, are within the scope of production resources/ tools (PRTs). You need to assign the PRTs to the operations and inspection characteris- tics of a task list. Depending on the PRT type, the master record can be a material, doc- ument, PRT master record, or equipment master record. © 73
sections.he: כל המשאבים לייצור — מסמכים, חומרי עזר, ציוד בדיקה, כלים, ציוד — בהיקף PRTs (production resources/tools). יש להקצות PRTs לפעולות ולמאפייני הבדיקה ב-task list. לפי סוג ה-PRT, הרשומה יכולה להיות חומר, מסמך, PRT master record, או equipment master record.

sections.title: Work Center
sections.en: 2.5 Work Center Note See Chapter 7 on QM integration with PM (test equipment management), which also covers various types of PRTs. The chapter includes cross-elements from quality plan- ning, repairs and maintenance (calibration tests), and their master records (equipment).
sections.he: **הערה:** ראו פרק 7 (אינטגרציית QM עם PM — ניהול ציוד בדיקה), המכסה גם סוגי PRT ואלמנטים חוצים מתכנון איכות, תיקונים ואחזקה (בדיקות כיול), ורשומותיהם (equipment).

sections.title: Master Recipe or Routing
sections.en: 2.3 Master Recipe or Routing In this task list type, the work-scheduling function records all elements in the task plan- ning area, and the QM function records all data for inspection planning. The produc- tion steps and capacities are linked to the work centers, and the required control functions for the production order are determined. The elements of inspection plan- ning, inspection characteristics, sampling procedure, and so on are fully integrated into the master recipe or routing.
sections.he: בסוג task list זה, פונקציית work-scheduling רושמת את כל האלמנטים בתכנון המשימות, ופונקציית ה-QM רושמת את נתוני תכנון הבדיקה. צעדי הייצור והקיבולות מקושרים ל-work centers, ופונקציות הבקרה להזמנת הייצור נקבעות. אלמנטי תכנון הבדיקה (inspection characteristics, ‏sampling procedure) משולבים במלואם ב-master recipe או routing.

sections.title: Reference Operation Set
sections.en: 2.4 Reference Operation Set The reference operation set contains virtually all the objects and functions of the rout- ing. It’s used mainly as a task list template for variations of a production procedure or as a general template. The individual operations in the reference operation set are refer- enced for this purpose in the routing or in the inspection plan (a fixed reference; every change in the reference operation set affects the inspection plan and the routing). Note The reference operation set, routing, and inspection plan are the same in terms of their structure and essential functions. This makes navigating in the different task list types quite simple for the inspection planner, who has to maintain the quality-relevant data in all task list types. Chapter 5 on production processes also covers details of the master recipe, routing, and reference operation set master data. 2.5 Work Center A quality work center is the physical or virtual location in which a user performs related quality inspection activities. A work center is always plant-specific. The work center is a master record that’s important mainly for PP and controlling. It’s likewise usually maintained by the Production Planning and Control department. Every work center is assigned to a cost center so that the accounting department can analyze quality costs. To this end, the system calculates the costs that arise from the work performed at the work center on the basis of the allocation records for the individual cost centers. 2 Quality Planning 74 To create a work center for quality inspection, use Transaction CRQI or follow menu path SAP  Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Work Center  QM Work Center  Work Center  Create. In the screen that appears, enter Plant “1710” and Work Center “QCLAB”, and then enter the Work Center Category “0003”. There are various categories available in the SAP sys- tem. A category groups together similar work being performed at the work center. Exam- ples of work center categories are machine, labor, production line, and quality inspection. On the screen shown in Figure 2.4, enter a short text to provide some details about the type of work center and the work performed in it. A person responsible is the in-charge or supervisor of the quality control lab. This can be an individual or a position. In gen- eral, the position option is preferred because a person may move to another depart- ment or leave the job. Figure 2.4 Work Center Enter Usage “009”, which acts as a control function to allow or disallow the activities the work center is used for. For example, a work center with the usage Plant Mainte- nance only allows maintenance-related activities to be associated with the work center. Similarly, a production work center (or a production line) is used for production- related activities in which, for example, the user doesn’t perform quality inspection- related activities. These controls manage the usage in a work center. A work center with all usage types is denoted as universal. Choose the Default Values tab, and enter Con- trol Key “QM04” (see Figure 2.5). © 75 2.5 Work Center Figure 2.5 Assigning the Control Key in the Default Values Tab A control key manages a set of activities that the user can or can’t perform for a work center. Select the Control key field dropdown, and the screen in Figure 2.6 appears. The details of control key QM04 are shown here when you click Detailed information, located on the lower right side of the screen. In the lower half of the screen, notice that the Insp. Char. Required checkbox is selected. This means that for work center QCLAB, the assignment of control key QM04 enables the system to assign master inspection characteristics, which are then used for quality inspection purposes. Similarly, select- ing the Print checkbox enables the printing option for all the activities that a user per- forms on this work center. Figure 2.6 Control Key 2 Quality Planning 76
sections.he:
ה-reference operation set מכיל כמעט את כל האובייקטים והפונקציות של ה-routing. משמש בעיקר כתבנית task list לווריאציות של נוהל ייצור או כתבנית כללית. הפעולות מקושרות (reference קבוע) ב-routing או ב-inspection plan — כל שינוי ב-set משפיע עליהם.
**הערה:** ה-reference operation set, ה-routing וה-inspection plan זהים במבנה ובפונקציות — מקל על המתכנן לתחזק נתונים בכל סוגי ה-task list. (פרטים — פרק 5.)

**2.5 Work Center:** ה-quality work center הוא המיקום הפיזי/הווירטואלי שבו המשתמש מבצע בדיקות. תמיד ספציפי-מפעל. רשומת אב חשובה ל-PP ולבקרה, מתוחזקת ע"י Production Planning and Control. כל work center מוקצה ל-cost center לניתוח עלויות איכות.
ליצירה: Transaction CRQI או SAP • Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Basic Data • Work Center • QM Work Center • Work Center • Create. הזינו Plant "1710", ‏Work Center "QCLAB", ‏Work Center Category "0003" (קטגוריה מקבצת עבודה דומה — מכונה, עבודה, קו ייצור, quality inspection).
ב-Figure 2.4, הזינו טקסט קצר ו-person responsible (עדיף position על אדם — תפקיד עשוי להשתנות).
הזינו Usage "009" (פונקציית בקרה לפעילויות המותרות). work center עם כל הסוגים = universal. בלשונית Default Values, הזינו Control Key "QM04" (Figure 2.5).
ה-control key מנהל את הפעילויות (Figure 2.6). בפרטי QM04 (Detailed information), תיבת Insp. Char. Required מסומנת — מאפשרת הקצאת master inspection characteristics לבדיקה. ‏Print מאפשר הדפסה.

sections.title: Inspection Method
sections.en: 2.6 Inspection Method An inspection method offers the provision to maintain detailed instructions for con- ducting physical or chemical quality tests of a material. The quality inspector can refer to the relevant inspection method for information or instruction while conducting an actual test. An inspection method can have several versions, which you can use to dif- ferentiate among various validity periods. To create an inspection method, use Transaction QS31 or follow menu path SAP  Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Method  Create. On the initial screen that appears, enter Insp. Method (inspection method) “QMINSP10” and Plant “1710”. You don’t need to enter the inspection method number or a date because the system automatically assigns an internal number to the inspection method and proposes a current date for the creation of the inspection method. Notice that it’s also possible to create a new inspection method by referencing an existing one. To create a new inspection method with reference to an already created inspection method, enter the details of reference fields such as plant, inspection method, key date, and version, and the system automatically copies all the information from the refer- ence inspection method to the new one. You can then change or update the new inspection method accordingly, saving data entry efforts. Tips and Tricks The option to create QM master data using templates or the copy function is generally available, and you can use it to quickly maintain master data, saving time and effort, as well as reducing data entry errors. In Figure 2.7, set the Status to 2 Released; this makes the inspection method available during subsequent QM activities in which you use the inspection method. If the status of the inspection method is set to Being Created, it isn’t available in further QM activities. You can enter a short text, and a good search term always helps in finding the relevant information when you’re searching in the system. An entry in the Authorization Group field controls authorization to create or make changes, or even display an inspection method. You may want to allow very few people access to make changes to an inspec- tion method because it’s critical, sensitive information. Inspector Qualific. (inspector qualification) is the minimum credential or experience a person must have to perform the tasks listed in an inspection method—for example, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) certified quality inspector or total quality management (TQM) accredited expert. Choose Long Text to create the long text of the inspection method; the system provides the option to write details of the inspection steps and procedures in the inspection method. It provides a Microsoft Word editor, with all the options normally available in Microsoft Word. In addition, there’s no limit to the amount of information you can enter as long text. When you finish entering © 77
sections.he:
inspection method מאפשר תחזוקת הוראות מפורטות לבדיקות פיזיות/כימיות. הבודק מתייחס אליו במהלך הבדיקה. יכול לכלול מספר גרסאות (תקופות תוקף).
ליצירה: Transaction QS31 או SAP • Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Basic Data • Inspection Method • Create. הזינו Insp. Method "QMINSP10", ‏Plant "1710". אין צורך במספר/תאריך (מוקצים אוטומטית). ניתן ליצור בהפניה לקיים — הזינו plant/method/key date/version וההעתקה אוטומטית.
**Tips and Tricks:** יצירת נתוני אב QM בתבניות/העתקה זמינה בד"כ — חוסכת זמן ומפחיתה שגיאות.
ב-Figure 2.7, קבעו Status ל-2 Released (זמין לפעילויות עוקבות; אם Being Created — אינו זמין). הזינו טקסט קצר ומונח חיפוש. ‏Authorization Group שולט בהרשאות יצירה/שינוי/הצגה (מידע קריטי — הגבילו). ‏Inspector Qualific. — הכישור המינימלי (כגון בודק מוסמך OSHA, מומחה TQM). בחרו Long Text לפרטי הצעדים (עורך Word, ללא הגבלה). בסיום, ‏Back, אישור — Text Messages Were Transferred.
**הערה:** ניתן לשלב classification לשיפור החיפוש, ומסמכים נוספים (שרטוטים, flowcharts) דרך DMS (פרק 20).

sections.title: Quality Agreements
sections.en: 2.7 Quality Agreements long text, click Back, and the system prompts you to confirm the details of the long text. The message Text Messages Were Transferred appears. Figure 2.7 Inspection Method Note You can also integrate classification with the inspection method to improve the searching inspection methods. You can also integrate additional documents, such as drawings, flowcharts, or process instructions, by integrating inspection methods with DMS. Chapter 20 discusses DMS in detail. 2.7 Quality Agreements Document Management System (DMS) discussed in Chapter 20 provides a wide range of document management functions that you can use both inside (documents) and outside (e.g., Microsoft Office documents) the SAP system. Documents can be anything from drawings from external CAD systems to specification texts. For the purposes of 2 Quality Planning 78 quality planning, documents are defined as PRTs. Inspection instructions and work regulations are examples. The standard offering in the SAP system provides preconfigured DMS document types that you can put to immediate use to maintain quality agreements and technical deliv- ery terms with suppliers or customers, which we’ll discuss in the following sections.
sections.he:
ה-DMS (פרק 20) מספק פונקציות ניהול מסמכים בתוך SAP (documents) ומחוצה לה (Office). מסמכים — שרטוטי CAD, טקסטי מפרט. לתכנון איכות, המסמכים מוגדרים כ-PRTs (הוראות בדיקה, תקנות עבודה).
המערכת מספקת סוגי מסמכי DMS מוגדרים-מראש לתחזוקת quality agreements ותנאי משלוח טכניים עם ספקים/לקוחות.

sections.title: Quality Assurance Agreement with Suppliers
sections.en: 2.7.1 Quality Assurance Agreement with Suppliers Quality agreements with suppliers enable the company to ensure that unless and until these agreements are already in place, the system won’t allow any procurement activity. To create a quality assurance agreement with a supplier, use Transaction QV01 or fol- low menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Quality Info Record: Procurement  Quality Assurance Agreement  Create. In the initial screen that appears, the system uses standard and preconfigured document type Q01. Simply press (Enter) once (while ensuring that the Document Type field is filled as “Q01”), and the screen in Figure 2.8 appears. Notice that the header of the quality assur- ance agreement uses the description of the DMS document type Q01. Enter the short description, and maintain the status of the agreement. Figure 2.8 Quality Assurance Agreement © 79 2.7 Quality Agreements In the Originals area, you can upload various documents, such as PDF or Microsoft Word files. Choose Object Links, and the screen in Figure 2.9 appears. Here, enter the previously created QM info record, which is the relationship between supplier and material, by entering the Material, Supplier, and Plant details. Save the quality assur- ance agreement; the system brings up the message that the document has been cre- ated. Figure 2.9 Object Links Note If a quality info record isn’t created yet, refer to Section 2.8 to first create it, and then proceed with creating the quality assurance agreement.
sections.he:
הסכמי איכות עם ספקים מבטיחים שעד שאינם קיימים, המערכת לא תתיר רכש.
ליצירה: Transaction QV01 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Logistics Master Data • Quality Info Record: Procurement • Quality Assurance Agreement • Create. המערכת משתמשת בסוג מסמך Q01. ‏Enter (Document Type = "Q01") (Figure 2.8). הכותרת משתמשת בתיאור Q01. הזינו תיאור קצר וסטטוס.
ב-Originals ניתן להעלות מסמכים (PDF, ‏Word). בחרו Object Links (Figure 2.9), הזינו את ה-QM info record (יחס ספק-חומר) — Material, ‏Supplier, ‏Plant. שמרו.
**הערה:** אם ה-quality info record לא נוצר, ראו 2.8.

sections.title: Quality Assurance Agreements with Customers
sections.en: 2.7.2 Quality Assurance Agreements with Customers To create quality assurance agreements with customers, use Transaction QV21 or fol- low menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Quality Info Record: SD  SD Documents  Quality Assurance Agreement. Here, the system uses document type Q03, and the available object links are Customer, QM Info Record: SD, and Quality Notification.
sections.he: ליצירת הסכמי איכות עם לקוחות: Transaction QV21 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Logistics Master Data • Quality Info Record: SD • SD Documents • Quality Assurance Agreement. המערכת משתמשת בסוג מסמך Q03; ה-object links — Customer, ‏QM Info Record: SD, ‏Quality Notification.

sections.title: Technical Delivery Terms with Customers
sections.en: 2.7.3 Technical Delivery Terms with Customers To maintain technical delivery terms with customers, use Transaction QV31 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Quality Info Record: SD  SD Documents  Technical Delivery Terms. Here, the system uses document type Q04, and the available object links are QM Info Record: SD and Quality Notification. 2 Quality Planning 80 Tips and Tricks Companies procure raw materials from suppliers and sell semifinished or finished goods to customers; therefore, assigning relevant control keys to the respective mate- rial masters makes sense in terms of controls that you want on quality assurance agreements with suppliers or customers.
sections.he:
לתחזוקת תנאי משלוח טכניים עם לקוחות: Transaction QV31 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Logistics Master Data • Quality Info Record: SD • SD Documents • Technical Delivery Terms. סוג מסמך Q04; ה-object links — QM Info Record: SD ו-Quality Notification.
**Tips and Tricks:** חברות רוכשות גלם ומוכרות גמורים — הקצאת control keys לאבי החומר הגיונית לבקרות על ההסכמים.

sections.title: Quality Information Record
sections.en: 2.8 Quality Information Record A quality information record is a one-to-one supply or buy relationship between a material and a supplier or a customer, respectively. To bring greater visibility to this relationship, the quality information record further subdivides into procurement and sales. Figure 2.10 shows the Quality Agreement tab of a quality information record for procurement and how the system incorporates the quality assurance agreement that you created in Figure 2.8. The Quality Agreement tab contains the same quality agree- ment, document 10000000680. Figure 2.10 Quality Agreements in the Quality Information Record
sections.he: quality information record הוא יחס 1:1 של אספקה/קנייה בין חומר לספק או לקוח. לנראות, מתחלק ל-procurement ו-sales. Figure 2.10 — לשונית Quality Agreement של רשומת רכש, וכיצד המערכת משלבת את ההסכם מ-Figure 2.8 (מסמך 10000000680).

sections.title: Master Inspection Characteristics
sections.en: 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics A master inspection characteristic denotes the physical or chemical property of the product that the company wants to monitor and control from a quality perspective. There are two types: © 81 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics  Qualitative  Quantitative A quantitative characteristic defines a physical or chemical property of a material as a numerical value (e.g., 2.3 kg, 1.8 lbs., or 11 ft.). Qualitative characteristics are attributes of a material or property having to do with nonnumerical qualities (e.g., smooth, pitted, and rusted for a surface, or red, tan, and brown for paint/color). You use master inspection characteristics when creating task lists as copy templates, or you reference (include) them in the inspection plan. The individual objects and control functions are the same as those of the characteristic in the inspection plan. From the organizational point of view, the master inspection characteristics, like the inspection plans, are assigned to the plant. Let’s now look at the steps necessary to get master inspection characteristics up and running in your system.
sections.he:
master inspection characteristic (MIC) מציין את התכונה הפיזית/הכימית שהחברה רוצה לנטר. שני סוגים:
• כמותי (Quantitative)
• איכותי (Qualitative)
כמותי מגדיר ערך מספרי (2.3 ק"ג, 11 רגל). איכותי — תכונה לא-מספרית (חלק/מחורר/חלוד למשטח; אדום/חום לצבע).
משתמשים ב-MICs ביצירת task lists כתבניות, או מפנים אליהם ב-inspection plan. האובייקטים ופונקציות הבקרה זהים למאפיין ב-plan. ארגונית, ‏MICs (כמו plans) מוקצים למפעל.

sections.title: Create Inspection Characteristics
sections.en: 2.9.1 Create Inspection Characteristics To create a master inspection characteristic, use Transaction QS21 or follow menu path SAP  Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Char- acteristic  Create. On the initial screen that appears to create the characteristics, enter plant “1710” and master inspection characteristic “QMHT10”. You don’t have to enter the Valid From date because the system automatically assigns the current date as the creation date. Press (Enter) so that the screen in Figure 2.11 appears. Figure 2.11 Master Inspection Characteristic 2 Quality Planning 82 Select the Quantitative Charc checkbox to set the master inspection characteristic as a quantitative characteristic. Set the Status of the characteristic as 2 Released, which makes it available during sub- sequent QM activities in which you use this master inspection characteristic. If the sta- tus of the master inspection characteristic is set to 1 Being Created, it won’t be available, for example, when you create an inspection plan. If the characteristic is used for quantitative inspections, it also makes sense to use the Incomplete Copy Model option. This means that you don’t have to set the nominal value, tolerance settings, and so on when maintaining the characteristic. Complete set- tings have to be made only after the master inspection characteristic is used in an inspection plan. A fixed reference can’t be made to an incomplete characteristic. Incomplete characteristics are suitable only as copy templates.
sections.he:
ליצירת MIC: Transaction QS21 או SAP • Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Basic Data • Inspection Characteristic • Create. הזינו plant "1710", ‏MIC "QMHT10" (אין צורך ב-Valid From — תאריך נוכחי). ‏Enter (Figure 2.11).
סמנו Quantitative Charc למאפיין כמותי. קבעו Status ל-2 Released (זמין; אם 1 Being Created — אינו זמין ביצירת plan).
למאפיין כמותי, הגיוני Incomplete Copy Model — אין צורך ב-nominal value/tolerance בתחזוקה; ההגדרות המלאות רק לאחר שימוש ב-plan. אי אפשר reference קבוע למאפיין לא-שלם — מתאים רק כתבנית.

sections.title: Edit Control Indicators
sections.en: 2.9.2 Edit Control Indicators Our next step is to choose Control Indicators (in the top menu of Figure 2.11), which brings up the screen in Figure 2.12. Figure 2.12 Master Inspection Characteristic: General Data © 83 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics Tips and Tricks You can incorporate the inspection method we covered in Section 2.6. You can also maintain the Sample-Drawing Text, which is then available during the actual testing of this characteristic. Table 2.4 covers the details of the various checkboxes and radio buttons that you see in Figure 2.12. Some rows in the Effects column are intentionally left blank, especially when the details in the Meaning column sufficiently explain the concepts. Note Although we’ve taken a “longer” path to help you understand how selecting or dese- lecting various options in the master inspection characteristic eventually impacts qual- ity inspection, you can also enter a preconfigured value in the Preset Indicators field shown earlier in Figure 2.12, and the system will automatically trigger the necessary selection options of the master inspection characteristic. We’ll cover the configuration details of preset indicators in Chapter 3. Control Indicator Meaning Effects Lower Specif. Limit A lower specification limit of the master inspection characteristic. – Check Target Value You have to enter a target value for this characteristic. If you set this indicator along with one or both tolerance indicator(s), the system checks whether the target value is within the tolerance range. Upper Specif. Limit An upper specification limit of the master inspection characteristic. – Characteristic Attribute The characteristic is attributive in character and references a selected set of catalog type 1. It’s only applicable for qualitative master inspection characteristic. This control is available for quali- tative master inspection charac- teristics only. Sampling Proce- dure You need to assign a sampling pro- cedure to this master inspection characteristic in the task list. A procedure to determine the size of the sample in an inspection. The sampling procedure also defines the valuation type that the system uses for results recording (attribu- tive, variable, manual, etc.). Table 2.4 Characteristic Control Indicators 2 Quality Planning 84 SPC Characteris- tic If you set this indicator, the system assigns a quality control chart to this characteristic. If you set this indicator, you also have to set the indicator for the sampling procedure. You then also have to enter a statistical process control criteria and a sampling procedure with a control chart type in the task list for the statisti- cal process control characteristic. Confirmation No. of Defects You can confirm the number of defects in the results recording. If you set this indicator, you can confirm the number of defective units in the results recording. This is only available for qualitative master inspection characteristics. Additive Sample The system increases the sample size by the quantity required for this master inspection characteris- tic. If the system uses a sample for multiple characteristics, the sam- ple-drawing instruction contains only the total sample quantity to be drawn. This indicator can be set if the inspection for this character- istic destroys the samples. In this case, the indicator has the effect that the sample size is increased by the quantity that is required for the inspection of this characteris- tic. Destructive Insp. Flags characteristics whose sam- ples are destroyed in the sampling process. In the usage decision, the system calculates the destroyed quantity and a proposed inventory posting of the sample. The calcula- tion includes all characteristics that are flagged as destructive and for which inspections have been carried out up to the time of calcu- lation, in accordance with the actual sample size. These can also be optional charac- teristics (skip), long-term charac- teristics, and unplanned characteristics. The sample calcu- lation includes physical samples, alternative sample units of mea- sure, partial samples, and the addi- tive sample indicator. For the inventory posting, the system pro- poses only the part of the destroyed quantity that is over and above the quantity posted for the sample. Control Indicator Meaning Effects Table 2.4 Characteristic Control Indicators (Cont.) © 85 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics Summ. Recording You can only record or report sum- marized values for the inspection results of a master inspection characteristic after the inspection. – Single Result You can record individual values (measured values, codes, etc.) for the inspection results of a master inspection characteristic after the inspection. – No Charc Record- ing No provision to record results for a master inspection characteristic after the inspection. – Classed Record- ing You can record the inspection results of a master inspection characteristic as classed values. – Defects Record- ing If this indicator is set, and if the master inspection characteristic has a rejected valuation, the sys- tem automatically calls upon defects recording for the master inspection characteristic. A prerequisite for background defect generation is that you define the defect codes in the task- list characteristic or in the master inspection characteristic. There are three defect codes for a quantita- tive characteristic:  Defect code for general rejec- tion  Defect code for rejection at the upper tolerance limit  Defect code for rejection at the lower tolerance limit For a qualitative characteristic, define the defect code for general rejection. Required Charc The inspection of a characteristic is closed by means of a confirmation. You need to confirm the inspection results for the master inspection characteristic before you can make the usage decision. If you want dynamic modification to be characteristic based, you have to flag all the characteristics that are intended for dynamic modification as mandatory char- acteristics. Control Indicator Meaning Effects Table 2.4 Characteristic Control Indicators (Cont.) 2 Quality Planning 86 Choose Continue, which brings up the screen shown in Figure 2.13. Figure 2.13 Characteristic Control Indicators Optional Charc You can close the inspection of an optional characteristic without the need for confirmation. There’s also no need to confirm inspection results for the master inspection characteristic before making a usage decision. – After Acceptance You can inspect this conditional master inspection characteristic only after the preceding manda- tory master inspection characteris- tic in the same operation has been valuated as “A” (accepted). – After Rejection You can inspect this conditional master inspection characteristic only after the preceding manda- tory master inspection characteris- tic in the same operation has been valuated as “R” (rejected). – Control Indicator Meaning Effects Table 2.4 Characteristic Control Indicators (Cont.) © 87 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics Table 2.5 covers the details of the various checkboxes and radio buttons that you see in Figure 2.13. Some rows in the Effects column are intentionally left blank, especially when the details in the Meaning column sufficiently explain the concepts. Control Indicator Meaning Effects Scope Not Fixed The system doesn’t check the inspection scope to make sure that it complies with the precalculated inspection scope in the results recording. – Fixed Scope The system does check the inspec- tion scope to make sure that it complies with the precalculated inspection scope in the results recording and doesn’t allow devia- tions. – Smaller Scope The inspection scope can be smaller than the precalculated inspection scope in the results recording. – Larger Scope The inspection scope can be larger than the precalculated inspection scope in the results recording. – No Documenta- tion There’s no need to create addi- tional documentation for this master inspection characteristic in the results recording. – Docu. If Rejected There is need to create additional documentation for this master inspection characteristic in the results recording only if the master inspection characteristic is rejected. – Docu. Required You need to maintain additional text, in the form of documentation of the inspection result, for the master inspection characteristic in results recording. – Table 2.5 Characteristic Control Indicators 2 Quality Planning 88 Long-Term Inspection The inspection for this master inspection characteristic can run for a long period. If you set this indicator for a mas- ter inspection characteristic, you can make a usage decision for the master inspection characteristic or set the status Short-Term Inspec- tion Completion. During the long- term inspection, you can use material that has been inspected and thus reduce the stock of the inspection lot. This means that you can also retroactively record results for the long-term inspec- tion. Scrap Share/Q- Score The system takes the share of defective units for this master inspection characteristic into account in the calculation of the scrap share in the inspection lot. If the usage decision uses a quality score procedure that refers to the share of scrap in the inspection lot or the master inspection charac- teristic, the system uses this mas- ter inspection characteristic to calculate the quality score only if this indicator is set. RR Change Docs If you set this indicator, change documents are written for this master inspection characteristic in the characteristics-based results recording. The change documents are written only when master inspection char- acteristics have been fully pro- cessed (status 5) and the data is already in the database. Test Equip. Assignmt If this indicator is set, you can assign an item of test equipment to the characteristic in the task list. If you don’t assign anything, the system alerts you to this fact by means of a warning message. – Record Mea- sured Vals Measured values for this quantita- tive master inspection characteris- tic are inspected and confirmed. – Print If you set this indicator, the system prints the master inspection char- acteristic on the inspection instruction. – Control Indicator Meaning Effects Table 2.5 Characteristic Control Indicators (Cont.) © 89 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics

sections.title: Assign Inspection Catalog
sections.en: 2.9.3 Assign Inspection Catalog Figure 2.14 shows the inspection catalog that you can assign to the master inspection characteristic. Here, you can assign the catalog type, such as 9 (Defect Type), as well as the code group and selected set (CGr/SSet). You can also assign default defect codes for rejection when the characteristic’s upper or lower tolerance specification limit is exceeded. Do Not Print If you set this indicator, the system doesn’t print the master inspec- tion characteristic on the inspec- tion instruction. – Do Not Print at Skip If you set this indicator, the system prints the master inspection char- acteristic on the inspection instruction only if there is no skip for the master inspection charac- teristic. – No Formula The inspection characteristic is not characterized as either a calcu- lated characteristic or a character- istic for input processing. – Calculated Charc. The characteristic is a calculated characteristic. The results for a calculated charac- teristic aren’t calculated by means of the master inspection charac- teristic. Instead, they’re calculated on the basis of the results of other characteristics within the same operation. Input Processing Setting this indicator ensures that entries for an inspection charac- teristic are processed using the predefined rules for input process- ing. – Control Indicator Meaning Effects Table 2.5 Characteristic Control Indicators (Cont.) 2 Quality Planning 90 Figure 2.14 Inspection Catalog You can assign defect codes to the characteristics. In many cases, performing valuation of a qualitative characteristic with OK/NOK or a quantitative characteristic with a mea- surement value is too general. For a more precise defect description in the case of a rejection, you can make a special catalog with catalog type 9, Defect Types, available to the characteristic. This catalog is then automatically highlighted with a Rejected valua- tion in the results recording, and the system prompts you to enter a defect code. Another important characteristic of this function is the automatic generation—during the results recording—of a defect record in the form of a quality notification. To acti- vate this functionality, select the Results Recording checkbox in the control indicators of the characteristic. You can then continue to fully edit the messages with the message type Q2, Internal Quality Notifications.

sections.title: Sampling Procedure
sections.en: 2.10 Sampling Procedure A sampling procedure enables the system to calculate the sample size of the inspection lot for quality inspection and then inspect and record its results. In a sampling proce- dure, you determine the sample size and the valuation rules for the inspection charac- teristics. © 91 2.10 Sampling Procedure Example A supplier delivers 100 kg of PET chips (a raw material used in making plastic bottles) against a purchase order. The system should be able to calculate a sample size of 5 kg because the sampling procedure stipulates inspecting 5% of the delivered goods as the sample size for inspection. To create a sampling procedure, use Transaction QDV1 or follow menu path SAP  Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sampling Procedure  Create. On the initial screen that appears, enter sampling proce- dure “FIX10” to denote the relevancy and the settings made. Press (Enter), and the screen shown in Figure 2.15 appears. From the Sampling Type dropdown, you can choose one of the four available sampling types:  100 Fixed sample Regardless of the quantity delivered by the supplier or produced in house, the sys- tem always calculates a fixed sample quantity for inspection. For example, for a pro- duced/procured quantity of either 100 kg or 1,000 kg, the system calculates the fixed sample size of 3, if the sample size is 3.  200 100% Inspection Regardless of the quantity delivered by the supplier or produced in house, the com- plete quantity is available for inspection.  300 Using sampling scheme A sampling scheme uses an incremental method of calculating sample size. The big- ger the produced/procured material is, the smaller the overall sample size available for inspection can be. For example, for a procured quantity of up to 100 kg, the sam- ple size is 5 kg, whereas for a procured quantity between 101 kg and 1,000 kg, the sample size is 8 kg. It’s impractical to inspect a large sample quantity if the overall delivered quantity is too big.  400 Sample percentage A percentage of the total produced/procured quantity is available as a sample size for quality inspection. For example, for a procured or produced quantity of 200 kg of material, the sample size is 4 kg because the sample percentage is defined as 2%. Whenever the system creates an inspection lot for produced or procured material, it automatically and immediately calculates the sample size. The purpose of a sampling procedure is to be able to calculate the sample size for quality inspection from the total inspection lot quantity. 2 Quality Planning 92 Figure 2.15 Sampling Procedure Next, choose Valuation Mode: Attributive inspection nonconf. units. The valuation mode defines how the system decides to accept or reject an inspection characteristic (valuation mode). Some of the manual or automatic decision options available are as follows:  A manual decision is required for attributive characteristics (i.e., characteristics for which no values are recorded). These are characteristics you simply accept or reject. This type of decision is also used in all other cases in which an automatic valuation isn’t possible or allowed.  Code valuation forms the basis of qualitative attributes. The decisions are stored in the catalog for characteristic attributes.  A decision can be based on a sampling plan for attributive inspection with the options of considering the number of defects, number of nonconforming units, or deviation from tolerance limits for quantitative characteristics.  A decision can be based on a sampling plan for quantitative characteristics (variable inspection) with the options to comply with the distribution limits of the character- istic values (s-method) or the mean value limits of characteristic values (checking the tolerance specifications). This is a special application of s-method, where k = 0.  A decision can be based on a control chart. © 93

sections.title: Inspection Plan
sections.en: 2.11 Inspection Plan Because you’re not going to use this sampling procedure for statistical process control, you don’t have to choose or enter anything in Control Chart Type. The Independent Multiple Samples option should be used only if you want to record multiple results for a characteristic of a part or results from multiple samples for a char- acteristic. An example of an independent multiple sample is the repeated measuring of the diameter at different points of a wave. Note that the inspection results should be attributed to only one unit of inspection in this case. The system can then calculate an arithmetical mean value of the measurements in a subsequent calculated characteristic. Choose Sample in the menu bar of Figure 2.15 to define the percentage of the sample for calculation. Enter a Sample Size of “10” in the popup. You can enter up to three decimal places to define the sample size as a percentage. Enter an Acceptance Number of “2” to denote that that the system still valuates the characteristic as acceptable if up to 2 out of 10 units are rejected. Note When you’re incorporating sampling procedures in the inspection plan, the system dis- plays only the allowed sampling procedure selection screen for the characteristic. In the worst case, no selection options are available. The rules that you previously created for the sampling procedure then need to be rechecked. It can happen, for example, that you’ve selected Scope Not Fixed in the control indicators and are trying to assign a sampling procedure for a control chart. In this case, the sampling procedure doesn’t appear in the selection because the sample size for a control chart has to be fixed. Therefore, you should set a fixed scope in the master inspection characteristic before assigning it to the inspection plan. 2.11 Inspection Plan You use the inspection plan’s task list type in QM to process procurement-, production-, or sales-related quality inspections. Its typical application areas are model inspections, goods receipt inspections, goods issue inspections, and goods receipts from produc- tion. Its main functions are the same as those of the routing. Besides assigning to the material, you can also assign the following to the inspection plan:  Material and business partner (supplier)  Material and business partner (customer) The inspection plan can include the reference operation set in their operations and thus use a modular system of operations and inspection characteristics. In the SAP S/4HANA system, the inspection plan is the production-based task list type that’s available in PP and PP-PI. From a QM perspective, this has the advantage that the inspection plan is structured in exactly the same way as the routing and thus already 2 Quality Planning 94 has useful and tried-and-tested planning instruments at its disposal. The basic structure consists of operations (work operations, inspection operations) and is the same in all task list types, including the inspection plan. In addition, every task-list type also has its own features that reflect its specific usage. The inspection plan is completely integrated into the supply chain of the SAP S/4HANA system and provides extended functions for task planning that cover capacity and costs. Therefore, having a good understanding of this topic is a prerequisite for ensuring that you effectively manage this important QM master data. To gain a better understanding of inspection plan management, let’s now look at the structure of the inspection plan and its individual components:  Task list header  Material assignment  Test equipment (PRT assignment)  Operations  Inspection characteristics  Dependent characteristics Figure 2.16 shows how various QM master data fits into an inspection plan. Figure 2.16 Inspection Plan In the following sections, we’ll explain the entire structure of the inspection plan you just saw in Figure 2.16 and how various QM master data elements connect with each other in an inspection plan. Material Task list header Operation 10 Inspection characteristic 10 Inspection characteristic 20 Test equipment 10 Operation 20 Inspection characteristic 10 Test equipment 10 © 95 2.11 Inspection Plan Tips and Tricks As part of your inspection planning, set up integration meetings with the procurement, production planning, and sales project groups early in the planning phase. In these meetings, introduce the participants to the whole area of inspection planning, and explain how it’s integrated with the various other technical departments. You should also use this opportunity to explain the organizational aspects and areas of responsi- bility that will be important when the team is working together on the inspection plan and routing.
