sections.title: First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process
sections.en: 4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process The remaining QM business processes for source inspection are the same:  Record results for source inspection (Transaction QE01)  Usage decision (Transaction QA11) Invoice Receipt The business process of the invoice receipt is the same as we previously covered in Sec- tion 4.2.1. 4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process SAP has introduced first article inspection for the production part approval process to cater to the quality control and quality assurance needs of industries, such as automo- tive, aerospace, and so on to ensure comprehensive pre-inspection of underproduction products by a company. It’s an alternate to pilot run inspection, which we’ll discuss in Section 4.4. A model inspection is used to identify and rectify quality issues beforehand prior to the production of remaining products. The first article inspection for the pro- duction part approval process is a new feature in SAP S/4HANA and can be easily set up as long as the necessary configuration, master data, and business processes are put in place that enable effectively reporting for timely and informed business decisions. Once the supplier has passed the quality process of first article inspection for the production part approval process for the material to be supplied to the company, then the regular quality inspection can take place. As needed, first article inspection for the production part approval process can also be reinitiated to begin the reevaluation of a supplier. Figure 4.18 shows the end-to-end business processes for first article inspection for pro- duction part approval. In the business process, the first step is to make the relevant set- ting in the quality info record, which is relevant for first article approval for production part approval. This is then followed by the regular procure-to-pay process (purchase to goods receipt), and the goods receipt will generate an inspection lot of type 01 (goods receipt inspection for purchase order) associated to standard inspection plan usage 51 (goods receipt model inspection). Figure 4.18 Business Process of First Article Inspection for the Production Part Approval Process Let’s discuss the configuration settings followed by the business process of first article inspection for the production part approval process: Update Quality Info Record Purchase Order Goods Receipt Quality Insp. Lot Insp. Plan Usage 51 Results Recording Usage Decision 4 Integrating with Materials Management 254 1. The first prerequisite is to define a specific inspection plan usage (first article inspec- tion usage) for first article inspection in the control key for QM in procurement. To perform the necessary configuration, follow the menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Control Keys for QM in Procurement. Define the FAI plan usage 51 (goods receipt model). We suggest that you quickly refer to control key settings we made in Section 4.1.2 and how control key 0007 was then assigned to the material master. 2. Maintain a quality info record (Transaction QI01) for the material (QM004) and sup- plier (EWM17-SU01) combination. In the Inspection Control tab of the quality info record, choose the PPAP Required checkbox followed by choosing New from the PPAP Status dropdown in Figure 4.19. Save your settings. Figure 4.19 PPA in Quality Info Record 3. Maintain two inspection plans (usage 51 and usage 5) for the material using Transac- tion QP01. 4. The quality planning of first article inspections for purchase orders can only be undertaken using the Manage Quality Info Records app (see Figure 4.20), as the clas- sical SAP GUI Transactions QI01 and QI02 don’t completely support this feature. 5. As we’ve just created the quality info record of the material-supplier-plant combina- tion using Transaction QI01, it’s now available in Figure 4.20. 6. Use the forward arrow located on the far-right side of the screen, so that Figure 4.21 appears. © 255 4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process Figure 4.20 Manage Quality Info Records App 7. The Inspection Control tab shown in Figure 4.21 will enable you to maintain the rele- vant production part approval process details, including production part approval process level and production part approval process status. 8. Choose the PPAP Level, for example, Warrant Only, followed by setting the PPAP sta- tus as In Process to initiate the first article inspection for the production part approval process. Figure 4.21 Quality Info Record: Detailed Screen 4 Integrating with Materials Management 256 9. Choose Add in Figure 4.22 to assign the purchase order line items that are relevant for first article inspection. This purchase order of material-supplier-plant combina- tion should already be created in the system, so this assignment is made possible here. For this example, Purchasing Document “4500001843” and its line Item “10” is assigned. The valuation code shown as Not valuated is due to the fact that the usage decision isn’t yet taken because an inspection lot will only be created when posting the goods receipt takes place for the corresponding purchase order line item. Figure 4.22 Purchase Orders Relevant for First Article Inspection for the PPA Process 10. Post goods receipt for this purchase order using Transaction MIGO, and as shown in Figure 4.23, the system creates an inspection lot for goods receipt (Inspection Type 01) and assigns this inspection lot the Usage 51. 11. After results recordings and setting the usage decision, the status of the inspection lot will be displayed in the quality info record, so the quality inspector can com- plete the production part approval process by changing the PPAP Status field to Completed (see Figure 4.24). Note The system gives a warning at the time of usage decision for the inspection lot to inform the quality inspector that the first article inspection isn’t yet valuated and therefore will eventually impact the supplier qualification to regularly supply the material. © 257 4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process Figure 4.23 Inspection Lot for Goods Receipt with Inspection Usage Assigned as 51 Figure 4.24 Production Part Approval Process Status Marked as Completed 4 Integrating with Materials Management 258 Now that we’ve discussed the new feature, first article inspection for the production part approval process, let’s discuss a similar (and overlapping) feature of run pilot inspection in the next section. It’s important to note here that a company can only use one at a time: either first article inspection for the production part approval process or run pilot inspection business process (and not both).

sections.title: Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102
sections.en: 4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102 Before “upgrading” the status of a first-time or new supplier to that of a regular sup- plier, a company often has stringent and comprehensive procedures and processes in place to ensure that a new supplier is able to provide material of sufficient quality. To achieve this objective, the company makes the supplier go through a series of trial runs or pilot runs of materials until the supplier is able to fulfill the quality requirements. Here, the SAP system can help by enabling the procurement and quality planners to put a series of checks and controls in place via status management. With each mate- rial’s delivery from the supplier, its corresponding inspection lot creation, results recording, and usage decision update the status (and controls) for the supplier. The following sections begin with discussing the necessary configuration settings that need to be in place for pilot run inspection so the same can then be assigned in the mas- ter data. The master data is then used to discuss the business processes of pilot run inspection.
sections.he: לפני "שדרוג" ספק חדש לקבוע, החברה מעבירה אותו סדרת trial/pilot runs עד שהוא עומד בדרישות. ה-SAP מסייע ב-status management — כל אספקה, ‏lot, רישום, ו-usage decision מעדכנים את הסטטוס (והבקרות). להלן תצורה, נתוני אב, ותהליכים.

sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.en: 4.4.1 Configuration Basics Before we cover the configuration basics of the pilot run, see Figure 4.25, which shows the Status tab of the quality info record (Transaction QI01), in which we assigned Status Profile QM_P_001. A status profile controls various business functions and whether they are allowed. A status profile is a cross-application component, so you can use it to control business functions not just in the QM area but also in other logistics and supply chain management areas. Figure 4.25 Status Profile in the Quality Info Record © 259 4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102 In this example of a pilot run inspection, use status profile QM_P_001, which SAP delivers. Alternatively, you can amend an existing status profile or create a new one with menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality in Logistics  QM in Procure- ment  Define Status of Supply Relationships. Figure 4.26 shows the standard supplier relationship status profile QM_P_001 available in the system. Here, there are multiple statuses, and the initial status is 0001 (Supply Relationship Initiated). The initial status is denoted by the checkbox selected in the Init. status column. The low and high numbers of the status control how the system changes from one status to another. Figure 4.26 Status Profile Figure 4.27 shows the assignment of different statuses of status profile QM_P_001 to inspection lots. To assign statuses to inspection types so that the system is able to fol- low the sequence in creating various inspection types, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Maintain Inspection Lot Origins & Assign Inspection Types. For this example, choose three different statuses of status profile QM_P_001, and cor- respondingly assign three different inspection types: 0101, 0102, and 01. When the sys- tem receives the material from the supplier and against the purchase order, it creates an inspection lot of inspection type 0101. This is because you assigned status 0002 to inspection type 0101, and this is the first status among the three statuses. On accepted usage decision for this inspection lot (and of inspection type 0101), the system auto- matically switches to the next status, which is 0003 (and correspondingly having inspection type 0102; look for the Next status column in Figure 4.27 to see how status change works). 4 Integrating with Materials Management 260 Figure 4.27 Status Profile and Assignment to Inspection Types In Section 4.4.3, we’ll cover end-to-end business processes of all three inspection types and their statuses. Tips and Tricks If you’ve configured other specific inspection types to attend to the pilot run inspec- tion’s business scenario, you can assign these configured inspection types at this stage (Figure 4.27).

sections.title: Business Processes of Pilot Run Inspection
sections.en: 4.4.3 Business Processes of Pilot Run Inspection In this business process, the first step is to create a purchase order for new a supplier and partially or completely receive goods. The system creates an inspection lot of inspection type 0101. Perform results recording, followed by making a usage decision and stock posting. The system considers the usage decision at this stage to decide whether it should move to the next status or remain the same. An accepted usage decision for inspection type 0101 triggers the system to create the inspection lot of inspection type 0102, and on the next goods receipt against the same purchase order or even a different purchase order. Again, the system considers results recorded and usage decision taken for the inspection lot of inspection type 0102 to see if it should switch the status to inspection type 01 or not. Finally, the accepted usage decision of inspection type 0102 © 261 4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102 leads to the system updating to inspection type 01. You then pay the supplier for goods delivered. The business process of the pilot run inspection is shown in Figure 4.28. Figure 4.28 Business Processes in Model Inspection Create a purchase order using Transaction ME21N; in this example, the system creates purchase order number 4500001848. On goods receipt against the purchase order (using Transaction MIGO), the system creates inspection lot 10000000661, as shown in Figure 4.29. Figure 4.29 Prototype Release: Inspection Type 0101 This inspection lot is of inspection type 0101. Notice that the system denotes the description of the inspection type as a qualification model and is the same as shown Purchase order Goods receipt QM inspection lot (Insp. type 0101) QM inspection lot (Insp. type 0102) QM inspection lot (Insp. type 01) Goods receipt Goods receipt Invoice receipt 4 Integrating with Materials Management 262 earlier in Figure 4.27. Record the results of this inspection lot, take its accepted usage decision, and perform a stock posting to unrestricted-use stock. Perform another goods receipt for the same or different purchase order, and this time, the system creates an inspection lot of inspection type 0102, thereby adhering to the sequence that we configured in Figure 4.27. This is shown in Figure 4.30 where the sys- tem creates an inspection lot 10000000678. Record the results of this inspection lot, take its accepted usage decision, and perform a stock posting to unrestricted-use stock. Correspondingly, the system updates the status of the inspection lot. Figure 4.30 Preliminary and Production Release: Inspection Type 0102 On the next goods receipt against the same or a different purchase order, this time, the system creates inspection lot 10000000685 of inspection type 01 (see Figure 4.31). Figure 4.32 shows the Status tab of the quality information record, in which the details of the inspection lot shown in Figure 4.31 are accordingly updated. © 263 4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102 Figure 4.31 Goods Receipt Inspection Figure 4.32 Status Management To summarize, let’s look at how the system updates the quality information record of the material QM003 and supplier EWM17-SU01 combination during the entire busi- ness process of the pilot run. The Status tab of the display quality information record (Transaction QI03) updates the statuses per the actions performed and incorporates the relevant inspection lot numbers. These inspection lots, 10000000681 and 10000000678, are the same as shown previously. It’s important to note that in Figure 4.32, the status is from before we recorded results and made a usage decision and stock posting. Once we do this, the system updates the status of inspection lot 10000000685 as shown in Figure 4.32. It updates this status after you undertake the usage decision for 4 Integrating with Materials Management 264 the inspection lot as 10000000685. Had it been a rejected inspection lot, the system would have maintained the previous status until acceptable results (and a usage deci- sion) were in place.

sections.title: Subcontracting: Inspection Type 0130
sections.en: 4.5 Subcontracting: Inspection Type 0130 The subcontracting process begins when the company hands over (issues) the compo- nents to a subcontractor, who is usually a supplier, against the subcontracting pur- chase order, to either assemble or add value to the product. The company takes the components’ inventory out of its books, and the same is reflected in the supplier’s inventory. When the supplier has done what it’s contracted to do, the company receives the goods against the same subcontracting purchase order from the supplier. On goods receipt from external processing (subcontracting), the system creates an inspection lot of inspection type 0130. Figure 4.33 shows the end-to-end subcontract- ing business process. The supplier invoices the company for the services rendered and receives payment. Figure 4.33 Subcontracting Business Process The following sections discuss the QM master data checklist to ensure that relevant QM master data is already created, as well as the end-to-end subcontracting process, which also involves quality inspection of externally processed material (subcon- tracted material).

sections.title: Stock Transfer Inspection: Inspection Type 08
sections.en: 4.6.1 Stock Transfer Inspection: Inspection Type 08 Components procured or produced in one plant may be required for assembly or con- sumption in another plant, which requires a stock transfer. In the quality inspection business process of stock transfers, it’s possible to conduct a quality inspection process not just for interplant or plant-to-plant stock transfer but also for other inventory man- agement functions, such as for store-to-store stock transfer within the same plant and material-to-material stock transfer. In this example, we’ll cover interplant transfer posting—that is, plant-to-plant stock transfer using a stock transport order. For a stock transport order for interplant transfer, the following sequence of steps is involved: 1 Create a stock transport order that consists of supplying plant and receiving plant details, along with other materials and quantities. 2 Goods are issued from the supplying plant with reference to the stock transport order. These goods are shown as stock in transit. 3 Goods are received at the receiving plant with reference to the same stock transport order. 4 Upon goods receipt at the receiving plant, the system creates an inspection lot for interplant stock transfer. Figure 4.39 shows the end-to-end business process of a stock transport order and for stock transfer between two plants. Figure 4.39 Business Process in Stock Transport Order Let’s now cover the QM master data requirements that you need to ensure to attend to this business process. QM Master Data Checklist The following is the QM master data checklist:  Inspection type 08 active in the QM view of the material master of the receiving plant  Inspection plan usage 5 and status 4 (for released) Stock transport order Goods issue from supplying plant Goods receipt at receiving plant QM inspection lot at receiving plant 4 Integrating with Materials Management 270 Stock Transport Order Access Transaction ME21N (see Figure 4.40) for the initial screen for the stock transport order. Select UB Stock Transp. Order from the dropdown list on the top-left side of the screen. Assign the supplying plant as 1720 (Plant 2 US), and then enter the item category as “U” (in column I), the Material as “QM003”, the Quantity as “100” PC, and the receiv- ing plant (Plant) as “1710” (Plant 1 US). Save the stock transport order, and in this exam- ple, the system creates a stock transport order number 4500001851. The next step is to issue the material from the supplying plant with reference to the same stock transport order number. Figure 4.40 Stock Transport Order Goods Issue (Transfer Posting) for Stock Transport Order Access the screen in Figure 4.41 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Issue and then Purchase Order from the dropdown lists at the top. Then, enter the purchase order (stock transport order) number “4500001851” in the blank field. The movement type for goods issue against a stock transport order is 351 and is shown on the top-right cor- ner of the screen. Save the entries, and the stock now appears in transit. © 271 4.6 Inventory Management Processes Tips and Tricks Although it isn’t shown in this example, you can also activate goods issue inspection for a stock transport order to meet any specific business needs. To do so, maintain the following QM master data:  Inspection type 02 active in the QM view of the material master of the goods issue or supplying plant  Inspection plan usage 6 and status 4 (for released) Refer to Chapter 6 for information on using inspection type 02. Figure 4.41 Goods Issue against a Stock Transport Order Stock in Transit Transaction MB5T takes you to the screen shown in Figure 4.42 after you’ve entered the initial parameters, such as supplying plant, issuing plant, and so on. The stock remains in transit until the receiving plant receives goods against the same stock transport order. Tips and Tricks You can also use Transaction MB5TD to view stock in transit on the key date, and even for intercompany or cross-company stock that is in transit. 4 Integrating with Materials Management 272 Figure 4.42 Stock in Transit Goods Receipt for Stock Transport Order Access the screen in Figure 4.43 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Receipt and then Purchase Order from the dropdown lists at the top. Then, enter the purchase order (stock transport order) number “4500001851” in the blank field. The movement type for goods receipt against a stock transport order is 101 and is shown at the top-right cor- ner of the screen. Save your entries. Figure 4.43 Goods Receipt for Stock Transport Order © 273 4.6 Inventory Management Processes Inspection Lot for Stock Transport Order Figure 4.44 show the inspection lot (Transaction QA03) that the system creates on goods receipt for stock transport order. The inspection type is 08 and consists of all the relevant details, such as stock transport order number 4500001851. Figure 4.44 Inspection Lot of Inspection Type 08
sections.he:
רכיבים מ-מפעל אחד עשויים להידרש באחר — stock transfer. ניתן בדיקה ל-מפעל-למפעל, מחסן-למחסן באותו מפעל, וחומר-לחומר. כאן — מפעל-למפעל עם stock transport order:
1. יצירת stock transport order (מפעל מספק ומקבל, חומרים, כמויות).
2. הנפקה מהמספק (stock in transit).
3. קבלה במקבל מול אותו STO.
4. בקבלה, המערכת יוצרת lot ל-interplant stock transfer (Figure 4.39).

sections.title: Other Goods Receipt: Inspection Type 05
sections.en: 4.6.2 Other Goods Receipt: Inspection Type 05 Although it may not happen all that frequently, companies also face or have business needs for which it’s imperative to quickly procure, receive, and make available goods for further consumption. This may be the case when, due to the urgency of a material requirement, a procurement person places and receives a material without going through the standard procurement process. On goods receipt without reference to a purchase order, the system still asks for supplier details to book its payment liability and be able to pay for the procured goods. For such business processes, SAP S/4HANA offers a standard inspection type to ensure that material received without reference to a purchase order still gets inspected. 4 Integrating with Materials Management 274 The following sections discuss the QM master data checklist to ensure the same is cre- ated and available in the system before proceeding further with discussion of the busi- ness process of goods receipt without a purchase order, which triggers the quality inspection process. QM Master Data Checklist The following is the QM master data checklist that you need to ensure:  Inspection type 05 active in the QM view of the material master  Inspection plan usage 5 and status 4 (for released) Goods Receipt without Purchase Order Access the screen in Figure 4.45 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Receipt and then Other from the dropdown lists at the top. The movement type for goods receipt without referring to a purchase order is 501 as shown on the far-right side of the screen. You need to enter the material code, its quantity, plant, storage location, and the sup- plier who delivered the material. If it’s a batch-managed material, then the system will create a batch number. Save your entries. Figure 4.45 shows the material document cre- ated as the result of goods receipt without reference to a purchase order. Figure 4.45 Other Goods Receipt Figure 4.46 shows the inspection lot (Transaction QA03) that the system creates on goods receipt and without referring to any purchase order. The inspection type is 05 and consists of all the relevant details that the system created in the previous step. It also consists of the material document details of goods receipt. © 275

• inspection plan usage 5, ‏status 4.

Figure 4.46 (Transaction QA03) — ה-lot מ-GR ללא הזמנה. type 05, כולל פרטי מסמך החומר.

sections.title: Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection Type 0800
sections.en: 4.7 Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection Type 0800 Figure 4.46 Inspection Lot of Inspection Type 05 4.7 Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection Type 0800 You can integrate QM even after implementation of SAP’s core business processes such as in areas of MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, production planning (PP), finance, and con- trolling. Until then, the only limited option available to restrict a material’s free-to-use stock (aka unrestricted stock) is to transfer or receive the stock as quality inspection stock. On quality clearance (out of SAP) from the quality department, the user performs the transfer posting of quality inspection stock to unrestricted-use stock by using Transaction MIGO and movement type 321. When the company implements QM and integrates it in logistics areas, the system requires that all stock placed in quality inspection within MM and not QM undergoes quality inspection again. This activity prevents inconsistencies between the stocks placed in quality inspection within MM and the stock that requires handling in QM. To attend to this scenario of ensuring stock consistency upon integrating QM with logis- tics, SAP S/4HANA offers standard inspection type 0800. 4 Integrating with Materials Management 276 However, to use inspection type 0800, you need to ensure that a single configuration setting is in place and then run its business process. Let’s first cover the configuration settings that you need to activate to use inspection type 0800.

ניתן לשלב QM גם לאחר יישום הליבה (MM, ‏Sales, ‏PP, ‏Finance, ‏CO). עד אז, האפשרות היחידה להגביל מלאי חופשי — קבלתו/העברתו כ-quality inspection stock. באישור (מחוץ ל-SAP), המשתמש מבצע transfer posting ל-unrestricted ב-Transaction MIGO, ‏movement type 321.
ביישום QM, המערכת דורשת שכל מלאי ב-quality inspection ב-MM (לא QM) ייבדק שוב — למניעת אי-עקביות. לכך, ה-SAP מציע inspection type 0800 (דורש הגדרה אחת).

sections.title: Configuration Settings
sections.en: 4.7.1 Configuration Settings At the plant level, you need to assign inspection type 0800 to each of the plants in which you plan to integrate QM. For this example, use plant 1710, and assign inspection type 0800. To perform the necessary configuration setting, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level. Choose Plant 1710, and enter “0800” in the InspTypeforInspStock field in the Insp. lot creation tab. Save your settings.

sections.en: 4.7.3 Inspection Lot on QM Activation To ensure QM activation for the stock that is already in quality inspection, use Transac- tion QA08, or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Information System  Inspection Setup. For this example, enter Plant “1710” and Material “2232”, make the settings shown in Figure 4.48 in the Activate Inspection Type tab, and then choose Execute (not shown). The screen in Figure 4.49 appears, which is the list of materials for mass change of the QM inspection setup. Figure 4.48 QM Inspection Setup 4 Integrating with Materials Management 278 Figure 4.49 Mass Changes to QM Inspection Setup Data Because this example consists of just one material 2232, select it; choose Save (not shown), and the screen in Figure 4.50 will confirm successful creation of inspection lot 8000000456. Figure 4.50 Inspection Lot for Stock Already in Quality Inspection Figure 4.51 Inspection Type 0800 © 279

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 4.8 Summary Tips and Tricks If you don’t want to use inspection type 08 in your routine business processes, you can also use Transaction QA08 to deactivate inspection type 08 using the options available in the Deactivate Inspection Type tab shown earlier in Figure 4.48. Figure 4.51 shows the display inspection lot (using Transaction QA03) of inspection lot 80000000456. The inspection type that the system assigns is 0800. Note You now have a good understanding of how QM integrates with MM and how inspec- tion types (and inspection origins) relate to movement types in SAP. In Appendix A, you’ll find a selected list movement types and associated inspection origins. You can use that list to integrate QM into many more business processes of procurement and inventory management as deemed necessary to meet business needs. 4.8 Summary In this chapter, you’ve seen how standard configurations and functionalities offered by SAP are sufficient to integrate QM into procurement and inventory management pro- cesses. The QM master data plays a central role in the effective implementation of QM in the procurement and inventory management processes. This one-time setup requires sig- nificant planning and concerted efforts, the importance of which can’t be overempha- sized. Apart from the routine procurement and inventory management processes in which you can integrate QM functionality, the SAP system also offers several options to man- age the complex and diverse businesses processes involved in the entire supply chain and logistics functions. Some of these are subcontracting, stock transfer, and goods receipt without reference to any procurement element, and you can integrate QM in all these business processes. The next chapter covers QM integration into production processes. ©
sections.he:
**Tips and Tricks:** אם לא רוצים type 08 — ניתן Transaction QA08 לביטולו (לשונית Deactivate Inspection Type; ‏Figure 4.48).
Figure 4.51 (Transaction QA03) — lot 80000000456, type 0800.
**הערה:** ראו Appendix A — רשימת סוגי תנועה ו-origins.
הפרק הראה שהתצורות התקניות מספיקות לאינטגרציית QM ברכש וב-IM. נתוני האב מרכזיים (הקמה חד-פעמית הדורשת תכנון). מלבד הרכש וה-IM השגרתיים, ה-SAP מציע — subcontracting, ‏stock transfer, ו-GR ללא הזמנה. הפרק הבא — אינטגרציית QM בייצור.

sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.en: 5.1 Configuration Basics The following sections discuss the configuration settings that you need to ensure are available in the system to integrate QM with PP.
sections.he: להלן הגדרות התצורה לאינטגרציית QM עם PP.

sections.title: Material Type/Task List Combination
sections.en: 5.1.1 Material Type/Task List Combination If the company uses the standard material types, such as raw materials (ROH), finished goods (FERT), or trading goods (HAWA), then their task list types are available in the system. However, if any material type that you want to go through the quality inspec- tion and control process (e.g., spare parts [ERSA] or company-specific material types) is not available, then you need to ensure that the combination of task list type Q and the material type exists in the system. To do so, follow configuration menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM Planning  Inspection Planning  Assign Task List Type to Material Type. Choose New Entries, add the material type/task list type combination, and save your entries.
sections.he: אם משתמשים בסוגי חומר תקניים (ROH, ‏FERT, ‏HAWA), ה-task list types זמינים. אם סוג שיעבור בדיקה (ERSA או ספציפי) אינו זמין — ודאו שצירוף task list type Q עם הסוג קיים. ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • QM Planning • Inspection Planning • Assign Task List Type to Material Type. ‏New Entries, הוסיפו את הצירוף, שמרו.

sections.title: Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters
sections.en: 5.1.2 Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters Process order creation signals to the production department to start production of the material and to check the material’s quantity during various stages of production. The process order quantity denotes the target or planned quantity for production. When the production department has actually produced some or all of the target/planned quantity, it proceeds to confirm this produced quantity in the SAP S/4HANA system. Although there are more PP-specific settings to enable the system to control different functions during process order creation, you make a single setting that is specific to QM. To set up order type-dependent plant parameters, use Transaction COR4 or follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Master Data  Order  Define Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters (see Figure 5.1). Figure 5.1 shows the Planning tab for plant 1710 and order type YBM2. Incorporate inspection type 03 to enable the system to perform in-process (during production) inspection of the material. © 283 5.1 Configuration Basics Figure 5.1 Order Type-Dependent Parameters Note In shop floor control (discrete manufacturing), you can use Transaction OPL8 to access Figure 5.1. This is an integration point between QM and PP. In Section 5.3.2, we’ll cover in-process inspection (inspection type 03). Tips and Tricks If you’ve configured any other inspection types of inspection origin 03, then these will also appear in the dropdown list for you to choose from.

יצירת הזמנת תהליך מאותתת להתחיל ייצור ולבדוק כמות בשלבים. כמות ההזמנה = יעד/מתוכנן. בייצור, הייצור מאשר (confirm) את הכמות. מלבד הגדרות PP, יש הגדרה אחת ספציפית-QM.
ל-Transaction COR4 או SAP IMG • Production • Production Planning for Process Industries • Process Order • Master Data • Order • Define Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters (Figure 5.1). לשונית Planning למפעל 1710, ‏order type YBM2 — שלבו inspection type 03 לבדיקת in-process (5.3.2).
**הערה:** בבדיד (shop floor control), ‏Transaction OPL8.
**Tips and Tricks:** types נוספים מ-origin 03 יופיעו ברשימה.

sections.title: Confirmation Parameters
sections.en: 5.1.3 Confirmation Parameters When you perform confirmation against a process order, whether it’s for an entire order or milestone confirmation, the system makes actual data updates of the yield, scrap, and rework objects. 5 Integrating with Production Planning 284 The confirmation process comprises the quantity produced at each phase of the pro- duction process. If there are quality checks and steps involved in the production pro- cess, then you can control whether the system adheres to the sequence of quality inspections with the configuration settings of confirmation parameters. Example After you mix paint, you want the quality inspector to inspect the mixed paint and record the results. Unless this step is ensured, the system shouldn’t allow the produc- tion person to confirm the next step of production. Further, if you have another step in which the quality inspector must check for filled-up paint cans before they are packed and sealed, then you can control these sequences of steps via the confirmation param- eters’ control. To set up parameters for order confirmation, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Operations  Confirmation  Define Confirmation Parameters. Figure 5.2 shows the parameters for the order confirmation for plant 1710 and order type YBM2. To ensure that the system adheres to confirming various phases of process order and according to the defined sequence, set the operation sequence to E Error when operation sequence is not adhered to. We’ll show how it works in Section 5.3.1. Figure 5.2 QM-Specific Settings in Order Confirmation © 285 5.1 Configuration Basics Similarly, set the Results Rec. (QM) to 1 Error message if no insp. results exist. This set- ting ensures that unless the quality inspection record results in an in-process inspec- tion, the system doesn’t allow confirmation of that specific phase. You’ll see how this setting works in Section 5.3.2. Note During the SAP S/4HANA system implementation project, you discuss, evaluate, and agree with the client on the level of controls required and then make the necessary set- tings. In general, the control should neither be too loose nor too stringent to compro- mise the day-to-day work of business process owners. The level of control also depends on the stability of production and quality processes, as well as business maturity, for optimal production without comprising on quality controls.

באישור מול הזמנת תהליך (הזמנה שלמה או milestone), המערכת מעדכנת yield, ‏scrap, ‏rework. האישור כולל את הכמות בכל phase. אם יש בדיקות בייצור, ניתן לשלוט אם המערכת עומדת ברצף בתצורת ה-confirmation parameters.
**דוגמה:** לאחר ערבוב צבע, הבודק בודק ורושם תוצאות; עד אז, המערכת לא תתיר לאשר את הצעד הבא. וצעד נוסף — בדיקת פחיות מלאות לפני אריזה.
ל-SAP IMG • Production • Production Planning for Process Industries • Process Order • Operations • Confirmation • Define Confirmation Parameters (Figure 5.2; מפעל 1710, ‏order type YBM2). לעמידה ברצף, קבעו operation sequence ל-E (Error when operation sequence is not adhered to) (5.3.1). קבעו Results Rec. (QM) ל-1 (Error message if no insp. results exist) — ללא תוצאות בדיקה, אין אישור (5.3.2).
**הערה:** ביישום, הסכימו עם הלקוח על רמת הבקרה (לא רופפת ולא מחמירה מדי).

sections.title: Control Key
sections.en: 5.1.4 Control Key With the relevant settings in the control key, you can control whether inspection char- acteristics are required or optional and whether the system is to undertake automatic goods receipt. Parameters also exist for scheduling, costing, and printing that are more relevant to PP than QM. Finally, you can also control how the system processes the con- firmations. To set the required parameters of the control key, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Operation  Define Control Keys for Inspection Operations (see Figure 5.3). Figure 5.3 Control Key for Operations 5 Integrating with Production Planning 286 Table 5.2 lists the details about the functions that occur when you enable any field by selecting the relevant checkbox. In general, there is no need to specifically configure control keys in QM; rather, you need to coordinate with a PP resource (or consultant) to enable you to integrate QM- related processes in production. We’ll show you how configuration settings made for control key QM04 apply in the business process for in-process quality inspection (inspection type 03). In Section 5.2.2, you’ll see the actual use of a control key in a mas- ter recipe, and then in business processes. Field Details Scheduling Enables scheduling of operations in a routing or master recipe. Print confirmation Enables the option to print a process order confirmation (the quantity produced in a shift). Det. Cap. Reqmnts Enables capacity requirements planning in the production process. Print Enables printing of shop floor papers. Insp. Char. Required Requires that a master inspection characteristic be assigned to a rout- ing or master recipe. Master inspection characteristics entered for a phase or operation then become the basis of results recording for in- process inspection. Cost Enables cost calculation for an activity. Automatic GR Enables automatic goods receipt when you confirm a process order. Sched. External Op. Enables the provision to enter scheduling data for external operations such as subcontracting or third-party processing. Print Time Tickets Enables printing of operation- and phase-level details of shop floor papers. Rework Enables the option to “rework” a process order. External Processing Option to allow or disallow external processing of operations for a process order. Confirmations Dropdown option to allow or disallow confirmation of operations. If you want the system to adhere to an operation’s sequence during con- firmation, then you need to choose 2 Confirmation required. If you’re using PP-PI, then the same principle applies to the phases’ confirma- tion (instead of the operations’ confirmation, which applies to shop floor control). Table 5.2 Control Key Parameters © 287

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 5.2 Master Data Tips and Tricks To ensure that you can incorporate master inspection characteristics for in-process inspection (during production), select the Insp. Char. Required checkbox. 5.2 Master Data Although significant master data pertaining to PP is managed by the PP team, the focus of this section is to show where, specifically, QM integrates with PP. During the SAP S/4HANA implementation project, QM consultants (or business users) coordinate with the PP team to incorporate the required QM master data (e.g., inspection charac- teristics) into the PP master data (e.g., master recipe or routing).
sections.he: אף שנתוני אב PP מנוהלים ע"י צוות PP, המוקד כאן — היכן QM משתלב. ביישום, יועצי QM מתאמים עם PP לשילוב נתוני אב QM (MICs) בנתוני PP (master recipe/routing).

sections.title: Production Planning and Quality Management Master Data Checklist
sections.en: 5.2.1 Production Planning and Quality Management Master Data Checklist The following is the PP master data that you need to ensure is available in the system:  Material master  Bill of materials (BOM)  Master recipe, rate routing, or routing  Production version The QM master data that you need in the system is as follows:  Inspection types 03 and 04 active in the QM view of the material master of the fin- ished good  Inspection type 02 active in the QM view of the material master of the raw material or semifinished good  Inspection plan usage 5 (for inspection type 04) and 6 (for inspection type 02), both with status 4 (for released)  No inspection plan needed for inspection type 03
sections.he:
**נתוני אב PP:**
• אב חומר
• BOM
• master recipe / rate routing / routing
• production version
**נתוני אב QM:**
• inspection types 03 ו-04 פעילים באב החומר של הגמור.
• inspection type 02 פעיל באב החומר של הגלם/חצי-גמור.
• inspection plan usage 5 (ל-04) ו-6 (ל-02), שניהם status 4.
• אין צורך ב-plan ל-type 03.

sections.title: QM Data in Master Recipe
sections.en: 5.2.2 QM Data in Master Recipe A master recipe uses something called a phase, which works in the same manner as operations do in routing for discrete manufacturing. It’s easier to maintain detailed levels working at the phase level in the master recipe because you can manage and incorporate more production and quality details. In the master recipe, you assign activities such as production duration or labor hours at the phase level and not at the operation level. Therefore, the confirmation of a process order is recorded for a phase and not an operation. You also assign a resource (work 5 Integrating with Production Planning 288 center) at the operation level. The phases below the operation then adopt the resource that you assign at the operation level. The system assigns the standard values and activities (controlled by a control key in the resource) as active at the phase level and not at the operation level. You can, however, integrate in-process quality inspections of QM at either the operation level or the phase level. Tips and Tricks For process manufacturing, we suggest that you integrate QM with PP at the phase level because it offers better controls and visibility, which we’ll show in this chapter. For discrete manufacturing, QM integration with PP for in-process inspection takes place at an operation level. To create a master recipe for which the production version already exists, use Transac- tion C201 or follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Master Data  Master Recipes  Recipe and Material List  Create. On the initial screen of the master recipe, enter Material “SG2200”, Plant “1710”, and Production Version “0001”, and the header screen appears. Figure 5.4 shows the Operations tab of the master recipe, in which the operation is 0010. Enter the Resource “QCLAB” at the operation level, and the system automatically copies it into all the phases below it. The system denotes phase 0040 by the Phase checkbox. When you define an operation as a phase, you also have to define the supe- rior operation, which, for this example, is 0030 (the operation). Operation 0010 and phase 0020 refer to the production process of filling (not shown), but it’s operation 0030 and phase 0040 (the superior operation of which is 0030) that are relevant to QM. Notice the control key QM04, the settings of which you previously made in Section 5.1.4. The system should adhere to the sequence of operations (essentially the same as phases in PP-PI) during confirmation; therefore, you must first confirm phase 0020, then phase 0040, and so on. If you deviate from or miss the phases’ confirmation sequence, the system displays an error message and doesn’t allow you to proceed fur- ther. Similarly, if you don’t record the results of phases 0020 and 0040, the system doesn’t allow you to confirm the respective phases. Because this is an in-process inspection, you also need to enter the master inspection characteristics that then form the basis of your results recording and usage decision. To enter master inspection characteristics, choose a relevant phase, such as 0040, and choose Inspection Characteristic, and the system brings up the screen shown in Figure 5.5. Here, you can enter the QM data elements, such as master inspection characteris- tics, maintain their values as shown in Figure 5.4, and save your settings. © 289 5.2 Master Data Figure 5.4 Master Recipe Figure 5.5 Quality Data in Master Recipe Tips and Tricks For the system to ensure it adheres to the defined phases during the confirmation pro- cess, you must maintain a predecessor-successor relationship between any two phases. To maintain the relationship of one phase to another, select the desired phase (e.g., phase 0040), and choose the Relationship icon (the chain link icon) shown in Figure 5.4. Once on the detailed screen of a phase relationship of phase 0040, enter the predecessor phase, which in this example is “0020”; here the relationship type needs to be “FS” (finish-start), which means that phase 0020 needs to finish before phase 0040 can start. For shop floor control (discrete manufacturing), there’s no such requirements for main- taining relationships among operations in a routing. 5 Integrating with Production Planning 290 Tips and Tricks If the production process also entails external processing, such as subcontracting, and if you must also perform quality inspection for it, then in the phase details that involve subcontracting, you can assign inspection type 0060 to enable you to integrate QM in the subcontracting process (external processing). For example, to enter external pro- cessing details in the screen in Figure 5.4, choose Phase 0060 and then choose Operat. Details (the magnifying glass icon). In the General Data tab, enter the external process- ing (subcontracting) details and inspection type 0130. Refer to Chapter 4, Section 4.5, in which we cover the end-to-end business process of subcontracting (external processing) and how to put inspection type 0130 to use. Note For discrete manufacturing (shop floor control), use Transaction CA01 to create a routing. For QM integration with PP in discrete manufacturing, you assign the master inspection characteristics at the operation level. To create a rate routing of a material in repetitive manufacturing (REM), use Transaction CA21; the process of assigning master inspection characteristics at the operation level is the same as in discrete manufacturing.

sections.title: Business Processes in Production Planning
sections.en: 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning In the following sections, we’ll cover the end-to-end business processes in PP, beginning with process order creation, quality inspection upon goods issue, and the in-process inspection, followed by quality inspection upon goods receipt into the warehouse.
sections.he: להלן התהליכים המלאים ב-PP — יצירת הזמנת תהליך, בדיקה ב-GI, in-process inspection, ובדיקה ב-GR למחסן.

sections.title: Process Manufacturing and Discrete Manufacturing
sections.en: 5.3.1 Process Manufacturing and Discrete Manufacturing Figure 5.6 shows an end-to-end business process for production execution in which QM integrates into the following all important steps: 1 A process order (or production order in shop floor control) is created. 2 Goods are issued out to begin the production process. 3 However, before the production operator uses the issued-out material, a quality check is put in place. This is via inspection lot creation upon goods issue, and the inspection type is 02, which must be quality cleared. 4 The actual production begins, and further quality checks must ensue for in-process inspection or during production inspection. This is ensured via inspection lot cre- ation wth inspection type 03. 5 The goods are produced and delivered or received at the warehouse. 6 At this stage, another round of quality checks takes place to ensure that the deliv- ered finished goods meet quality standards. For this, the system creates an inspec- tion lot with inspection type 04. © 291 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning Figure 5.6 Business Processes in Production Planning Let’s begin with the first step: creating a process order. Process Order To create a process order, use Transaction COR1 or follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Process Order  Process Order  Create  With Material. Note For discrete manufacturing (shop floor control), Transaction CO01 is used to create a production order. On the screen that appears, enter Material “SG2200”, Plant “1710”, and Order Type “YBM2”, and then press (Enter). This leads to the process order header screen shown in Figure 5.7. Enter the Total Qty. (process order quantity) of “100” kg. With PP-relevant settings in place, the system performs several functions, such as automatically enter- ing start and end dates of production. Figure 5.7 Process Order: General Data After you release and save the process order, the Assignment tab shown in Figure 5.8 already has an in-process inspection (inspection type 03) lot number, 30000000555. Depending on the PP settings, the system creates the in-process inspection lot either at Process order/ production order Goods issue QM inspection lot (Insp. type 02) Goods receipt QM inspection lot (Insp. type 04) In-process inspection (Insp. type 03) 5 Integrating with Production Planning 292 the time of creating a process order or on its release. You use this inspection lot num- ber to record results and make a usage decision for relevant phases of the process order of the Goods Receipt tab. Figure 5.8 Process Order: Assignment Figure 5.9 shows that on goods receipt of a process order, the system triggers quality inspection (inspection type 04) and places the stock in quality inspection. Choose Material to view the components (accordingly, the BOM of material SG2200) that material RM1420 will be consumed in production. Figure 5.9 Process Order: Goods Receipt © 293 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning Figure 5.10 shows the material list of a process order consisting of material RM1420 and the requirement quantity of 10 kg. Because there is also a quality inspection on goods issue for the process order, the system creates an inspection lot (inspection type 02). You can also choose Operations in Figure 5.10, and the system brings up the master rec- ipe that we covered in Section 5.2.2. Save the process order, and the system creates pro- cess order number 1002145. Figure 5.10 Process Order: Material List Goods Issue against Process Order Access the screen in Figure 5.11 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Issue and then Order from the dropdown lists at the top. Enter process order number “1002145” in the blank field. The movement type for goods issue against a process order is 261 and is shown at the top-right corner of the screen. Save the entries, and the system creates material document number 4900007692 and an inspection lot of inspection type 02. Figure 5.11 Goods Issue for Process Order Goods Issue Inspection: Inspection Type 02 Figure 5.12 shows the inspection lot of inspection type 02 (Transaction QA03) that the system creates on goods issue of material RM1420 and batch number 45 for the pro- cess order (refer to Figure 5.10). The inspection lot consists of relevant details, such as 5 Integrating with Production Planning 294 material document number 4900007692 and process order number 1002145. This inspection type isn’t stock-based, so the quality inspection steps are results recording and usage decision. Warning If the material is rejected during goods issue inspection (inspection type 02), there is no way for the system to control that it’s not to be used further in the production process. To ensure better controls, you must return the issued-out defective material back to the warehouse using the Return Delivery option. For return delivery, use Transaction MIGO (refer to Figure 5.11 again), and select Return Delivery and then Material Docu- ment from the dropdown lists at the top. Enter the material document number, which in this example is “4900007692” (the same document number against which you issued the material from the warehouse). The relevant movement type for return deliv- ery is 262. In the return delivery option, you can also control the quantity of defective material that you’re returning to the warehouse. Figure 5.12 Inspection Type 02 © 295 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning Confirmation To bring greater visibility to the production process and the quality steps involved, you periodically confirm the produced quantity at a resource or work center. The frequen- cies with which you confirm an operation, phase, or order depend entirely on business needs. For example, in 24 hours, you can confirm the quantities produced at the end of an eight-hour shift. This means you have to perform two partial confirmations and then one final confirmation. When you perform the final confirmation, the system no longer expects any further confirmations against the operation or the order. To proceed with confirmation of a time ticket, use Transaction COR6N or follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Process Order  Confirmation  Enter for Phase  Time Ticket. Note For time ticket confirmation in discrete manufacturing (shop floor control), use Trans- action CO11N. Figure 5.13 shows the initial screen to confirm the time ticket. Enter the Order number as “1002145”, enter the Phase as “0060”, and press (Enter). Figure 5.13 Time Ticket Confirmation of a Process Order 5 Integrating with Production Planning 296 We deliberately enter the Phase as “0060” to check whether the configuration you undertook for operation/phase sequence adherence in Figure 5.2 is working. The sys- tem displays an error message, as shown at the bottom of the screen. This means you have to first confirm the phase as 0020, which is the first phase in Figure 5.4. So, you undertake the phase-wise confirmation as shown in Figure 5.4 while also ensuring that before you confirm phase 0060, you’ve recorded results for that operation/phase. Figure 5.14 shows the error message that appears when you try to confirm a phase with- out first recording results of phase 0040. Again, this is due to the settings that you made in Figure 5.3, which stipulates that unless the QM results are first entered for the phase, the system doesn’t allow you to confirm the phase. All these quality controls, checks, and balances during the production process help you manage quality aspects of production, thereby minimizing or eliminating in-process or produced goods rejec- tions. Figure 5.14 Error Message Indicating QM Data Is Missing In-Process Inspection: Inspection Type 03 Figure 5.15 shows the in-process inspection lot number 30000000555 for process order number 1002145. As already mentioned, the in-process inspection for production © 297 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning (process order or production order) has inspection type 03. The details here are the same that you saw in Figure 5.8, such as inspection lot number and batch number. Inspection lots of inspection type 03 aren’t stock-relevant, so you need to record results and undertake a usage decision (and no stock posting is involved). Note You can also integrate QM business processes of in-process inspections using process instruction sheets. Similarly, you can also conduct in-process quality inspections using inspection points. Figure 5.15 Inspection Type 03 Note For in-process inspection of inspection types 03 or 13, there is no need to create an inspection plan (Transaction QP01) of a material. This is because you already incorpo- rate the relevant master inspection characteristics in the phases/operations of the master recipe, routing, or rate routing of material. Refer again to Figure 5.5, where you entered the in-process quality inspection data for phase 0020 of the master recipe of material SG2200. 5 Integrating with Production Planning 298 For a flexible in-process inspection, you can have the system create inspection lot char- acteristics for released production order operations. Therefore, changes to unreleased order operations are still possible and are reflected in the inspection lot as soon as they are released. This allows for a flexible in-process or in-production inspection. To use this feature, follow the menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Client Level. In the Further Settings area of the screen, select the Late Characteristic Creation checkbox. Goods Receipt for Process Order Once the goods are produced for a process order, you deliver them to the warehouse so that the warehouse staff can record the goods receipt. On goods receipt, the system cre- ates an inspection lot of inspection type 04 with reference to the process order 1002145. Access the screen in Figure 5.16 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Receipt and then Order from the dropdown lists at the top. Then, enter process order number “1002145” in the blank box. The movement type for goods receipt against a process order is 101 and is shown at the top-right corner of the screen. Save your entries, and the system creates material document number 5000000018. Figure 5.16 Goods Receipt for Process Order Goods Receipt Inspection: Inspection Type 04 Figure 5.17 shows the inspection lot of inspection type 04 (Transaction QA03) that the system creates on goods receipt for process order 1002145 (refer to Figure 5.9). The inspection lot consists of relevant details, such as material document number 5000002463 and process order number 1002145. This inspection type is stock-relevant, so the quality steps are results recording (and any defects recording), usage decision, and stock posting. © 299 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning Figure 5.17 Inspection Type 04 Now that you know the difference between inspection types 03 and 04, Table 5.3 pro- vides a comparison overview of the two inspection types, wherein an X denotes the availability of the feature or functionality. Feature/Function Origin 03 Origin 04 (Early Inspection Lot) Separate planning X Dynamic modification X X Stock relevant X Partial lots X Table 5.3 Differences between Inspection Types 03 and 04 5 Integrating with Production Planning 300 Tips and Tricks You can also let the system create an early inspection lot for inspection type 04 at the time of creating, or release a process or production order so that you can inspect the goods and record its results before posting them in stock. To do so, choose Early Inspec- tion Lot Creation for Order Item in the Control InsLot (inspection lot) field from the dropdown list while activating inspection type 04 in material master. This entire pro- cess is known as early inspection lot creation for a process or production order.

sections.title: Repetitive Manufacturing
sections.en: 5.3.2 Repetitive Manufacturing Repetitive manufacturing (REM) finds greater application in production scenarios with high repetition rates, high product stability, and low product complexity. REM is char- acterized by quantity-based and period-based production (uninterrupted production over a longer period of time). In this section, we’ll cover the important REM processes of not just PP but also QM. Either the system automatically creates inspection lots or you have to undertake the relevant business process steps. Figure 5.18 shows the end-to-end REM business processes: 1 Create the REM planned order (also interchangeably referred to as the run schedule header). 2 Create the QM inspection lot of inspection type 13 for the in-process inspection. 3 The confirmation process ensures goods issue and goods receipt (depending on the settings made in the REM profile). 4 On goods receipt, the system creates another inspection lot of inspection type 04. Figure 5.18 Business Processes in REM Inspection points X X Batch classification X X Direct link inspection lot order X Feature/Function Origin 03 Origin 04 (Early Inspection Lot) Table 5.3 Differences between Inspection Types 03 and 04 (Cont.) REM planned order QM inspection lot (Insp. type 13) QM inspection lot (Insp. type 04) Reporting point confirmation (automatic goods issue and goods receipt) © 301 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning PP and QM Master Data Checklist The following is the PP master data that you need to ensure is available in the system:  Material master  BOM  Rate routing or routing  Production version The QM master data that you need in the system is as follows:  Inspection types 13 and 04 active in the QM view of the material master  Inspection plan usage 5 (for inspection type 04) with status 4 (for released) Note For in-process inspection of inspection type 13, there is no need to create an inspection plan (Transaction QP01) for the material. This is because you already incorporate the relevant master inspection characteristics in the operations of routing or rate routing of the material. Run Schedule Header The production team often has to make changes to the existing planning elements, such as planned orders, or create new planned orders to account for production con- straints or other practical realities, such as an unplanned plant or machine shutdown. This example uses an already created REM planned order 2694 and continues with the remaining business processes, with greater focus on QM integration in the REM pro- duction type. Tips and Tricks You can use Transaction MD11 to create a REM-planned order. On the initial screen for Planned Order Profile, choose LA-Stock Order. Enter Material “FG233”, Plant “1710”, and Order Quantity “100” kg, and save. In-Process Inspection for Run Schedule Header: Inspection Type 13 With the planned order for the material already available in the system, you can now proceed to create an in-process inspection lot for the REM-planned order (run schedule header). It’s important to note that for in-process inspection in REM, the system doesn’t consider the quantity of the REM-planned order that you previously created. Rather, the system creates an inspection quantity based on a material/plant/production version 5 Integrating with Production Planning 302 combination. So, the quantity details that you enter for the production version become the basis for the system to calculate inspection lot quantity. To create an inspection lot for in-process inspection for the REM-planned order, use Transaction MFPR or follow menu path Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Creation  Inspection Lots for Prod. Versions (see Figure 5.19). Here you see the initial screen for inspection lot processing of materials produced using the REM production type. Choose the QM Active radio button so that the system brings up the materials with QM active, and enter Plant “1710”, Material Number “FG233”, and Production Version “0001”. Choose Execute, which leads to Figure 5.20. Figure 5.20 shows that the last inspection lot the system created for material FG233 and plant 1710 was 130000000000. The red signal light indicates that the results recording and usage decision for inspection lot 130000000000 are already made, and the sys- tem is now ready to create a new inspection lot. The fact that a usage decision for inspection lot 130000000000 is already made is also shown by the green checkmark. Were this inspection lot still open, the signal light would be red, and the system wouldn’t allow you to create a new inspection lot for this material, plant, and produc- tion version combination. The system would also not display the green checkmark for the open inspection lot. Figure 5.19 REM Inspection Lot Processing Select the checkbox on the left side of Figure 5.20 for production version 0001, and then choose More  Create Inspection Lots for All Selected Items. The system creates a new inspection lot of inspection type 13 and displays a confirmation message. © 303 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning Figure 5.20 REM Inspection Lots for Production Versions: Worklist Figure 5.21 shows the in-process inspection lot number 130000000000 for the run schedule header (REM-planned order). Other relevant details that you’ll find in the Data for Order area are the Material number FG233, Plant 1710, and Production Version 0001 combination. Figure 5.21 Inspection Type 13 Figure 5.22 shows that the system considers the maximum quantity of the production version to create an inspection lot quantity. Depending on the sampling procedure, the system calculates the sample of inspection quantity. 5 Integrating with Production Planning 304 Figure 5.22 Inspection Lot Quantities in REM As with all in-process inspections, inspection lots of inspection type 13 aren’t stock- relevant, so you need to record results and undertake a usage decision (and no stock posting is involved). Repetitive Manufacturing Assembly Confirmation A REM confirmation indicates that you’ve performed actual production and are now entering the details of the goods produced in the system. It’s important to note that during the assembly backflush, the system automatically posts the component con- sumptions (goods issue). Depending on how the PP team has set up the REM profile and assigned it to the mate- rial, the system performs the necessary functions. It also often makes sense to use reporting point confirmation to post the withdrawal of components and production activities at an earlier stage and after operations are already completed. When you post the goods receipt for the finished parts during confirmation, the sys- tem performs several different actions by default (these are controlled to a large extent using the REM profile). To access the REM confirmation for an assembly backflush, use Transaction MFBF or follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Data Entry  Repet- itive Manufacturing Confirmation (see Figure 5.23). On the initial screen of REM confir- mation, select the Assembly backflush radio button. You use the screen to confirm the production yield, as well as record component consumption and activities. In the screen shown in Figure 5.23, you now perform the actual assembly backflush posting for Material FG233, Plant 1710, and Production Version 0001. The yield confirmation for the material in this REM assembly backflush is 10 kg. Reporting point backflush in REM occurs when the system is able to automatically backflush several operations in the processing sequence. Using the reporting point backflush procedure, you can backflush components synchronized with actual con- sumption as much as possible. © 305 5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning Figure 5.23 REM Confirmation When you save the REM assembly backflush, the system issues a message at the bot- tom of the screen confirming the goods movements (goods issue and goods receipt) and activities posting. Note If you have a specific business need to conduct a quality check on goods issue of the REM production type, then you need to follow the steps that we covered for inspection type 02 in Section 5.3.1. However, we suggest that you ask your PP team to configure the settings of the REM profile so that the goods issue and goods receipt steps aren’t performed in the same step. It makes more sense to first issue out (goods issue) the component for a reporting point, perform its quality inspection, and then, as a next step, perform goods receipt subsequently (or at the end of production process) and on another reporting point. Goods Receipt Inspection (REM): Inspection Type 04 Figure 5.24 shows the inspection lot of inspection type 04 (Transaction QA03), which the system creates on goods receipt for the run schedule header. The inspection lot consists of relevant details, such as material document number 4900007694. This inspection type is stock-relevant, so you perform the quality steps such as results recording, usage decision, and stock posting. 5 Integrating with Production Planning 306 Figure 5.24 Inspection Type 04 Table 5.4 shows a comparison among the three manufacturing types—discrete, repeti- tive, and process—and how they fit into QM. sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.en: 6.1 Configuration Basics The following are the configuration settings that you need to ensure are available:  Assignment of inspection lot origin to delivery type  Assignment of inspection type to delivery category Inspection Type Inspection Plan Usage Inspection Type Description 06 6 Inspection for customer returns 10 6 Inspection for delivery to customer (with order) 11 6 Inspection for delivery to customer (without order) 12 6 General inspection for delivery Table 6.1 Inspection Types in SAP S/4HANA Sales 6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales 310 To assign an inspection lot origin to a relevant delivery type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Inspection at Shipping  Assign Inspection Lot Origin to Delivery Type (see Figure 6.1 1). Figure 6.1 Inspection Type and Inspection Origin Assignments First, you assign the inspection lot origin to the relevant delivery type. You already know that you can’t change the inspection lot origin; therefore, logically assigning the inspec- tion lot origin to delivery types ensures that the necessary business functions work cor- rectly. For example, inspection origin 06 is specific to customer returns, so assigning this inspection origin for all delivery types for customer returns makes sense. In this example, assign inspection lot origin 10 to delivery type (DlvTy) LF (Outbound Delivery), 11 to LO (Delivery w/o Ref.), and 06 to LR (Returns Delivery). Although it isn’t shown, also assign inspection lot origin 12 to delivery type LO2 (Delivery w/o Ref.) in Figure 6.1 1. We’ll show the associated business process later in this chapter. Inspection origin 12 is for inspection for general delivery. The second configuration step is to assign the inspection type to a delivery category. Follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Inspection at Shipping  Assign Inspection Type to Delivery Category 2. Here, you can assign inspection types of relevant inspection origin to the relevant delivery category (Delv.Cat). If you’ve configured a specific inspection type to cater to a business need, then you can assign it in this step. The different usage of a delivery category is shown in Figure 6.1 2.

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 6.2 Master Data Ensure that the following SAP S/4HANA Sales master data is available in the SAP S/4HANA system: © 311 6.2 Master Data  Material master, including complete maintenance of sales views  Business partner in a customer role  Material pricing condition The QM master data that you need is as follows:  Inspection types 06, 10, 11, and 12 active in the QM view of the material master of the finished good  Inspection plan usage 6 (goods issue) having status 4 (for released) for all four inspection types  Quality information record: SD A quality information record (SD) is a relationship between materials that the cus- tomer orders. In this specific master data creation step, you maintain the QM integra- tion relationship with SAP S/4HANA Sales. To create a quality information record (SD), use Transaction QV51 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Quality Info Record: SD  Create. On the initial screen that appears, enter Customer “17100003” and Sales Organization “1710”, and choose Control Data. The screen in Figure 6.2 appears; choose Edit  New Info Record (not shown; located on bottom-right side of the screen) to go to the dialog for creating new data, and proceed as follows: 1. Enter the Material as “QM001”. 2. Choose the Delivery cat.. If there is no specific category, leave it blank. 3. Enter a short text for Additional information (optional). 4. Choose the Before delivery radio button in the Quality inspection area. Here, if you choose Before delivery, then the system requires you to perform QM functions before you can issue goods. For After delivery, the system allows goods issuance, and you can subsequently perform QM functions. The By customer option refers to spe- cial cases when the customer inspects the goods to confirm that they meet the spec- ifications. 5. Save the customer information record. Figure 6.2 also shows one important difference: customer information records control individual materials for a customer, whereas customer specifications apply to all mate- rials of a customer. This example is based on a customer information record, which provides better differentiation in terms of material assignment. Tips and Tricks When choosing Documents in Figure 6.2, you also have the option to link the quality information record with a quality document (e.g., quality assurance agreements or special specifications). In the dialog window for linking the QM information record to documents, use the input help to choose the document that you want to attach. 6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales 312 Figure 6.2 Quality Information Record: Customer

sections.title: Business Processes
sections.en: 6.3 Business Processes This section covers the following four business processes in SAP S/4HANA Sales:  Customer delivery with sales order  Customer delivery without sales order  Return order  General delivery
sections.he:
סעיף זה מכסה ארבעה תהליכים ב-Sales:
• משלוח ללקוח עם הזמנה
• משלוח ללקוח ללא הזמנה
• הזמנת החזרה
• משלוח כללי

sections.title: Customer Delivery with Sales Order
sections.en: 6.3.1 Customer Delivery with Sales Order The customer places an order for a material, for which you create a sales order. When you’re ready to deliver the material with reference to the sales order, you first create an outbound delivery. At this time, the system informs you in the status bar that the qual- ity inspection is being prepared. You perform the QM functions, such as results record- ing and usage decision. Next, you post goods issue with reference to the outbound delivery and proceed to bill the customer and receive payment (not covered in this chapter). Figure 6.3 depicts this business process. © 313 6.3 Business Processes Figure 6.3 Business Process of QM Integration with SAP S/4HANA Sales Note If the customer has a scheduling agreement or a quantity or value contract with the company, you can still use this business process to integrate QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales. Instead of a sales order, replace it with the relevant sales option. First, use Transaction VA01 to create a sales order. Enter order type “OR”, as well as the details of organizational data, such as sales organization “1710”, distribution channel “10”, and division “00”, and then press (Enter). As shown in Figure 6.4, enter the customer, who in this case is Sold-to Party “17100003”, the Delivering Plant “1710”, the payment terms 0001 (not shown), and the Incoterms in the header of the sales order. Figure 6.4 Sales Order Sales order Outbound delivery Results recording and usage decision Post goods issue Billing and payment QM inspection lot (Insp. type 10) 6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales 314 At the item level, enter Material “QM001” and the Order Quantity “10” PC. There is sig- nificantly more information that you can maintain in the sales order, but this is the minimum information that you need to maintain. If you navigate to the item’s details view of the material, you can also maintain its usage that the system will refer to while creating the inspection lot of the relevant inspection type. Notice that the Requested Deliv.Date (required delivery date) in this case is 02/24/ 2024. Save the sales order, and the system creates sales order number 5612 in this example. Using Transaction VL01N, the initial screen will the Outbound Delivery with Order Ref- erence screen. Here, enter Shipping Point “1710”, Selection Date “02/24/2024” (the delivery date covered in the previous step), and (sales) Order “5612”. Because the config- uration of the sales order automatically picks up the relevant delivery type, you don’t need to enter anything in this field. This leads to Figure 6.5. Figure 6.5 Outbound Delivery with Reference to Sales Order In the screen in Figure 6.5, select the line item for which you want to create an out- bound delivery. Further, at this stage, you also need to enter the pick quantity as 10 PC, which in this example is the same as the order quantity. A pick quantity is the actual quantity that you pick or load to create delivery. If you try to issue goods for the out- bound delivery at this time by choosing Post Goods Issue, you’ll see an error message at the bottom of the screen (not shown). The system creates inspection lot 100000000308 while you’re still creating the out- bound delivery for the sales order. Because you set the Before delivery radio button in the quality information record (SD) for the customer/material/plant combination, you must first perform quality functions before the system allows you to post goods issue © 315 6.3 Business Processes for the delivery. Save your outbound delivery, and the system creates delivery number 80005137. In due course, you record results and undertake usage decision for inspection lot 100000000308. The system now allows you to post goods issue by using Transaction VL02N and entering delivery number 80005137. Figure 6.6 shows Inspection Lot 100000000308 of Inspection Type 10 (Transaction QA03), which the system creates for delivery to the customer for Sales Order 5612. The reference of Delivery 80005137 is also shown for said inspection lot. Figure 6.6 Inspection Type 10: Delivery to Customer with Customer Order
