sections.title: Customer Delivery without Sales Order
sections.en: 6.3.2 Customer Delivery without Sales Order You can create inspection lots for a customer delivery for which there is no sales order (or customer order) reference. This may be the case when the customer requests urgent 6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales 316 or immediate delivery without first issuing an order (a purchase order for the customer and sales order for the company). Access the screen in Figure 6.7 using Transaction VL01NO, and enter Shipping Point “1710” and Delivery Type “LO”, as well as the details of the organizational data, such as Sales Organization “1710”, Distribution Channel “10”, and Division “00”, and press (Enter). In Figure 6.8, enter the customer, who is also ship-to party “17100003” in this case. At the item level, enter Material “QM001” and the Order Quantity of “10” PC; select the line item for which you want to create the outbound delivery. At this stage, you also need to enter the Picked Quantity of “10” PC. Here, again, if you try to issue goods for the outbound delivery at this time by choosing Post Goods Issue, an error message appears, explaining that the system created inspection lot 110000000000 when you were still creating the delivery without reference to a sales order. Because you set the Before delivery radio button in the quality information record (SD) for the customer/ material/plant combination, you must perform quality functions before the system allows you to post goods issue for the delivery. Save the outbound delivery, and the sys- tem creates delivery number 80005138. Figure 6.7 Customer Delivery without Sales Order Reference Meanwhile, after performing all the necessary quality functions, the system creates inspection lot 110000000000. The system now allows you to post goods issue by using Transaction VL02N and by entering delivery number 80005138. Figure 6.9 shows the Inspection Lot 110000000000 of Inspection Type 11 (Transaction QA03), for which the system creates customer delivery without reference to sales order. The reference of Delivery 80005138 is available in the inspection lot. © 317 6.3 Business Processes Figure 6.8 Delivery without Reference to Sales Order Figure 6.9 Inspection Type 11: Delivery to Customer without Sales Order 6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales 318

sections.title: Return Order
sections.en: 6.3.3 Return Order A return order may occur due to defective or damaged goods or excess or slow-moving products that the customer returns and the company accepts. Figure 6.10 shows the steps involved in the business process of a return order: 1. Create the return order (order type RE; Transaction VA01). 2. Create the outbound delivery with reference to a return order (Transaction VL01N). 3. Perform QM functions such as results recording and usage decision. There is no stock posting involved. 4. Post goods receipt (Transaction VL02N). Because this is a customer return and is with reference to the return order, the system automatically provides the option to post goods receipt using this transaction. 5. Issue the credit memo. Figure 6.10 Business Process Flow for Return Orders Figure 6.11 shows Inspection Lot 60000000000 of Inspection Type 06 (Transaction QA03), which the system creates for Sales Order (return order) 60000235. In this business scenario, you can integrate inspection type 05 (other goods receipt). Refer to Chapter 4, Section 4.5.2, which covers inspection type 05, for more information. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 6.4 Summary 6.4 Summary Standard solutions and configurations delivered by SAP S/4HANA are sufficient to independently configure, implement, and integrate QM into SAP S/4HANA Sales busi- ness processes. By making necessary configuration settings and then setting up the rel- evant QM master data, a one-time task, you can quickly and comprehensively integrate QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales. You can also leverage quality certificate functionality to issue outgoing quality certificates for goods that you send to customers. The next chapter covers integrating QM with plant maintenance (PM), specifically for test equipment management. ©
sections.he: הפתרונות התקניים מספיקים לאינטגרציית QM עם Sales. בתצורה ובהקמת נתוני אב (חד-פעמית), ניתן לשלב מהר ומקיף. ניתן גם תעודות איכות יוצאות ללקוחות. הפרק הבא — אינטגרציית QM עם PM (ניהול ציוד בדיקה).

sections.title: Deciding which Functionalities to Implement
sections.en: 7.1 Deciding which Functionalities to Implement As already mentioned, apart from the central role that the QM plays, two other areas of SAP S/4HANA that contribute significantly to test equipment management business processes are PM and MM. Figure 7.1 shows the four possible business scenarios in which you need to decide on integrating PM, MM, both, or neither to meet business needs. We’ll evaluate all four possible business scenarios in the following sections. Figure 7.1 Possible Scenarios to Handle Test Equipment Management PM MM PM MM PM MM PM MM Test Equipment Management x x x x © 325
sections.he:
מלבד QM, שני תחומים תורמים לניהול ציוד בדיקה — PM ו-MM. Figure 7.1 — ארבעה תרחישים: לשלב PM, ‏MM, שניהם, או אף אחד.
(Figure 7.1 — Test Equipment Management: ‏PM✓/MM✗; ‏PM✓/MM✓; ‏PM✗/MM✓; ‏PM✗/MM✗.)

sections.title: Scenario 1: PM without MM
sections.en: 7.1.1 Scenario 1: PM without MM In PM, you maintain test equipment as a piece of equipment, hierarchically structured and assigned to a detailed maintenance plan. This makes it possible to monitor inspec- tion dates and to create and process maintenance plan orders (e.g., for calibration). With this option, you create and manage pieces of equipment independently of mate- rial master data. Because equipment in PM isn’t stock-relevant, business functions of MM, such as purchase requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice receipt, and inventory management (storage of equipment), aren’t in scope.
sections.he: ב-PM, מתחזקים את ציוד הבדיקה כ-equipment, מובנה היררכית, מוקצה ל-maintenance plan — לניטור תאריכי בדיקה וליצירת maintenance plan orders (כיול). יוצרים ומנהלים את הציוד עצמאית מאב החומר. מאחר שה-equipment ב-PM אינו מבוסס-מלאי, פונקציות MM (דרישת רכש, הזמנה, GR, חשבונית, IM) אינן בהיקף.

sections.title: Scenario 2: PM with MM
sections.en: 7.1.2 Scenario 2: PM with MM Implementing this business scenario is the most workload-intensive, but its enormous benefit is that it enables extensive visibility and availability of information across the logistics and supply chain management. In this chapter, we’ll be covering this business scenario so that you have the maximum available information to help you decide whether it’s worth the time and effort to integrate QM with both PM and MM or just with one. Because MM is also in scope, the business user can procure and store the test equipment. Moreover, it’s also possible to serialize and manage as a piece of equip- ment. This is also the option to synchronize the material master, equipment master, and serial number.
sections.he: התרחיש העתיר ביותר בעומס, אך עם נראות וזמינות מקיפות. מכוסה בפרק. מאחר ש-MM בהיקף, ניתן לרכוש ולאחסן את הציוד, ולסדר (serialize) ולנהל כ-equipment. גם לסנכרן אב חומר, equipment master, ו-serial number.

sections.title: Scenario 3: MM without PM
sections.en: 7.1.3 Scenario 3: MM without PM With this business scenario, you create test equipment as the material master and pro- cess all management of purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and goods receipt. Fur- thermore, the materials that you create also integrate with the different task list types in the same way as the production resources/tools (PRTs). This business scenario doesn’t include any of the PM business processes, such as calibration planning, calibra- tion monitoring, and their documentation.
sections.he: יוצרים את ציוד הבדיקה כאב חומר ומעבדים דרישות רכש/הזמנות/GR. החומרים משתלבים ב-task lists כמו PRTs. ללא תהליכי PM (תכנון/ניטור כיול ותיעוד).

sections.title: Scenario 4: Neither MM nor PM
sections.en: 7.1.4 Scenario 4: Neither MM nor PM This business scenario has only a restricted management of test equipment as a PRT or a document master record. Ultimately, it’s available as the where-used list in QM. There is no calibration planning, execution, or documentation or information availability in the SAP system, nor does it go through the procurement process available in MM. 7.2 Defining Test Equipment In quality planning, you can manage test equipment as a PRT, which you can define in the SAP system by using different types of master records: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 326  Material master record  Equipment master record  PRT master record  Document master record Let’s briefly review each of these available options.
sections.he:
ניהול מוגבל של ציוד הבדיקה כ-PRT או document master record. זמין כ-where-used ב-QM. ללא תכנון/ביצוע/תיעוד כיול, וללא תהליך רכש.

**7.2 הגדרת ציוד בדיקה:** בתכנון איכות, מנהלים ציוד בדיקה כ-PRT, מוגדר בסוגי רשומות שונים:
• material master record
• equipment master record
• PRT master record
• document master record

sections.title: Test Equipment as a Material
sections.en: 7.2.1 Test Equipment as a Material If you need logistics functions, such as procurement, storage, or quality inspection, then it makes sense to represent test equipment in the material master records. This provides all the views of the material master record. The material merely defines the type of test equipment. This is sufficient for processing purchasing and planning oper- ations (task lists, inspection plans, etc.) because the individual pieces of test equipment of a given type usually have the same properties and are therefore interchangeable. For IM, the individual pieces of test equipment aren’t relevant; rather, it’s the number of pieces of test equipment that is important. With the option for serializing materials, the system also provides the option to repre- sent individual pieces of test equipment. In this case, the material itself corresponds to a particular configuration for test equipment, and the serial number represents the individual test equipment.
sections.he:
אם נדרשות פונקציות לוגיסטיות (רכש, אחסון, בדיקה) — הגיוני באב חומר (כל התצוגות). החומר מגדיר את סוג הציוד — מספיק לרכש ולתכנון (החלקים מאותו סוג בעלי תכונות זהות וניתנים-להחלפה). ל-IM, מספר החלקים חשוב (לא הבודדים).
עם serializing, ניתן לייצג חלקים בודדים — החומר תואם לתצורה, וה-serial number מייצג חלק בודד.

sections.title: Test Equipment as PM Equipment
sections.en: 7.2.2 Test Equipment as PM Equipment A significantly higher range of functionality is available if you represent the test equip- ment as equipment in PM. Equipment master records are maintained in PM and allow you to define individual devices and structure them hierarchically. This means that you can represent both individual test equipment and combined test equipment or more complex measuring tools. PM provides comprehensive functions for managing, monitoring, maintaining, and calibrating the test equipment. When pieces of equip- ment are included in task lists, you can check whether all the relevant test equipment is available when production lots are issued. When material numbers are serialized, the system provides an option for defining and linking both master records (material master and equipment master) in one process. First, you enter the material number or select an existing number. Then, you generate a new serial number using the serialization function. In the subsequent dialog box, you can then switch to the equipment view, activate the equipment master record, and add device-specific data. You can generate reports such as results history, graphical trend analyses, and usage lists. © 327
sections.he:
פונקציונליות רבה יותר אם מייצגים כ-equipment ב-PM. ה-equipment master maintained ב-PM, ומאפשר הגדרה היררכית (ציוד בודד או משולב/מורכב). ‏PM מספק ניהול, ניטור, אחזקה וכיול. ב-task lists, ניתן לבדוק זמינות ציוד בהנפקת lots.
עם serialization, ניתן להגדיר ולקשר שתי הרשומות (material ו-equipment) בתהליך אחד: הזינו מספר חומר, צרו serial number, עברו ל-equipment view, הפעילו את ה-equipment master, והוסיפו נתוני מכשיר. ניתן דוחות (results history, ‏trend analyses, ‏usage lists).

sections.title: Test Equipment as a Production Resource/Tool
sections.en: 7.2.3 Test Equipment as a Production Resource/Tool Creating test equipment as a PRT enables you to store information about its status and location, as well as the standard SAP system management data. You can also group the test equipment (e.g., measurement equipment, inspection equipment, etc.) or classify it using the central classification system. The master record for PRT doesn’t contain a great deal of data, which greatly restricts the related functionality in the SAP system. In most cases, when you represent test equipment as a PRT, you maintain only rough master data, while the system doesn’t support other logistics functions either. For this reason, representing test equipment as a PRT is the simplest option and doesn’t allow any additional functionality beyond providing a where-used list.
sections.he: יצירה כ-PRT מאחסנת סטטוס ומיקום ונתוני ניהול. ניתן לקבץ (מדידה/בדיקה) או לסווג. ל-PRT master record מעט נתונים — מגביל את הפונקציונליות. לרוב נתוני אב גסים בלבד; אין תמיכה בפונקציות לוגיסטיות. הפשוט ביותר — רק where-used.

sections.title: Test Equipment as a Document
sections.en: 7.2.4 Test Equipment as a Document You can use the PRT master record to refer to document data, or you can directly use the document master records in task lists and inspection plans as a PRT. The interfaces and functions in document management enable direct access to drawings and other documents. The representation of test equipment in document records or the inclusion of docu- ment records in the other types of PRTs makes it possible to use test equipment in terms of documents (e.g., drawings, descriptions, etc.). This method is also used primar- ily for planning and documentation of test equipment usage. It’s characterized by spe- cial document management functions. Due to the many alternatives for representing test equipment in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem, we suggest that you evaluate every option very carefully on the requirements that test equipment management should satisfy. 7.3 Configuration Basics In this section, we’ll cover the minimal configuration steps that you need to integrate QM with test equipment in PM. Apart from the QM configuration steps that you have to perform separately at various levels, these configuration steps will help you if you need to generate QM inspection lots while creating and releasing PM orders. For this, the first configuration step is to assign the inspection type with the PM inspec- tion origin. Each piece of test equipment also has a unique serial number that you use to identify one from another, and you can maintain control of a piece of equipment’s serial number usage and identification in business processes. If your business process requires the system to create an inspection lot for a functional location, then you need to perform only the first configuration step. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 328
sections.he:
ניתן להשתמש ב-PRT master record להפניה לנתוני מסמך, או ישירות ב-document master records ב-task lists כ-PRT. הממשקים ב-document management מאפשרים גישה לשרטוטים ומסמכים. מתאים לתכנון ותיעוד שימוש בציוד. בשל החלופות הרבות, העריכו כל אפשרות בזהירות.

**7.3 יסודות תצורה:** ליצירת QM inspection lots ביצירת/שחרור הזמנות PM. הצעד הראשון — הקצאת inspection type ל-PM inspection origin. לכל ציוד serial number ייחודי. אם נדרש lot ל-functional location — רק הצעד הראשון.

sections.title: Inspection Type Assignment to PM Order Type
sections.en: 7.3.1 Inspection Type Assignment to PM Order Type To integrate QM with PM so that you can calibrate test equipment using a PM order, you need to assign inspection type 14 to the relevant PM order and plant combination. Inspection type 14 of inspection origin 14 (plant maintenance) is specific to handling QM’s integration with PM and is available as a standard offering in the SAP system. To assign any configured, specific inspection type of inspection origin 14, use standard inspection type 14 via menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Define Inspections in Plant Maintenance (see Figure 7.2). In this example, we used the plant 1710 and calibration order YBA2 combination, to which you assign inspection type 14. Save your settings. During the equipment calibra- tion process, when you create and then release a calibration order of order type YBA2 for plant 1710, the system will automatically create the necessary inspection lot. Figure 7.2 Assigning Inspection Type 14 to the Combination of Plant and Order Type
sections.he: לכיול דרך הזמנת PM, הקצו inspection type 14 לצירוף הזמנת PM+מפעל. ‏type 14 (origin 14, plant maintenance) ספציפי לאינטגרציה. ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Define Inspections in Plant Maintenance (Figure 7.2). בדוגמה, מפעל 1710 והזמנת כיול YBA2 — הקצו type 14. שמרו. בכיול, ביצירת/שחרור הזמנת YBA2 למפעל 1710, המערכת תיצור lot.

sections.title: Serial Number Profile
sections.en: 7.3.2 Serial Number Profile Each piece of test equipment can have a unique serial number that you can use to track its inventory, as well as its calibration history. You can also control how the system pro- cesses business transactions of equipment with a serial number by maintaining rele- vant settings in the serial number profile. To set up a serial number profile, use Transaction OIS2 or menu path SAP IMG  Plant Maintenance and Customer Service  Master Data in Management Plant Maintenance and Customer Service  Technical Objects  Serial Number Management  Define Serial Number Profiles. Figure 7.3 shows the initial screen for maintaining serial number profiles. You can either make changes to an existing serial number profile or create a new one. For this example, use profile 0001, and select the ExistReq. (existing requirement) checkbox, which ensures that the system checks whether a serial number is created and available before it allows you to create and test equipment. We’ll show you how these settings work when we cover the master data creation processes later in this chapter. Set StkCk (stock check) to 1 so that the system checks for consistency between the material stock and its serial number. Choose profile 0001 , and then choose Serializing procedures on the left side, and the screen in Figure 7.4 appears. © 329 7.3 Configuration Basics Figure 7.3 Serial Number Profile Figure 7.4 Serializing Procedure Figure 7.4 shows serial number profile 0001, which consists of various functions or pro- cedures to control business functions using serial numbers in logistics and inventory management functions. From goods issue and goods receipt to their use in production and sales functions, you can control a material’s serial number management from an 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 330 optional entry to determine whether each serial number should have a corresponding equipment number. For the business function or procedure QMSL, for inspection lot maintenance, set the serial number usage as mandatory (option 03), and an inspection lot for calibration equipment must also contain a serial number (option 02). You assign this serial num- ber profile 0001 to the material master of the equipment. This assignment then ensures that during business processes involving the test equipment, the system refers to the controls that you maintained in serial number profile 0001. Save your settings. That’s the entire configuration that you need to undertake. Let’s now delve into creat- ing the relevant test equipment master data, which will form the basis of running busi- ness processes and thereby integrating QM and PM.
sections.he:
לכל ציוד serial number ייחודי (מעקב מלאי והיסטוריית כיול). ב-serial number profile שולטים בעיבוד. ל-Transaction OIS2 או SAP IMG • Plant Maintenance and Customer Service • Master Data in Management Plant Maintenance and Customer Service • Technical Objects • Serial Number Management • Define Serial Number Profiles (Figure 7.3). בדוגמה, profile 0001. סמנו ExistReq. (בדיקה ש-serial number קיים לפני יצירת ציוד). קבעו StkCk "1" (עקביות בין מלאי ל-serial number). בחרו 0001, ‏Serializing procedures (Figure 7.4).
ה-profile 0001 מכיל פונקציות לבקרת serial numbers (מ-GI/GR ועד ייצור ומכירה). לפונקציה QMSL (inspection lot maintenance), קבעו שימוש ב-serial number כחובה (option 03), ושה-lot לכיול חייב serial number (option 02). הקצו את profile 0001 לאב החומר של הציוד. שמרו.

sections.title: Test Equipment Master Data
sections.en: 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data In the following sections, we’ll discuss how to create important master data in MM, PM, and QM, while also touching on the integration aspects among them. This master data will then be subsequently used in business processes or in transactional data.
sections.he: להלן נתוני אב ב-MM, ‏PM, ‏QM, והאינטגרציה ביניהם.

sections.title: Create Material Master
sections.en: 7.4.1 Create Material Master To create the material master for the test equipment, which is a PRT, use Transaction MM01 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Test Equipment Management  Test Equipment  Material  Create. On the initial screen that appears, choose Industry Type Mechanical and Material Type FHMI Prod. Resources/tools, and then select at least the following views:  Basic Data 1  Purchasing  Prod.resources/tools  Plant data / stor. 1  Plant data / stor. 2  Quality Management  Accounting 1 In the Organization Area, choose Plant 1710 and Storage Location 0001, and then choose Continue. In the Basic Data view tab, maintain the Description, which in this example is “Lab Test Equipment”; the Base Unit of Measure as PC; and the Material Group as 001. If you’re going to procure this calibration equipment, then you need to maintain the relevant © 331 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data entries in the Purchasing view tab of the material master (QM/MM integration was dis- cussed in Chapter 4). Figure 7.5 shows that the previously configured serial number pro- file 0001 is assigned to the material master. Doing so makes it possible to use serial number assignment differently in the various SAP areas (e.g., for finished products and test equipment). The serial number profile here is set especially for test equipment monitoring. In addition, for the field SerLevel, enter “1” to enable the system to syn- chronize equipment number assignment with its serial number. Figure 7.5 Serial Number Profile 0001 Assignment in Material Master Figure 7.6 shows the Prod.resources/tools view tab. This is where you enter the task list usage “009” (all task list types) because you want to include the test equipment in your inspection plans and task lists. Other information that you enter on this screen has direct implications on PRT planning and its availability. Selecting any of the check- boxes makes that specific field a reference field, and you won’t be allowed to make changes in business transactions. Save your entries. Creating these views means the setup for the material master for test equipment is complete. In this example, the system assigns Material 2231 for Plant 1710 for the test equipment (Descr.) Lab Test Equipment. After creating the material master for calibration equipment, the next step is to main- tain its serial number. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 332 Figure 7.6 PRT View of Material Master

Resources/tools), ולפחות התצוגות: ‏Basic Data 1, ‏Purchasing, ‏Prod.resources/tools, ‏Plant data/stor. 1, ‏Plant data/stor. 2, ‏Quality Management, ‏Accounting 1. ב-Organization, ‏Plant 1710, ‏Storage Location 0001, ‏Continue.

Figure 7.6 — תצוגת Prod.resources/tools. הזינו task list usage "009" (כל הסוגים) לכלילת הציוד ב-plans. סימון תיבה הופך לשדה reference (לא ניתן לשינוי). שמרו. בדוגמה, המערכת מקצה Material 2231 למפעל 1710 (Lab Test Equipment).

sections.title: Material Serial Number
sections.en: 7.4.2 Material Serial Number To maintain the serial number of the just created material 2231 (which is the test equip- ment), use Transaction IQ01 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Serial Numbers  Create. On the initial screen that appears, enter material number “2231” in the Material field. If you want to assign a spe- cific serial number to the material because the test equipment already has a serial num- ber, enter it in the appropriate field. If you leave this field empty, the system automatically assigns the next highest number. Finally, you must also enter “Q” in the Type field to denote that the equipment is test/measurement equipment. Press (Enter), and the system displays the detailed view for the serial number, as shown in Figure 7.7. In various available tabs, either the system automatically copies the infor- mation from material 2231, such as in the ConstType (construction type) field (not shown), or you can maintain the values, such as for the work center. The system assigns serial number 10002974 to material 2231. Tips and Tricks Using the classification system, you can supplement master data, such as equipment, material, functional location, and so on, with any fields required for the process flow. These fields are then available in numerous standard evaluations. During characteris- tics creation, you can control the permissible values, the input format, and the type of field (e.g., mandatory or optional entry field). © 333 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data Figure 7.7 Serial Number Creation with Material Number

sections.title: Test Equipment and Serial Number Synchronization
sections.en: 7.4.3 Test Equipment and Serial Number Synchronization While maintaining the serial number of a material, you can create the same material as a piece of equipment. To do so, choose Activate Equipment View, and the screen in Figure 7.8 appears that shows a three-way combination among material 2231, serial number 10002974, and equipment 10002974. Maintain the stock-relevant information of equipment 10002974, such as stock type 01 (for unrestricted stock), plant 1710, and storage location 0001. Maintaining this information will help the inventory manager know where it belongs in the store and be able to quickly place the equipment upon receiving it for maintenance. Tips and Tricks When you place the cursor in the Stock type field, the system doesn’t bring up a dropdown menu for you to choose the relevant stock type, such as unrestricted or quality inspection. To enter the code that meets your business needs, place the cur- sor in the Stock type field, and press (F1). In the help that appears, the system dis- plays the relevant stock types, together with their codes, which you can then use in this field (Stock type). 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 334 Figure 7.8 Equipment Number Synchronization with Serial Number You get to the Status submenu by choosing the blue i button (at the end of the Status field). The system displays the permitted status values on the right side of the selection menu. You can configure the statuses to meet your business requirements. Some pos- sible status values include the following:  0001: Test equipment is in storage.  0002: Test equipment is being used.  0004: Test equipment is in repair.  0005: Test equipment is at a contractor location. Save your entries, and the system creates a material’s serial number, which also syn- chronizes with the test equipment number.

sections.title: Test Equipment
sections.en: 7.4.4 Test Equipment To view test equipment with the corresponding serial number, you can also use Trans- action IE02 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Test Equipment Manage- ment  Test Equipment  Equipment  Change. On the screen that appears, enter equipment “10002974”, which is the same as serial number 10002974; press (Enter); and the screen in Figure 7.9 appears. © 335 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data Figure 7.9 Organization View of Equipment Here, you can then fill out the details in the Organization tab. In the Account assign- ment area, you can enter the cost center that the system then books the cost to, and do so for internal activity allocation for the test equipment. With the appropriate configu- ration settings in place, the time it takes to calibrate the test equipment can be billed to this cost center through PM order management. In the Responsibilities area, enter the Planning Plant, Planner Group, and the responsible work center (Main WorkCtr). These entries correspond to the entries that you already know from Chapter 2. Tips and Tricks To bring about significant business process improvement, you can integrate classifica- tions with test equipment. Choose Class overview, shown in Figure 7.9, and the system brings up the classification view, in which you maintain the previously created class of class type 002 (equipment class) and its characteristics. Choose the SerData (serial data) tab that is available at the right side of Figure 7.9, and the screen in Figure 7.10 appears. This screen shows the three-way combination and data synchronization among Material 2231, Serial Number 10002974, and the Equip- ment 10002974. When you routinely calibrate this equipment, you can view its calibra- tion history by choosing History. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 336 Figure 7.10 Material, Equipment, and Serial Number Synchronization Tips and Tricks Depending on how deeply you want to go to integrate equipment calibration of PM with QM, you can also integrate Measuring Points/Counters for test equipment. A measuring point is the identifier that you use to measure a piece of equipment’s char- acteristic. This identifier can be, for example, a sensory test, and it maintains its value at 100. So, after every 100 sensory tests, the sensory test equipment is due for calibra- tion. With measuring documents, you maintain the actual number of sensory tests that this equipment performed. A sensory test is one of the tests (others are aroma and taste) found often in the food industry to measure consumers’ reaction to under- development or under-trial products. Measuring points also use classification.

sections.title: General Task List
sections.en: 7.4.5 General Task List The SAP S/4HANA system provides two tools for planning test equipment monitoring. First, it provides the maintenance plan that specifies when and how frequently you should calibrate test equipment. Second, it provides the general task list that specifies what tasks to perform during calibration. © 337 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data You need to assign a unique maintenance plan and general task list to every piece of test equipment. Theoretically, you can assign a common maintenance plan to several pieces of equipment if they all have exactly the same maintenance date. In this exam- ple, however, we create a separate maintenance plan for every piece of equipment. In the same way, you can assign separate general task lists to every piece of equipment. In this example, we create a shared task list named equipment calibration tasks. You first need to create a general task list. This is a type of routing that business users use to perform maintenance and calibration tasks. In some places in the SAP S/4HANA system, the term task list or PM task list is used. In this section, we provide only limited information on the required entries. You can create operations for the individual work steps, assign workstations and PRTs to the operations, schedule setup times and work times, and enter corresponding costs. Assume that one general task list suffices for all equipment, which you can then assign to all maintenance plans from the very beginning. Also assume that there is only one central calibration point with one workstation. Costs are entered at a flat rate through cost center accounting and aren’t dependent on calibration duration. This configura- tion provides you with a relatively easy-to-implement scenario, which you can still enhance and adapt to changing requirements at any time after a productive start. To create a general task list, use Transaction IA05 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Test Equipment Management  Calibration Planning  Maintenance Task List  General Task List  Create. On the initial screen, you don’t have to enter any infor- mation. The system automatically assigns a group number and a group counter. In this example, it’s group 40, and the group counter is 1. You can also assign an external group number if there is any such business need. Similarly, you can enter a key date if you want the task list to be effective from any specific date. If you don’t enter any date, the system incorporates the date of general task list creation as the key date (or effec- tive date). Press (Enter), and the screen in Figure 7.11 appears, which is the header of the general task list. Enter the task list name “Equipment Calibration Tasks” and fill out the other manda- tory fields, such as Overall Status as 4 (Released) and Usage also as 4 (Plant Mainte- nance). You can also assign a maintenance strategy that applies to all the equipment to which this task list is assigned. Any information that you enter on this screen applies to the entire task list. For example, entering Work Center “RES-0100” and Plant “1710” automatically copies to all operations of the task list. In the QM Data area, assign Inspection Points as 300, as the system will refer to it during results recording for inspection lot. The next step is to create operations (or steps) for the general task list. Choose Operation, and the screen in Figure 7.12 appears. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 338 Figure 7.11 Header View of General Task List Figure 7.12 consists of three operations for the test equipment’s calibration as a work- station, which is work center RES-0100. Two different control keys set here are PM01 and QM04. You can use these control keys to control special functions, such as confir- mations of operations. Figure 7.12 Operation Overview of General Task List © 339 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data Note Refer to Chapter 2, in which we extensively covered the configuration details of control keys and how you can use them to control various business functions, including adher- ing to the operations sequence during confirmation so that the system doesn’t allow an operation’s confirmation until you record inspection results of that operation (in this case, 0020). In Figure 7.12, you can assign components that may be consumables or spare parts you’ll need for equipment maintenance. Whenever you use this general task list for equipment maintenance, the system automatically proposes the components you need for equipment maintenance and which you can issue out from the warehouse. Tips and Tricks You can integrate Document Management System (DMS) for specific operations of a general task list. Visual instructions help the equipment maintenance or calibration engineer have access to relevant drawings or specifications that are needed to perform equipment calibration tasks. Chapter 20 covers DMS. Choose Activity 0010, and then choose Master Ins. (master inspection characteristic) to assign inspection characteristics to specific operations of the task list (see Figure 7.13). Here, you see the operation view in which you can assign the master inspection charac- teristics and their values, which then become available during results recording. For our example, enter a quantitative master inspection characteristic with the short text “Color rays” and with upper and lower limits. Notice that the system offers the options to maintain comprehensive QM data here. Save your entries. After saving the general task list, you can create the maintenance plan for the individ- ual test equipment. Figure 7.13 Inspection Characteristics Assignment in General Task List 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 340 Tips and Tricks If you need to create a task list that is specific to a piece of equipment, then you can use Transaction IA01 to create an equipment task list. The principles and fundamentals that apply to general task lists also apply to equipment task lists, with the difference that an equipment task list is specific to individual pieces of equipment only.

sections.title: Maintenance Plan
sections.en: 7.4.6 Maintenance Plan The purpose of a maintenance plan is to plan maintenance deadlines and cycles for cal- ibration. Although this example uses time-dependent planning, the system also sup- ports activity-specific planning (e.g., calibration after 300 uses) or a combination of both (e.g., check after every three months or 300 uses). In addition, you can assign order specifications or maintenance strategies. The type of activity is defined using a reference in the maintenance plan to the corresponding task list. A prerequisite for cre- ating the maintenance plan is that you’ve already created the test equipment that you want to calibrate with this maintenance plan, as well as the corresponding general task list. To create a maintenance plan, use Transaction IP41 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Calibration Planning  Maintenance Planning  Maintenance Plan  Cre- ate Single Cycle Plan. On the screen that appears, for Maintenance Plan Category, choose Maintenance Order. This means that you want the system to create the PM order (the calibration order) each time the test equipment’s calibration is due. Other options available are inspection lot creation for stability study, physical samples, PM notification, and even service orders for the services that the supplier provides. In the Maintenance plan cycle tab, enter the cycle (frequency) of the calibration inter- val. This value denotes the frequency with which you need to conduct equipment cali- bration. Typical values can be three months, six months, or one year. In the screen in Figure 7.14, enter “365 DAY”. Scroll down so that the screen in Figure 7.15 appears. In the Reference object area of Figure 7.15, enter the serial and material numbers for the test equipment in the respective fields. Then, fill out the Task List area with the infor- mation shown. This is where you create the link between this maintenance plan and the general task list. If you know the task list type, plan group number, and plan group counter for your general task list, then you can enter them directly in the respective fields. Otherwise, you can search for the general task list using the binoculars icon in the application toolbar and copy the data. In this case, look at Task List Typ A (task list). You’ve already entered task list type A (general), so enter “40” in Task LstGrp. If you entered the data completely and correctly in the equipment and if the necessary settings are in place, the system automatically copies the available data to the Planning Data area, and you don’t have to make any more entries. However, we suggest that you pay special attention to the information in the Planning Data area, such as whether the © 341 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data right order type (YBA2 in this example) is there. When the system creates a mainte- nance call object, it refers to the information that you maintain here. Similarly, if you set the Do Not Rel. (release) Immediately indicator, the system doesn’t release the cali- bration order on its creation. Putting this control in place can help business users if there is a need to evaluate the system-created calibration orders before releasing them for further processing or action. Figure 7.14 Maintenance Plan Figure 7.15 Planning Details in Maintenance Plan 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 342 Lastly, you need to set the scheduling parameters. Refer to the Maintenance plan scheduling parameters tab in the maintenance plan header (see Figure 7.16). Figure 7.16 Scheduling Parameters of the Maintenance Plan You can change the testing schedule of maintenance planning. This may be the case when there is a need to change the testing frequency of calibration equipment. You can also use this option to enter any missing or incomplete information in the mainte- nance plan. Tips and Tricks You can also use Transaction IP02 to directly make changes to the maintenance plan. Enter maintenance plan “151” on the initial screen, and press (Enter), and you’re taken to the screen in Figure 7.16. Figure 7.16 shows the screen where you can define when the system should include test equipment requiring calibration in the worklist and when the next cycle for calibration should start again. For example, the worklist can contain upcoming calibrations that are due four weeks before the deadline. A call horizon, defined as a percentage, enables the business process owner to control when the system creates a call object on its planned or due date. For example, a 0% call horizon means that as soon as the planned or due date of the call object (which, in this case, is a calibration order) occurs, the system immediately creates the calibration order. Similarly, a 90% call horizon means the system will call the object on a time horizon of 90% from the date of the next planned inspection lot creation. Other available options are how the system should respond when there are deviations between planned and actual tasks. You can define not only the tolerance for early or late completion in © 343 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data percentages, but also how much (as a percentage) the system should shift in dates when it finds deviations between planned and actual tasks. Save your entries, and the system creates maintenance plan 151. Note For the example in Figure 7.16, Scheduling period is set to one day. In a real-life busi- ness scenario, you need to evaluate how frequently, such as monthly or after every six months, the system should schedule and then create calibration orders for equipment.

sections.title: Schedule Maintenance Plan
sections.en: 7.4.7 Schedule Maintenance Plan To start automatic monitoring of calibration deadlines, scheduling must begin after you create test equipment and its maintenance plan. To schedule a maintenance plan, use Transaction IP10 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Calibration Plan- ning  Maintenance Planning  Maintenance Plan  Scheduling. On the initial screen, enter maintenance plan “151”, which you created in the previous step, and press (Enter), and the screen in Figure 7.17 appears. Choose the Start button, and the system opens a pop-up that defines the date from which you want the system to schedule the maintenance plan. Choose Yes to confirm the start of maintenance plan scheduling, and then enter the date for the system to start the planning cycle. Figure 7.18 shows the log of scheduled or manual calls made for a specific maintenance plan. Figure 7.17 Scheduling Maintenance Plan 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 344 Figure 7.18 Log of Scheduled or Manual Calls for Maintenance Plan Tips and Tricks To check and test whether the system will indeed create a calibration order per the testing schedule, choose the Manual call button shown in Figure 7.17 to prompt the system to manually trigger calibration order creation. When the system asks for the date (in a Manual Call popup), enter today’s date. Save your entries, and check for the newly created calibration order using Transaction IW33, which should have the latest/ last created calibration order number. We’ve put this manual call option to use, which you’ll see in Section 7.5.1.

sections.title: Deadline Monitoring
sections.en: 7.4.8 Deadline Monitoring For deadline monitoring of maintenance plans, you need to manually trigger schedul- ing monitoring in the system. Maintenance plans apply to calibration orders, as well as to other objects in which they integrate with PM; the details that we cover here remain the same. To set up deadline monitoring for a maintenance plan, use Transaction IP30 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Calibration Planning  Maintenance Planning  Maintenance Plan  Deadline Monitoring. Figure 7.19 shows the initial screen where you can enter an individual maintenance plan or a complete range of it. For this example, enter Maintenance Plan as “151”, and choose Execute (not shown; located on the bottom-right side of the screen), and the screen in Figure 7.20 appears. This screen shows a deadline monitoring log that confirms successful scheduling of maintenance plan 151. © 345 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data Figure 7.19 Deadline Monitoring for Maintenance Plans Figure 7.20 Log of Maintenance Plan Deadline Monitoring Tips and Tricks In practice, it has proven beneficial to schedule a periodic batch program that can start scheduling monitoring once a week or once every two weeks, for example, and the sys- tem can generate the maintenance orders for all the test equipment that you want to calibrate. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 346

sections.title: Business Processes in Test Equipment Management
sections.en: 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management The example in this chapter stipulates that the system automatically create a calibra- tion order of order type YBA2, according to maintenance plan 151. Further, the neces- sary configuration settings will also ensure that the system automatically creates an inspection lot of inspection type 14 on release and on saving the calibration order. Before we get into that process, we’ll also cover the business scenario in which a busi- ness user needs to inform the maintenance personnel of faulty or defective test equip- ment. Figure 7.21 shows that a business user can also create a maintenance request (a PM noti- fication in the system by using Transaction IW26) to communicate the need to perform equipment calibration. The business user may also create a PM notification due to equipment malfunction by using Transaction IW24. All of these scenarios apply when there is an actual and practical need to calibrate the test equipment instead of waiting for the system to create calibration orders according to the maintenance plan. Figure 7.21 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management The maintenance planner can evaluate the PM notification to see if there is a need to convert it to a PM order. If so, the maintenance planner can use the PM order creation option available right in the PM notification creation screen. Alternately, using Trans- action IW34 enables the maintenance planner to reference the PM notification while creating a PM order, which is basically converting a PM notification into a PM order. On release and on saving the PM order, the system automatically creates the QM inspec- tion lot of inspection type 14. Maintenance engineers can then approach the ware- house to issue the components or spare parts required for equipment maintenance. The next quality steps entail recording results and making a usage decision. If PM is to further integrate with QM, then the business user can perform confirmation of opera- tions (tasks) performed with Transaction IW31. Finally, the business process ends with completion of the PM order—both technical and business completion. Note There is a great similarity of functions and functionality between PM notification cre- ation and that of QM notification. If there’s a business need to create a PM notification before converting it into a PM order, then refer to Chapter 12 on quality notification. Let’s detail our example in the following sections. PM notification PM order (calibration order) Components goods issuance QM inspection lot (Insp. type 14) Results recording and usage decision PM order confirmation PM order completion © 347 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management

sections.en: 7.5.1 Calibration Order Via Transaction IW33, Figure 7.22 shows display calibration order 4000840 for equip- ment 10002974. The system denotes the released status of the PM order with REL. Further, the sys- tem also automatically creates an inspection lot for this PM order and denotes it with the status ILAS. Notice that the system also automati- cally incorporates the general task list of task list type A (general), group 40, and group counter 1. This is consistent with the settings that you previously made in Figure 7.14. Figure 7.23 Calibration Plan Triggered by Maintenance Plan

sections.title: Results Recording
sections.en: 7.5.3 Results Recording The advantage of entering results and a usage decision in the SAP S/4HANA system is that this provides complete information visibility for the inspection in the same sys- tem. If you’ve made the necessary settings in the system, you can skip one or both activities of results recording or usage decision. This makes it possible to proceed directly from order release and inspection to inspection completion. Figure 7.25 Inspection Specifications of Inspection Lot 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 350 Figure 7.25 shows the Inspection Specifications tab of inspection lot 140000000000. The system assigns the general task Group 40, with Group Counter 1, which you had previously created. Figure 7.26 shows Inspection Lot 140000000000 and for the inspection point, which in this case is equipment 10002974 for calibration order 4000840. Figure 7.26 Results Recording of Inspection Lot Note With the PM order and its associated results recording and usage decision, you can print a calibration label that contains the equipment calibration details.

sections.title: Calibration Orders Worklist
sections.en: 7.5.4 Calibration Orders Worklist The order list contains all the test equipment used for calibration. The list is filled auto- matically by the periodic batch program for scheduling monitoring. The list is pro- cessed manually. To bring up the calibration orders worklist, use Transaction IW38 or menu path Quality Management  Test Equipment Management  Calibration Inspec- tion  Order  Order List  Change Data. On the screen that appears, select the Order Sta- tus Outstanding checkbox because all new inspection orders start with the outstanding status. In the Order Type field, enter “YBA2” (for Calibration Orders) because you want to select only orders that are due for calibration. © 351 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management To start calibrating the test equipment, you first need to select the required line and release the order using the Release Order function. This creates an inspection lot with all the data required for calibration inspection. At the same time, the status of the order is changed to In Process. You can also automate this manual release step with the right configuration settings.

sections.title: Calibration Orders Completion
sections.en: 7.5.5 Calibration Orders Completion As soon as calibration of the test equipment is complete, you select all the pieces of test equipment that have the status In Process. Referring once again to the list that you cre- ated using Transaction IW38 (Section 7.5.4), you use menu path Order  Functions  Com- plete (Technically) to inform the system that you’ve completed calibration of the selected test equipment. To fully complete the calibration order, however, you also need to complete it in business terms through menu path Order  Functions  Complete (Business). Now the calibration order is fully completed for the SAP system, and the next planning cycle starts. Tips and Tricks If the calibration operation takes a longer (e.g., after being sent to an external calibra- tion station), you must remember to also set the user status accordingly in the equip- ment view of the serialized material. Don’t confuse the status of the PM order with the user status of the equipment.

sections.title: Evaluations
sections.en: 7.5.6 Evaluations As in in all applications, real-time reports and standard or flexible analyses are avail- able for test equipment management. There can be any number of required evalua- tions: for example, total number of pieces of test equipment; where-used lists for test equipment for specific departments, individuals, or warehouses; calibration costs; number of calibration orders; and reported errors. With the results history, you can dis- play changes to specific characteristics of a piece of test equipment across defined peri- ods. You can also display these changes in a run chart. You can use the evaluation options for the standard configuration of the SAP S/4HANA system to cover most business requirements. Consider the cost-center-specific usage list. This may be of interest to managers who want to identify test equipment in certain locations within their own cost centers. If you want to identify the location of specific test equipment within your own cost center, start with Transaction IQ09 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Serial Numbers  List  Display. The system dis- plays a list selection screen for serial number selection (the same as in other applica- tions), in which you can select according to many criteria. In this example, you want to 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 352 select test equipment within the cost center, so you fill out the Plant, Maintenance Plant, and Cost Center fields with the required values. Although Plant and Maintenance Plant aren’t mandatory fields, restricting the search scope (in this case to the plant) when dealing with large data stocks and several locations can significantly reduce the search time. Note See Chapter 18 for evaluation and reporting in the SAP S/4HANA system.

sections.title: Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916
sections.en: 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 While the PM-QM integration has generally been used as a workaround to manage rou- tine or periodic inspections of technical objects (equipment or functional locations), SAP has introduced the inspection checklist functionality to process this critical main- tenance process of results recording in the system in the form of a checklist. Depending on the configuration settings, the system can even trigger follow-on activities, such as creating notifications for prompt and timely maintenance. Inspection checklist is again a PM-QM integration process, and SAP has introduced a new inspection type, 8914, as well. Further, standard configuration is already predeliv- ered that can either be used right away or can be used as a reference to create different checklists. Apart from results recording and usage decisions undertaken by the maintenance team, another alternate is using the mobile solution from SAP called SAP Service and Asset Manager, which is intuitive and more user friendly than using the SAP Fiori and SAP GUI options available in the SAP S/4HANA system. The following sections cover the configuration and other prerequisites that need to be in place for an inspection list, followed by setting up the required master data. This is then followed by discussing the end-to-end business process of the automatic creation of an inspection checklist when a maintenance order is released.

sections.title: Configuration Basics and Other Prerequisites
sections.en: 7.6.1 Configuration Basics and Other Prerequisites We’ll need to first activate a business function followed by assigning two business roles to the business user so that the necessary option to configure and implement inspec- tion checklists is available, as follows: 1. Activate the business function LOG_EAM_CHECKLIST using Transaction SFW5. 2. Assign the business roles SAP_BR_MAINTENANCE_PLANNER and SAP_BR_QUALITY_PLANNER to your business user. 3. To check or make changes to the already available plant-order type combination for the inspection checklist, use menu path SAP IMG  Plant Maintenance and Customer © 353 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 Service  Maintenance and Service Processing  Maintenance and Service Orders  Functions and Settings for Order Types  Configure Checklists for Maintenance Order Types. 4. Figure 7.27 shows the Plant 1710 and Order Type PM07 combination in which the Inspection Type 8914 is assigned. Be sure to select all checkboxes so that the system is able to automatically generate a checklist on order release, which we’ll show later in this section. You can use already-delivered and available order type PM07 and associated configuration settings or create new entries, if deemed necessary. For this example, we’ll use the already-available configuration settings of order type PM07 and plant 1710. The lower half of the screen shows DMS, which we cover in detail in Chapter 20, while the quality notification is discussed in Chapter 12. After reading these chapters, you can come back to this section to see if any configuration settings need to be maintained or changed for DMS or quality notifications. 5. Be sure to check if the inspection type 8914 is assigned to the PM order type PM07 via menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Define Inspections in Plant Maintenance. Figure 7.27 Order Type PM07 for Checklists 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 354 This brings an end to the minimal configurations that either need to be in place or to be checked so that we can proceed further with setting up the relevant master data for checklist. We’ll use the same master data of material master and equipment master that we’ve used in the previous sections of this chapter, that is, material 2231 and equip- ment 10002975.

1. הפעילו את ה-business function LOG_EAM_CHECKLIST ב-Transaction SFW5.
2. הקצו roles SAP_BR_MAINTENANCE_PLANNER ו-SAP_BR_QUALITY_PLANNER למשתמש.
3. לבדיקת/שינוי צירוף plant-order type ל-checklist: SAP IMG • Plant Maintenance and Customer Service • Maintenance and Service Processing • Maintenance and Service Orders • Functions and Settings for Order Types • Configure Checklists for Maintenance Order Types.
4. Figure 7.27 — צירוף Plant 1710 ו-Order Type PM07 עם Inspection Type 8914. סמנו את כל התיבות (יצירה אוטומטית בשחרור). ניתן PM07 המסופק או חדש. החצי התחתון — DMS (פרק 20) ו-quality notification (פרק 12).
5. ודאו ש-type 8914 מוקצה ל-PM07: SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Define Inspections in Plant Maintenance.

sections.title: Setting Up the Master Data for Inspection Checklist
sections.en: 7.6.2 Setting Up the Master Data for Inspection Checklist Follow this step-by-step approach to maintain master data for inspection checklist: 1. To be able to match inspection plans (inspection checklist templates) with the check- list type field in a maintenance order’s operation, create a new characteristic using Transaction CT04. Enter Characteristic “CL_TYPE”, and choose the Create icon. Be sure to select Multiple Values in the Basic data tab. Then, in the Addnl data tab, enter Table Name “AFVC” and Field Name “CL_TYPE” (see Figure 7.28). 2. Next open the Values tab, choose Other Value Check, and select Check Table. In the popup that appears, enter Table Name “EAM_CL_CU_TYPE” containing allowed checklist types, which we’ll maintain later on. 3. In the Restriction tab, maintain an entry “0018” to restrict this characteristic to the task list class only. Figure 7.28 Characteristics with Table Reference 4. The next step is to define the matching of characteristics between the inspection plan and technical object (equipment or functional location) using the new Transac- tion IW98. Refer to Figure 7.29, and then in the Edit mode, create a new entry of the previously created characteristic name “CL_TYPE” in the table under Characteristic of Inspection Plan and value “EAM_CL_TYPE” under Characteristic of Technical Object. Value EAM_CL_TYPE indicates the characteristic that must match with the checklist type field in the maintenance order operation for checklist generation. © 355 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 Figure 7.29 Matching the Characteristic of an Inspection Plan with the Characteristic of a Technical Object 5. To classify the technical objects (equipment/functional location) that are relevant for inspection checklists, use Transactions IE (for equipment) or IL02 (for functional location). Choose the Class overview from the top menu bar in Figure 7.30 1, and enter the class already created in the system for the checklists. It can be an empty class without characteristics, but its name has to match the name of the class that we’ll create for the inspection plan in the next step. For this example, we first created a class named GASBOILER of Class Type 002 (equipment) and assigned it to Equip- ment 10002975 2. Figure 7.30 Assigning Classification in a Technical Object (Equipment) 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 356 6. We now define the applicable checklist types using Transaction IW99. For this exam- ple, create a new checklist type CL01ME, as shown in Figure 7.31. Then, select this checklist type, and double-click Short Texts in the Dialog Structure to maintain the description of this checklist in different languages. Checklist types can also be deleted when they aren’t used in any task list operation or order operation. But if a checklist type isn’t use, then you can mark it as Inactive to deactivate the usage of this checklist type. No inspection plan search is executed for inactive entries, and users get a warning if they use inactive checklist types in operations. Figure 7.31 Defining Checklist Types 7. Inspection checklists are created for certain maintenance order operations in the task list in the PM component. Use Transaction IA06 to create a general task list, and assign the type of checklist at the operation level in new field Checklist Type at the far right of the General Operation Overview table (see Figure 7.32). For this example— general task list 41 with group counter 1 and description Boiler Inspection—we assign Checklist Type “CL01ME” to Act. 0010. Figure 7.32 General Task List © 357 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 8. For QM master data, be sure to assign inspection type 8914 to material master 2231. 9. Using Transaction CL01, create a class of class type 018 (task list class) with the same name as the one for the technical object (of class type 002). For this example, we created the class GASBOILER of class type 018. This class is used to match the class name of the technical object, that is, equipment or functional location. The CL_ TYPE specific classification characteristic for the inspection plan matches with maintenance order operation field Checklist type. All of these matches were already ensured in Figure 7.29. 10. Create a quality inspection plan that is used as a template for generation of inspec- tion checklists, that is, quality inspection lots assigned to the maintenance work order operation and technical object. An inspection plan must have a reference to a material master and a class. Use Transaction QP02 to change the inspection plan of material 2231, and then, at the header level, navigate to Extras  Classification  Header, as shown in Figure 7.33. The screen shown in Figure 7.34 will appear. Figure 7.33 Classification in an Inspection Plan Task List 11. In Figure 7.34, assign the class GASBOILER of Class Type 018. Then, in the lower half of the screen, add a value to the characteristic checklist type to match the checklist type of the operation, which in this example is the checklist type “CL01ME”. Addi- tionally, notice that the task list type is Q (which is for quality inspection), with Group as 5, and the Group Counter is 1. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 358 Figure 7.34 Classification in an Inspection Plan This brings an end to setting up the PM-QM master data required to create an inspec- tion checklist. Let’s now discuss the associated business process.
sections.he:
הצעדים:
1. ליצירת מאפיין להתאמת plans (templates) לשדה checklist type בפעולת הזמנה: Transaction CT04. הזינו Characteristic "CL_TYPE", ‏Create. סמנו Multiple Values (Basic data). בלשונית Addnl data, ‏Table Name "AFVC", ‏Field Name "CL_TYPE" (Figure 7.28).
2. בלשונית Values, ‏Other Value Check, ‏Check Table. הזינו Table Name "EAM_CL_CU_TYPE" (סוגי ה-checklist המותרים).
3. בלשונית Restriction, ‏"0018" (להגביל ל-task list class).
4. להגדרת ההתאמה בין ה-plan לאובייקט הטכני: Transaction IW98 (Figure 7.29). במצב עריכה, צרו "CL_TYPE" תחת Characteristic of Inspection Plan ו-"EAM_CL_TYPE" תחת Characteristic of Technical Object (חייב להתאים ל-checklist type בפעולה).
5. לסיווג האובייקטים הרלוונטיים: Transaction IE (ציוד) או IL02 (functional location). בחרו Class overview (Figure 7.30), הזינו class (יכול להיות ריק, אך שמו חייב להתאים ל-class של ה-plan). בדוגמה, ‏class GASBOILER (Class Type 002), מוקצה ל-Equipment 10002975.
6. להגדרת סוגי ה-checklist: Transaction IW99. בדוגמה, ‏checklist type CL01ME (Figure 7.31). בחרו אותו, לחיצה כפולה על Short Texts לתיאורים בשפות. ניתן למחוק (אם לא בשימוש) או לסמן Inactive.
7. ה-checklists נוצרים לפעולות מסוימות ב-task list. ‏Transaction IA06 ליצירת general task list, הקצו את ה-Checklist Type ברמת הפעולה (Figure 7.32). בדוגמה, ‏general task list 41, ‏group counter 1, ‏Boiler Inspection — הקצו Checklist Type "CL01ME" ל-Act. 0010.

10. ליצירת plan כ-template: ‏Transaction QP02 לשינוי plan של 2231; ברמת הכותרת, ‏Extras • Classification • Header (Figure 7.33 → Figure 7.34). ל-plan נדרשת הפניה לחומר ול-class.
11. ב-Figure 7.34, הקצו class GASBOILER (Class Type 018). בחצי התחתון, הוסיפו ערך ל-checklist type "CL01ME". task list type Q, ‏Group 5, ‏Group Counter 1.

sections.title: Business Process of Inspection Checklist
sections.en: 7.6.3 Business Process of Inspection Checklist Following is the step-by-step approach to run the business process of creating and then recording results of an inspection checklist: 1. Use Transaction IW31 to create a maintenance order. On the initial screen that appears, enter Order type “PM07”, Equipment “10002975”, and Planning plant “1710”. 2. On the main order screen that appears, maintain other information in the manda- tory fields, such as a short description of the order, main work center and its plant, and other associated details. © 359 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 3. From the top menu bar, choose Extra  Task List Selection  General Task List, and then choose task list 41. This is the same general task list we created earlier. You’ll first be prompted to delete any operations of the work center, and you can confirm this deletion. 4. The system will prompt with selecting the relevant task list (in this example, task list 41) and its associated operations that you’ll need to confirm. 5. Once the task list is selected, choose Release to release the order (see Figure 7.35 1). Figure 7.35 Plant Maintenance Order with Checklists 6. On releasing the maintenance order, the system will automatically create an inspec- tion lot, which is 890000000314 in this example 2. Further, quality inspection plan (task list type Q) 5 is assigned to this inspection lot, and the associated Equipment 10002975 is also shown. 7. Notice the option to not only activate the inspection lot is available but to also view results recorded for the inspection lot. 8. Access Figure 7.36 via Transaction QA03 to view the details of inspection lot 890000000314 and notice the Material 2231, Order 1002157, and Inspection Type 8914. Once the results are recorded, a usage decision can be made. 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 360 Figure 7.36 Inspection Lot Type 8914 As mentioned in the beginning of this section, apart from the regular process of results recording using Transaction QE01, SAP offers the SAP Service and Asset Manager app that can be installed on a laptop, tablet, and mobile devices to support the maintenance team in performing various business functions, including creating notification and orders, or even recording results in the inspection checklists (see Figure 7.37). Figure 7.37 SAP Service and Asset Manager App © 361 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 Finally, let’s briefly discuss Transaction IW97 to simulate the what-if analysis, that is, which inspection plans and inspection characteristics the system will create if the mas- ter data is setup correctly. Use Transaction IW97 or follow menu path Plant Mainte- nance  Maintenance Processing  Order  Inspection Processing (see Figure 7.38). sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 7.7 Summary This chapter covered the necessary configuration you need to integrate QM with PM in general and for test equipment calibration in particular. We walked you through the options for automatic calibration order creation through maintenance planning, as well as manual steps that business users can perform. We also covered test equipment and its integration with the material master and serial number. We also briefly dis- cussed the reporting and evaluation options that are available to you. Finally, we introduced the end-to-end setup of successfully creating an inspection checklist, which is a new functionality available in SAP S/4HANA. The next chapter covers integration between QM and embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in the SAP S/4HANA system. ©
sections.he: הפרק כיסה את התצורה לאינטגרציית QM עם PM ולכיול ציוד בדיקה. עברנו על יצירת הזמנת כיול אוטומטית דרך maintenance planning, וצעדים ידניים. כיסינו את ציוד הבדיקה ואינטגרציה עם אב החומר וה-serial number, ואת הדיווח. לבסוף, ה-inspection checklist (תכונה חדשה). הפרק הבא — אינטגרציה בין QM ל-embedded EWM.

sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.en: 8.1 Configuration Basics Objects created or configured in an SAP area are then assigned to master data, which is covered in the next section of this chapter. Standard solutions and configurations delivered by embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA are sufficient to independently config- ure, implement, and integrate QM with embedded EWM. Table 8.1 consists of various inspection types available in SAP S/4HANA that find greater usage in embedded EWM areas and into which you can integrate the QM area. Ensure that you assign and activate the relevant inspection types in the material mas- ter. Refer to Chapter 2, wherein the configuration details of an inspection type are dis- cussed in detail. CIF not required Master data Plant Shipping point Business partner Material Transaction data Inbound delivery Outbound delivery QRFC Master data Location Business partner Product Transaction data SAP EWM inbound delivery Outbound delivery order SAP S/4HANA core SAP EWM X © 365 8.1 Configuration Basics The following sections discuss the QM-specific configurations that need to be in place so that the configured objects are then assigned to the master data.

sections.title: Activate Inspection Object Type
sections.en: 8.1.1 Activate Inspection Object Type An inspection object type defines the following:  Business process for the inspection  Inspected object—for example, the product, the handling unit, or the delivery  Warehouse number Each inspection object type can have many inspection rules. Based on selection criteria (also known as properties), the inspection rule determines which objects to trigger an inspection for and specifies the inspection details—for example, the inspection pro- cess, the procedure, the inspection frequency, and usage decision codes, as well as their associated logistical functions. There are six inspection object types to cater to different business processes, as shown in Table 8.2. Inspection Type Inspection Plan Usage Inspection Type Description 17 9 Extended Warehouse Inspection (EWM) 1701 9 EWM: Goods receipt inspection for pur- chase order 1704 9 EWM: Goods receipt inspection from production 1708 9 EWM: Stock transfer inspection 1709 9 EWM: Recurring inspection of batches Table 8.1 Inspection Types in Embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA Inspection Object Type Description 1 Preliminary inspection – inbound delivery 2 Counting inbound deliveries 3 Quality inspection – return delivery 4 Quality inspection for product/batch – inbound delivery 5 Quality inspection for product/batch warehouse – internal 6 Preliminary inspection – handling unit Table 8.2 Inspection Object Types 8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management 366 Note Inspection object types 1 to 3 are still not available in embedded EWM with the SAP S/4HANA 2023 release but are expected to be available in future releases. When integrating with QM, you can define that the inspection setup data of the Quality Management view in the material master is used. An inspection rule is no longer required. In embedded EWM, the inspection types 01 (goods receipt inspection for pur- chase order), 04 (goods receipt inspection from production), 08 (stock transfer inspec- tion), and 09 (recurring inspection of batches) are supported. For sampling, the following is true:  When using the business process acceptance sampling, you specify the inspection type in the quality info record for the material.  When using the business process presampling in production, you specify the inspec- tion type in the Quality Management view of the material master. Note If you want to change your settings from inspections with inspection rules to inspec- tions without inspection rules, refer to SAP Note 2787302. You can use quality inspection without inspection rules in the following processes:  Acceptance sampling  Inspections after goods receipt  Presampling in production  Stock inspections  Recurring inspections To configure and define quality inspection without inspection rules, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Manage- ment  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Basics and Integration  Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent Activation of IOTs (Inspection Object Types). Here, you’ll find the following:  For Inspection Setup Origin, you specify that no inspection rule is used and that the inspection lot setup originates from the Quality Management tab of the material master.  Under Insp. Planning without Rules, you specify the inspection settings and the quality inspection process. © 367 8.1 Configuration Basics Let’s now discuss how to set up QM integration with embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA. You need to activate an inspection object type for a warehouse so it can be used. To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Management  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Basics and Integration  Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent Activation of IOTs. The screen that appears, as shown in Figure 8.2, shows the control functions that can be applied for the quality inspection process in embedded EWM. The last two options con- trol if the system should look for inspection rule setup in embedded EWM for quality inspection processes or in the material master of SAP S/4HANA. Figure 8.3 shows the options available for inspection planning without the rules. Figure 8.2 Inspection Object Type 8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management 368 Figure 8.3 Inspection Planning without Rules

sections.title: Maintain Inspection Object Types Version
sections.en: 8.1.2 Maintain Inspection Object Types Version Maintaining an inspection object type version in embedded EWM is one of the prereq- uisites for quality inspection processing. To maintain an inspection object type ver- sion, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Management  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Basics and Integration  Maintain Inspection Object Types Version. In Figure 8.4, select the checkboxes under the Activ. IOT (active inspection object) col- umn for relevant business processes. For example, inspection object type 4 will trigger quality inspection for incoming or inbound materials (goods receipt), whereas inspec- tion object type 5 will trigger quality inspection when one stock type moves to another (e.g., from unrestricted or blocked stock to quality stock). Figure 8.4 Inspection Type Object Version Figure 8.5 shows the detailed level of properties for inspection object type 4 and is a control function on the level of details an inspection rule needs to have. For example, if a country of origin doesn’t influence the quality inspection process in any way, then this field can be removed from the list so that it won’t appear while creating an inspec- tion rule for the material (or the warehouse product) in the warehouse. © 369 8.1 Configuration Basics Figure 8.5 Maintain Properties of Inspection Object Types

sections.title: Define and Assign Follow-Up Actions
sections.en: 8.1.3 Define and Assign Follow-Up Actions You can maintain follow-up actions for an inspection outcome—that is, while recoding the usage decision of an inspection lot. Follow-up actions are used for quality control or simply for informative purposes. To define follow-up actions, use menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Management  Cross Process Settings  Quality Management  Inspection Results  Maintain Follow-Up Actions  Define Follow-up Actions. Figure 8.6 shows the control functions of follow-up actions that can be applied to an inspection lot or to a usage decision by choosing the relevant option from the drop- down available under the FolUpAct column. Select the EWM_A follow-up function, and then choose Function Modules from the left side of the screen so that the screen in Figure 8.7 appears. Figure 8.6 Follow-Up Actions for Inspection Results 8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management 370 Figure 8.7 Details of Follow-Up Actions Figure 8.7 shows the standard function module that will trigger the embedded EWM logistical follow-up action we cover next. An existing or standard function module can be changed or a new one created and assigned to a usage decision to meet any specific business need. It’s best to engage an ABAP consultant for this task. Once the follow-up actions are defined, the next step is to assign embedded EWM logis- tical actions to the previously defined follow-up function. To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Management  Cross Process Settings  Quality Management  Inspection Results  Maintain Follow- Up Actions  Assign Logistical Follow-Up Actions. Figure 8.8 shows the detailed screen with entries for the previously defined FolUpAct “EWM_A” with IOT “4” for Warehouse No. “1710”. In Assign Logistical Follow-Up Actions, it’s possible to control how and where the stock moves when it’s assigned a specific follow-up logistical action. Figure 8.8 Logistical Follow-Up Actions © 371 8.1 Configuration Basics
