sections.title: Business Processes
sections.en: 9.9.3 Business Processes The business processes in WIP batches entail creating a process order, which is followed by confirmation, in which the WIP batches are created. The system automatically posts the goods issue and goods receipt. We’ll cover these processes in the following sections. © 463 9.9 Batch Traceability of Work in Process Batches Process Order Consider the example shown in Figure 9.84 of a regular process order that appears after executing Transaction COR2. This screen shows the Material List, in which one compo- nent, 104, is assigned batch number 7. To post the confirmation using WIP batches, you need to create a link between the raw material and the finished product. It isn’t necessary to make any change in the process order header or components, and you can directly proceed to order confirmation. Figure 9.84 Process Order with Material List Confirmation and Goods Issuance When posting a confirmation using the WIP batch confirmation profile, you’ll notice some of the following details:  The button to display the Goods Movements overview isn’t displayed.  The goods receipt goods movement is always proposed, even if automatic goods receipt isn’t set for the process order.  The goods issue goods movements are always proposed, even if the Backflush check- box isn’t set for the components.  All the goods movements are proposed without quantity. Access the screen shown in Figure 9.85 using Transaction COR6N, and then enter pro- duction Order “1000098” and its first Phase, which in this example is “0020”. Scroll down the screen to evaluate the information provided here. The same three areas—WIP Batch: GI, WIP Batch: GR, and WIP Batch Entry—that were set in the confirmation profile are displayed here. In the WIP Batch: GI area, the system may propose several components, of which we choose raw Material 104 and its associ- ated Batch 7 for consumption (using Mvmnt Type 261). Select this line item, and then choose the WIP Batch button. 9 Batch Management 464 Figure 9.85 Confirmation with WIP Batches In the popup screen that appears (see Figure 9.86), enter the name of the WIP batch in the WIP Batch field (e.g., “WIP_B_006”). With this process, a link between the raw mate- rial batch consumed and the WIP batch is being established. Choose Continue. Figure 9.86 WIP Batch The screen shown in Figure 9.87 prompts you to maintain characteristic values of WIP batch WIP_B_006. Figure 9.88 shows the newly created WIP batch WIP_B_006. Next, maintain the standard confirmation details, such as the yield, scrap, rework, and associated activities (e.g., machine or labor hours) as is normally done in the confirma- tion process. © 465 9.9 Batch Traceability of Work in Process Batches Figure 9.87 Maintaining Characteristic Values of the WIP Batch Figure 9.88 Yield Entry for the WIP Batch Work in Process Batch Goods Receipt As explained previously in this section, the goods receipt movement is proposed by default in the WIP Batch: GR section; however, it’s proposed without a quantity, so you’ll need to input the quantity. After that, select the goods receipt item and the respective WIP Batch, as shown in Figure 9.89, where you first select WIP_B_006 and 9 Batch Management 466 then choose the WIPB->GR button. If the batch for the finished good was already cre- ated at the time of creating or releasing the process order, then this step isn’t needed. This will bring up the screen shown in Figure 9.90. Figure 9.89 Assigning the WIP Batch to the Finished Good Batch In Figure 9.90, notice that the system has created GR Batch number 25 for finished good Material 107 in the WIP Batch: GR section. This confirmation can now be saved, and because the WIP batch was already linked to the raw material, a link between the raw material and the finished product material is created. Figure 9.90 WIP Batch Goods Receipt © 467 9.9 Batch Traceability of Work in Process Batches This is how the system links up a raw material’s batch to a WIP batch and then to a fin- ished good’s batch for the process order 1000098: Raw material 104 (batch number 7): WIP batch (WIP_B_006): Finished good 107 (batch number 25). We’ll see the same link- up when we cover reporting in Section 9.9.4. When posting goods receipt of a finished goods batch, a few more screens or popups may appear to maintain additional details, such as date of manufacture or characteris- tic values of the finished good’s batch that are created by the system at the time of goods receipt. Note Now that you have a basic understanding of WIP batches and how they work, we sug- gest exploring several additional features and functionalities available to handle all business processes. For example, in the earlier Figure 9.89, we showed how to link up the WIP batch with goods receipt, but what if a user mistakenly created a wrong link? To undo or delink this linkage, use the WIPB><GR icon to correct the error.
sections.he:
התהליך — יצירת הזמנת תהליך ואז אישור שבו נוצרות אצוות ה-WIP; המערכת רושמת GI ו-GR אוטומטית.
**הזמנת תהליך:** דוגמה (Figure 9.85) להזמנה רגילה לאחר Transaction COR2 — ה-Material List, רכיב 2265 עם אצווה 0000000130. אין שינוי בכותרת/רכיבים; ניתן לעבור ישר לאישור.
**אישור והנפקה (GI):** באישור עם פרופיל WIP batch: כפתור Goods Movements אינו מוצג; תנועת ה-GR מוצעת תמיד (גם ללא GR אוטומטי); תנועות ה-GI מוצעות תמיד (גם ללא Backflush); כל התנועות מוצעות ללא כמות.
ב-Transaction COR6N (Figure 9.86) הזינו Order "1002208" ו-Phase "0020". מוצגים שלושת האזורים — WIP Batch: GI, ‏WIP Batch: GR, ‏WIP Batch Entry. ב-WIP Batch: GI, המערכת מציעה רכיבים; בחרו חומר 2265 ואצווה 130 לצריכה (Mvmnt Type 261), בחרו את השורה ו-WIP Batch.
בחלון (Figure 9.87) הזינו את שם ה-WIP batch (למשל "WIP_B_006") — קישור בין אצוות חומר הגלם ל-WIP batch. ‏Continue. ב-Figure 9.88 תחזקו ערכי מאפיינים של WIP_B_006. ‏Figure 9.89 — ה-WIP Batch החדש. תחזקו פרטי אישור רגילים (yield, ‏scrap, ‏rework, פעילויות).
**GR של WIP batch:** ה-GR מוצע כברירת מחדל ב-WIP Batch: GR אך ללא כמות — הזינו כמות. בחרו את פריט ה-GR ואת ה-WIP Batch (Figure 9.90): בחרו WIP_B_006 ו-WIPB->GR (אם אצוות המוצר כבר נוצרה ביצירת/שחרור ההזמנה, אין צורך). ב-Figure 9.91, המערכת יצרה GR Batch 0000000136 למוצר 2264 ב-WIP Batch: GR. שמרו — נוצר קישור בין חומר הגלם למוצר.
כך המערכת מקשרת לאצוות מוצר עבור הזמנה 1002208: חומר גלם 2265 (אצווה 130) → WIP batch (WIP_B_006) → מוצר גמור 2264 (אצווה 136). אותו קישור נראה בדיווח (9.9.4).
ברישום GR של אצוות מוצר, עשויים להופיע מסכים נוספים (תאריך ייצור, ערכי מאפיינים).
**הערה:** לתיקון קישור שגוי, השתמשו בסמל WIPB><GR לביטול הקישור.

sections.title: Reporting
sections.en: 9.9.4 Reporting Access the Batch Information Cockpit screen (see Figure 9.91) using Transaction BMBC to see the report on WIP batches. Enter Material “107”, its associated Batch “25”, and Plant “1105”, and then choose Selection (at the top left in the menu bar). Figure 9.91 Batch Information Cockpit 9 Batch Management 468 Figure 9.92 shows Batch (25) for Material 107, which meets the selection criteria. Choose this batch 25 on the left side of the screen, then select Usage from the Details dropdown icon located on the top-right side of the screen. For batch 25 for the finished good 107, Figure 9.92 shows the Top-Down Analysis of the process order 1000098, the raw material 104, and its associated batch 07. However, these screen details still don’t show the associated WIP batch that was created during confirmation. To view the details of the WIP batch, choose process order 1000098, and then choose WIP Batch. Figure 9.92 Batch Usage The lower half of the screen in Figure 9.92 shows the same WIP batch’s linkage that we previously covered: Raw material 104 (batch number 7): WIP batch (WIP_B_006): Fin- ished good 107 (batch number 25). Note Refer to SAP Note 1473025, which answers frequently asked questions about WIP batches. Further, note the following:  Transaction BMOBPRO is a report that shows original batches in production.  Transaction BMOBPUR is a report that traces original batches in procurement.  As a troubleshooting tip, Transaction MB57 can be used once if the batch where- used list isn’t appearing in the Batch Information Cockpit. The next section looks at the Batch Information Cockpit and how it can be used to ana- lyze and monitor batches. © 469
sections.he:
לדיווח, גשו ל-Batch Information Cockpit (Figure 9.92) ב-Transaction BMBC. הזינו Material "2264", ‏Batch "0000000136", ‏Plant "1710", ‏Selection.
Figure 9.93 — אצווה 0000000136 לחומר 2264. בחרו אותה (שמאל), ואז Usage מרשימת Details (ימין-עליון). מוצג Top-Down Analysis של הזמנה 1002208, אך עדיין ללא ה-WIP batch. להצגתו, בחרו הזמנה 1002208 ו-WIP Batch.
החצי התחתון (Figure 9.93) מציג את הקישור: חומר גלם 2265 (אצווה 130) → WIP batch (WIP_B_006) → מוצר גמור 2264 (אצווה 136).
**הערה:** ראו SAP Note 1473025 (שאלות נפוצות על WIP batches). בנוסף:
• Transaction BMOBPRO — דוח אצוות מקור בייצור.
• Transaction BMOBPUR — מעקב אצוות מקור ברכש.
• פתרון בעיות: השתמשו ב-Transaction MB57 פעם אם ה-where-used אינו מופיע ב-Cockpit.

sections.title: Batch Information Cockpit
sections.en: 9.10 Batch Information Cockpit 9.10 Batch Information Cockpit In process industries, such as food and pharmaceuticals, traceability of the ingredients or components within a production or procurement process is of paramount impor- tance. Batch traceability across logistics and supply chain processes is also a legal requirement in many industries and good manufacturing practice to maintain in case there is a batch recall. Companies often develop complex custom reports to view and analyze batch traceability when the Batch Information Cockpit can serve the same pur- pose. With the Batch Information Cockpit, you can do the following:  Perform top-down and bottom-up traceability analysis. With top-down analysis, a finished good traces all the raw, packaging, and semifinished materials that were used in making the finished product’s batch. With bottom-up analysis, it’s possible to trace the ingredients or raw materials and trace all the finished goods that were made using these ingredients or raw materials’ batches.  Access the batch master to display and change information related to the batch directly from Batch Information Cockpit while performing the traceability analysis of a batch.  Display the stock information of the batch.  Display the stock position of a material and its associated batches. To access the Batch Information Cockpit, follow menu path Logistics  Central Functions  Batch Management  Batch Information Cockpit, or use Transaction BMBC. Figure 9.93 shows the initial screen to set parameters that the system then considers to bring up relevant batches of materials. Notice the various tabs available on the right side, which can be used to enter specific information. The left side of the screen provides a search functionality. Figure 9.93 Batch Information Cockpit 9 Batch Management 470 For this example, enter Material “81” and Plant “1105”. Choose Selection, and then choose Execute. This brings up the screen shown in Figure 9.94. The left side shows that the system is able to find the relevant material-plant-batch combination. The right side appears when a user selects Usage from the Details dropdown. Figure 9.94 Bottom-Up Analysis Figure 9.94 shows the bottom-up analysis for batch 7 of material 81 in plant 1105. It shows that this batch was consumed in process order 1000097, which in turn produced batch 23. The raw materials procured externally from suppliers will show up with the material document numbers in the same top-down analysis. Note We suggest exploring several features and functionalities of the Batch Information Cockpit to take advantage of a large amount of available information. For example, in Figure 9.94 and in the Usage tab, choose whether the system should bring up a top-down list or bottom-up list. Similarly, a user can gain comprehensive vis- ibility into all batches that have expired or whose expiration dates are approaching. In Figure 9.95, the Batch Information Cockpit has been run, and several batches have been selected. The materials are shown, and the matches can be displayed by highlight- ing the material. The information regarding the batch is then displayed in a main screen. The tabs represent the number of different screens with information on this batch. © 471
sections.he:
בתעשיות תהליכיות (מזון, תרופות), מעקב הרכיבים בתהליך קריטי. מעקב אצוות הוא גם דרישה חוקית בתעשיות רבות ו-good manufacturing practice לקראת recall. חברות מפתחות דוחות מותאמים מורכבים, בעוד ה-Batch Information Cockpit משרת את אותה מטרה.
עם ה-Cockpit ניתן:
• ניתוח top-down ו-bottom-up. ‏Top-down של מוצר גמור עוקב אחר כל חומרי הגלם, האריזה והחצי-גמורים. ‏Bottom-up עוקב מחומר הגלם לכל המוצרים שיוצרו ממנו.
• גישה לאב האצווה ישירות (להצגה/שינוי) תוך כדי המעקב.
• הצגת מידע מלאי לאצווה.
• הצגת מצב המלאי של חומר ואצוותיו.
לגישה: Logistics • Central Functions • Batch Management • Batch Information Cockpit, או Transaction BMBC (Figure 9.94). הלשוניות בימין לפרטים; שמאל — חיפוש. בדוגמה, הזינו Material "2264", ‏Plant "1710", ‏Selection, ‏Execute Selection (Figure 9.95). שמאל — צירוף חומר-מפעל-אצווה; ימין — בבחירת Usage. מוצג ניתוח bottom-up של אצווה 130 (2264, מפעל 1710): נצרכה בהזמנה 1002208 שייצרה אצווה 136. חומרי גלם שנרכשו חיצונית יוצגו עם מספרי מסמכי חומר בניתוח top-down.
**הערה:** חקרו את התכונות. בלשונית Usage (Figure 9.95) ניתן לבחור top-down או bottom-up, ולקבל נראות לכל האצוות שפקעו או מתקרבות לפקיעה.
ב-Figure 9.96, ה-Cockpit הורץ ונבחרו מספר אצוות. החומרים מוצגים; הדגשת חומר מציגה מידע אצווה במסך הראשי. הלשוניות מייצגות מסכי מידע שונים.

sections.title: Electronic Batch Record
sections.en: 9.11 Electronic Batch Record Figure 9.95 Central Area of the Batch Information Cockpit 9.11 Electronic Batch Record In highly regulated industries, such as pharmaceuticals, there’s often a legal require- ment to maintain a complete trail and record of all the batches used in the logistics and supply chain of manufacturing a product. Often, it’s not just the batches received from the procurement process or batches consumed in the production process that are important for record keeping; maintaining a complete record of various quality inspec- tions that took place in the manufacturing process is important as well. The electronic batch record, or batch record for short, captures these inspection details too. Access the screen shown in Figure 9.96 by following menu path Logistics  Central Func- tions  Batch Management  Tools  Batch Record or using Transaction COEBR. On the left side, you can see a complete trail for material 81 and its associated Batch 15. As you drill down in the same node, the related process orders will appear: (1) the two types of quality inspections (04 for finished goods inspection, 03 for in-process inspection) if the PP-QM integration is in place, and (2) the Material List (BOM) used in the produc- tion process. On the upper-right side of the same screen, you can only approve an electronic batch record for archiving with the Approve button if the statuses of various elements (e.g., process or process order, inspection lots, etc.) are set as required for electronic archiving. Here, the system also guides you to check all the prerequisites for electronic batch record. After approval, an electronic batch record can be archived by clicking the Archive button. 9 Batch Management 472 Figure 9.96 Electronic Batch Record The lower-right side shows comprehensive details of the electronic batch record in PDF format. Note We recommend engaging an SAP NetWeaver consultant to ensure that the necessary authorizations required for archiving electronic batches are granted. The SAP Net- Weaver consultant will also set up a document repository required to store the elec- tronic batch records being archived. In some industries, such as consumer products or automotive suppliers, there are legal requirements to store where-used data of materials used for production and delivered to customers. Enabling recall actions becomes a mandatory and critical issue for these industries. Data can be recorded by managing all relevant materials in batches, but this method has a negative impact on data volume. When turning on batch management, entering a batch number becomes obligatory for all goods movements. Then, all inven- tory postings must be executed on the batch level, and labor costs for inventory man- agement will increase. With the documentary batch record, it’s important to ensure that a partial stock of a material is traceable without having to maintain a batch’s data. This reduces the effort and complexities involved in maintaining batch data. The documentary batch record finds greater use in automotive and consumer goods industries but is unsuitable for use in dangerous goods. © 473
sections.he:
בתעשיות מפוקחות (תרופות), לרוב יש דרישה חוקית לתחזק מסלול ורשומה מלאים של כל האצוות בשרשרת. חשוב לתעד לא רק אצוות שהתקבלו/נצרכו, אלא גם את בדיקות האיכות בתהליך. ה-electronic batch record (רשומת אצווה) לוכד פרטים אלו.
לגישה: Logistics • Central Functions • Batch Management • Tools • Batch Record, או Transaction COEBR (Figure 9.97). בשמאל — מסלול מלא לחומר 2264 ואצווה 136. בצלילה מופיעות הזמנות התהליך הקשורות: (1) שני סוגי בדיקות איכות (04 לבדיקת מוצר גמור, 03 לבדיקה בתהליך) אם יש אינטגרציית PP-QM; (2) ה-Material List (BOM).
בפינה ימנית-עליונה, ניתן לאשר (Approve) רשומה לארכוב רק אם הסטטוסים (הזמנת תהליך, inspection lots) מוגדרים כנדרש. המערכת מנחה לבדוק את התנאים. לאחר האישור, ניתן לארכב ב-Archive. הפינה הימנית-תחתונה מציגה פרטים מקיפים ב-PDF.
**הערה:** ערבו יועץ SAP NetWeaver להרשאות הנדרשות לארכוב ולהקמת document repository.
בתעשיות מסוימות (מוצרי צריכה, ספקי רכב), יש דרישות חוקיות לאחסן נתוני where-used של חומרים שיוצרו ונמסרו. אפשור recall קריטי. ניתן לרשום נתונים בניהול כל החומרים באצוות, אך עם השפעה שלילית על נפח הנתונים — הזנת מספר אצווה הופכת חובה לכל תנועות הסחורה, כל הרישומים ברמת האצווה, ועלויות העבודה גדלות.
עם ה-documentary batch record, חשוב להבטיח שמלאי חלקי ניתן למעקב ללא תחזוקת נתוני אצווה — מפחית מאמץ ומורכבות. שימושי ברכב ומוצרי צריכה, אך לא מתאים ל-dangerous goods. ניתן לבצע documentary batch:
• הזנת documentary batches בתנועות סחורה.
• בהזמנת תהליך — רק ב-backflush.
• ב-embedded EWM — בעת אישור transport order.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 9.12 Summary Documentary batch processing can be achieved in the following ways:  Documentary batches can be entered during goods movements.  In a process order, entering documentary batches is only possible at backflush.  In WM, entering documentary batches must be enabled during transport order con- firmation. 9.12 Summary Batch management is important to a large number of process-based industries. It has developed from just an identification of a group of items to a process that allows com- panies to perform product recalls, select and sell by batch characteristics, and identify expiring stock. As the drive for competitive advantage continues, companies will fur- ther investigate how batch information can lower production time and hasten material to the customer. Chapter 10 will discuss sample management. ©
sections.he: ניהול אצוות חשוב למספר רב של תעשיות תהליכיות. הוא התפתח מזיהוי קבוצות פריטים לתהליך המאפשר product recalls, בחירה ומכירה לפי מאפייני אצווה, וזיהוי מלאי פוקע. ככל שהתחרות נמשכת, חברות יחקרו כיצד מידע אצווה יכול להפחית זמן ייצור ולהאיץ אספקה. פרק 10 — ניהול דגימות (sample management).

sections.title: Plant Settings
sections.en: 10.1 Plant Settings In this step, you make the necessary configuration settings that act as a control for business users to enter information on the number of containers at the time of goods receipt for a purchase, process, or production order. You also incorporate the sampling procedure that the system refers to if it’s unable to find the required information in the master data setup for sample management. This is necessary for the system to calcu- late the sample size on inspection lot creation for sample management by using the sampling procedure. For the relevant plant-wise settings for sample management, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level. Choose the relevant plant, which in this example is plant 1710 (see Figure 10.1). In the Insp. Lot Creation tab, choose Recording of number of containers required in Enter Container at GR. This setting doesn’t let the business user save the goods receipt for a purchase or process order until information about the number of containers is entered. Further, in the Settings for Sampling Procedures area, enter the code for a previously created sam- pling procedure, “PFIX5”, in the Sample Management field. This sampling procedure denotes that the system will create a fixed sample size of five units upon goods receipt. Figure 10.1 Plant Parameters © 477
sections.he:
כאן מגדירים בקרה להזנת מספר המכלים ב-GR (הזמנת רכש/תהליך/ייצור), ומשלבים sampling procedure שהמערכת מתייחסת אליו אם לא מוצאת מידע בנתוני האב — לחישוב הדגימה ב-sample management.
ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Basic Settings • Maintain Settings at Plant Level. בחרו plant 1710 (Figure 10.1). בלשונית Insp. Lot Creation, בחרו Recording of number of containers required ב-Enter Container at GR (חוסם שמירת GR עד הזנת מספר המכלים). ב-Settings for Sampling Procedures, הזינו את ה-sampling procedure "PFIX5" בשדה Sample Management (דגימה קבועה של חמש יחידות ב-GR).

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 10.2 Master Data Note Refer to Chapter 3 for how to create a sampling procedure that you can use in this step. While creating a sampling procedure, choose the Sample Management radio button that’s available in the Inspection Point area. 10.2 Master Data As with other business processes into which QM integrates, sample management also requires that you maintain the master data before you can run the business processes. Apart from the regular master data, such as relevant inspection type activations in the material master and creating inspection plans, you also need to maintain a sample- drawing procedure and assign it to the material’s inspection plan for planned physical samples. In the following section, we’ll discuss master data specific to sample management, including the sample-drawing procedure, inspection plan, and ensuring the QM master data checklist is adhered to.
sections.he:

sections.title: Sample-Drawing Procedure
sections.en: 10.2.1 Sample-Drawing Procedure You can use the sample-drawing procedure to plan automatic (planned) physical sam- ple generation during inspection lot creation. In a sample-drawing procedure, you define how many samples the system should draw, whether the business user needs to confirm a sample’s drawing, and which category of physical sample to draw. The fol- lowing physical sample categories are available for selection:  Primary sample You draw the primary sample directly from a material/batch stock. You can inspect these samples or create pooled samples from them.  Pooled sample You create this sample by mixing other physical samples from the same material/ batch.  Reserve sample You draw the reserve sample from a material/batch stock and store it for other inspections. With the sample-drawing procedure, you can also control when the system should automatically print out the sample-drawing instructions, which contain detailed infor- mation on how to draw a sample. If the material is supplied in different physical sample containers, you can store corresponding drawing instructions depending on the phys- ical sample container. For all planned physical sample creation, you assign the sample- drawing procedure to the material’s inspection plan, master recipe, or routing. 10 Sample Management 478 In sample management, it’s often also necessary to draw physical samples that weren’t originally planned and are therefore known as unplanned physical samples. This busi- ness scenario generally applies when you have to conduct additional tests on a mate- rial that didn’t show satisfactory inspection results and for which you need more physical samples to conduct another round of testing. For such unplanned physical samples, the following two options are available:  You can manually generate an entirely new physical sample.  You can manually generate a physical sample for an existing physical sample record. In the sample-drawing procedure, you can determine whether the system automati- cally or manually releases (or confirms) the automatically created physical samples. When you confirm a physical sample drawing, the system releases some or all corre- sponding physical samples. Considering the compliance aspects of Good Manufactur- ing Practice (GMP), there may be a need for quality inspection to manually confirm physical sample drawing. Further, there is the option to enter digital signatures (see Chapter 3), which ensures that only authorized employees can execute certain activi- ties (e.g., the confirmation). You have to manually confirm the manually created phys- ical samples. To make the relevant settings for the sample-drawing procedure, use Transaction QPV2 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sample-Drawing Procedure  Edit. Note To display the sample-drawing procedure, use Transaction QPV3 or menu path Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sample-Drawing Procedure  Display. Figure 10.2 shows the initial screen for the sample-drawing procedure. For this exam- ple, enter “S200” and select the Consider No. of Containers checkbox so that the system makes it mandatory for a business user to enter the container information in the inspection lot. In addition, and only if required, select the Confirmation Req. checkbox to enable the business user to confirm sample drawing as a separate step. Figure 10.2 Sample-Drawing Procedure © 479 10.2 Master Data Tips and Tricks If a sample-drawing procedure is no longer in use or becomes obsolete, you can block its usage by selecting the Blocking indicator checkbox. Choose sample-drawing procedure S200, and then choose Sample-drawing item on the left side; this leads to the screen in Figure 10.3. Figure 10.3 Primary, Pooled, and Reserve Samples Figure 10.3 1 shows the Primary samples tab, where you enter the unit of measure for Lot Container as “EA” (each). From Sample contnr (container), you can choose the rele- vant container that you’ll use for storing physical samples from the dropdown. In Size factor, you enter a number that the system then uses to multiply with the physical sample quantity. For example, if you enter a size factor of 2, then the system creates a physical sample quantity double the originally calculated value. In the Number of Sam- ples area, you can define how the system calculates the quantity of physical samples. Here, apart from the option to have a fixed number of (primary) physical samples, you can use a sampling scheme that the system can use to calculate the number of physical samples. If you do use the sample scheme option, you also have to assign the Insp. severity, as well as the acceptable quality level (AQL value). Finally, you can also enter a formula to calculate the number of physical samples. For this example, enter the fixed number of physical samples as 3, and the system auto- matically creates three primary physical samples. Choose the Pooled samples tab 2. 10 Sample Management 480 The options for pooled samples are the same as for primary samples. Enter “2” to auto- matically create two pooled samples during inspection lot creation. Finally, choose the Reserve samples tab 3. Here, the system only offers the option to enter a fixed number of reserve samples, the quantity for each sample, and the unit of measure to go with the quantity. Enter the details shown so that the system creates one reserve sample of 3 KG. To summarize the physical sample settings that you’ve made so far, the system creates four physical samples—one primary sample, two pooled samples, and one reserve sample—during inspection lot creation. We’ll show these happening when we cover the business processes of sample management. Save your settings.

sections.title: QM Master Data Checklist
sections.en: 10.2.3 QM Master Data Checklist The following is the QM master data checklist:  Inspection type 01 is active in the Quality Management view for material QM003. In addition, activate inspection type 15 for sample management.  Inspection plan usage 5 (for goods receipt), inspection plan usage 9 (material check), and both inspection plans must have status 4 (released). For inspection type 15 (sam- ple management), the system uses the inspection plan with usage 9. Note You can integrate sample management with inspection types 01, 02, 04, 05, and 08. 10.3 Business Processes When materials are delivered, they’re usually in one or more containers, from which the quality inspector draws physical samples. The system determines the scope of the physical sample drawing from the information in the inspection plan and the assigned 10 Sample Management 482 sample-drawing procedure and prints it out on the sample-drawing instruction when it creates an inspection lot. Here, you perform goods receipt for an already created purchase order, in which the system asks for information about the number of containers. It also creates a goods receipt inspection lot, as well as physical samples of various sample categories. Then, you release the physical samples, followed by printing labels. You perform results recording of not only the goods receipt inspection lot but also inspection lots created for physical samples. Figure 10.6 illustrates this process. Figure 10.6 Business Process of Sample Management in Goods Receipt from Procurement Process In the following sections, we’ll show how to create a goods receipt of an already created purchase order. The goods receipt process will prompt the user to enter details of phys- ical samples. At the same time, the goods receipt will also create an inspection lot with multiple physical samples. Samples are released so that standard QM processes such as results recording and usage decision can occur. We’ll also discuss how to manually cre- ate a physical sample. Note Refer to Chapter 4 to learn more about business processes in procurement and inven- tory management, including how to create a purchase order and then perform a goods receipt for the same purchase order.

sections.en: 10.3.3 Physical Samples for Goods Receipt Click the Samples button shown in Figure 10.9, and the system opens a popup window showing an overview of various physical samples created for this specific inspection lot, as shown in Figure 10.10. The system also assigns the sample-drawing number (SampDraw) 3 to all four physical samples. This sample drawing is a common reference point for all physical samples. There are three cate- gories of physical samples, and these are set per sample-drawing procedure S200 that you maintained in Figure 10.3. For details of each physical sample category, place the cursor in the Cat field and either use the dropdown option that appears or press (F4). This is shown in the lower half of the screen, where 1 denotes Primary Sample, 2 Pooled Sample, and 3 Reserve Sample. A primary sample is the main sample used the sample management process. A pooled sample can be used for multiple trials and stability studies, while a reserved sample is used in case there’s an issue with the primary or the pooled sample, and the quality inspector needs another sample, which can be drawn from the reserved samples. So, the system creates one primary sample, two pooled samples, and one reserve sample, consistent with the settings made in Figure 10.3. The initial status of physical samples is CRTD (created), and you need to release or con- firm a sample drawing in a separate step. All of these actions are the direct result of set- tings made in Figure 10.2.

sections.title: Release and Print Physical Sample Label
sections.en: 10.3.4 Release and Print Physical Sample Label A physical sample with status CRTD (created) doesn’t allow subsequent business func- tions, like creating an inspection lot of inspection type 15, without which you can’t record results or make its usage decision. For an automatically or manually created physical sample, you release the physical sample drawing so that it attains the REL (released) status. To do so, use Transaction QPR2 (Change Physical Sample). On the initial screen, enter the physical sample, and press (Enter). Choose Release Sample from the top menu bar and save. For automatically created (planned) physical samples, you can print out labels for phys- ical samples. You can create these labels according to your requirements; print details such as name, date, time, batch, sample number, and inspection lot number; and even add a barcode. You can also manually trigger label printing for the sample data record. To view the print labels request or send it to the printer spool, use Transaction SP02 or menu path More  System  Own Spool Requests (see Figure 10.11). Figure 10.11 Label Print of a Physical Sample 10 Sample Management 486 Note Ensure that function module QPRP_LABEL_PRINT_MULTIPLE_1 is assigned to the sample type for label printing. Refer to Section 10.5.2, where the relevant configuration settings are discussed.

sections.title: Inspection Lots for Physical Samples
sections.en: 10.3.5 Inspection Lots for Physical Samples Upon releasing physical samples and confirming their withdrawal, you can create inspection lots of physical samples for subsequent results recording and usage deci- sion. To create inspection lots for physical samples, use Transaction QPR5 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Sample Management  Phys- ical Sample-Drawing  Create Inspection Lots. Figure 10.12 shows the initial screen to create inspection lots for physical samples and to view the status of physical samples and their storage deadlines with Monitor Con- trol. Enter Sample-Drawing Number “3”, and in the Monitor Control dropdown, choose Inspection lot creation. Finally choose Execute (not shown) so that the screen in Figure 10.13 appears. Figure 10.12 Inspection Lot for Physical Samples © 487 10.3 Business Processes Figure 10.13 brings up the same four physical samples of sample drawing 3. In this step, you specifically create inspection lots for physical samples. To do so, choose Select All (or choose a sample) to select all four physical samples, and then choose Create Inspec- tion Lot. In the screen that appears, refer to the Current Insp. Lot column, which con- tains details of individual inspection lots that the system creates for all four physical samples at the time of goods receipt, which in this example is inspection lot 10000000662. For this example, sample 100000012 was selected followed by choos- ing Inspection Lot Creation from the top menu bar, which led to the physical sample’s inspection lot creation for sample management 150000000004. Figure 10.13 Worklist for Inspection Lots Creation for Physical Samples When you save, you’ll see the log that appears upon successful (or unsuccessful) cre- ation of inspection lots. If inspection lot creation for a physical sample is unsuccessful, the system displays the complete reason for it (e.g., missing master data or incorrect/ incomplete inspection plans). Tips and Tricks You can use this same option to create multiple inspection lots for the same physical sample. For example, after finding the initial results of the physical sample unsatisfac- tory, say you want to retest the physical sample. You’ll need another inspection lot for the same physical sample, need to record new results, and need to make another usage decision. We’ll now individually review both inspection types. The first inspection type is for goods receipt for a purchase order (inspection type 01) and how the system prompts the business user to select from pooled physical samples as inspection points during the quality inspection process. The second inspection type, 15, is for the physical sam- ple. Note You can also create inspection type 15 for pooled samples so that you can inde- pendently perform all the QM functions, such as results recording and usage decision 10 Sample Management 488 for pooled samples, first, and then enter the findings as inspection points (basically pooled physical samples) in goods receipt inspection for the purchase order (inspection type 01). We suggest that although the system offers several options to record results and make usage decisions for pooled physical samples, you should evaluate all available options to maintain a balance between having information in the system and having to enter the inspection data multiple times.

sections.title: Results Recording for Pooled Samples (Goods Receipt Inspection)
sections.en: 10.3.7 Results Recording for Pooled Samples (Goods Receipt Inspection) The business process of results recording for the physical sample is no different from that of inspection lot results recording. One or several physical samples can exist for an inspection lot. You also have the option of making a usage decision for an inspection lot only when you’ve processed and evaluated all physical samples for an inspection © 489 10.3 Business Processes lot. For unplanned (manually created) physical samples, you may need to manually release the physical samples before you can record results. Access the screen in Figure 10.15 through Transaction QE01, and enter Inspection Lot “10000000662” and Operation “0010” to bring up the list of physical samples avail- able. In the Inspection point area, place the cursor on Sample, and use the dropdown option or press (F4). Out of the four physical samples that the system creates, it brings up only two pooled physical samples, 100000009 and 100000010, for you to choose from as inspection points. These two available pooled physical samples as inspection points are shown on the right side of Figure 10.15. Choose the first physical sample (100000009), and press (Enter), which brings up the results recording screen for inspection lot 10000000662, operation 0010, and physical sample 100000009. The sample size is 5 PC. You record the results of these two physical samples with reference to their inspection point and also make their usage decisions. Figure 10.15 Results Recording of Pooled Samples: Initial Screen Next, let’s evaluate the inspection lots for a physical sample (sample management)— that is, the inspection lot of inspection type 15.

sections.title: Manually Creating a Physical Sample
sections.en: 10.3.8 Manually Creating a Physical Sample You can manually create physical samples at any given point in time with or without reference to any of the previously created objects, such as material documents or sam- ple-drawing instructions. The system offers several options to create physical samples 10 Sample Management 490 to meet business scenarios, such as physical samples of competitor goods, samples for complaints against a supplier, or customer and physical samples for a stability study (see Chapter 15). When you choose one of the reference objects to create a physical sample, the system brings up the option to enter details of that reference object so that it can logically con- nect the newly created physical sample with that reference object. For example, if you create a physical sample for a stability study, the system opens a popup in which you can enter a reference of a stability study for which you want to create the physical sam- ple. Similarly, if you want to create a physical sample for complaints against the sup- plier, then the system opens a popup for you to enter the material document number against which you initially received the supplier’s goods. To create a physical sample, use Transaction QPR1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Sample Management  Physical Sample  Create. Figure 10.16 shows the initial screen to create a physical sample. Figure 10.16 Creating the Physical Sample: Initial Screen The system offers various options to create different types of physical samples, which are available when you choose the Sample Type dropdown. You can also use the copy model function to copy data from an existing object to the next physical sample. For example, you can use a reference of an already created physical sample to create a new physical sample, thus saving you time and effort in data entry. Similarly, you can refer- ence the already created physical sample drawing to attach to the physical sample. © 491 10.3 Business Processes For this example, choose Sample Type 01 Goods Receipt Sample, and, in the Sample Drawing area, select the Extend Existing radio button. Enter the previously created physical sample Drawing Number “3” (this is the same physical sample drawing that previously created four physical samples for goods receipt against the purchase order). Finally, choose Sample (not shown, but located at the bottom-right corner of the screen). This opens the popup that informs you of the details against which the system will create the physical sample and of which it will also automatically incorporate all the references, such as material, batch, and material document numbers. Choose Continue to see the screen in Figure 10.17, which depicts physical sample 100000012. The system automatically references all information from physical sample drawing 3. Notice that the status of the physical sample is CRTD (created). Figure 10.17 Unplanned Physical Sample Creation You can also print labels on this screen. You can enter additional information in the fields that are available for data entry. Because this is a manually created physical sam- ple, the system denotes this with the checkmark in the Sample manually created check- box. Choose the Sample Detail tab. Here, choose the sample category, such as Initial Sample, Pooled Sample, or Reserve Sample, from the dropdown list, and enter the sample quan- tity, such as 1 PC in this example, to denote the sample quantity of the physical sample. 10 Sample Management 492 Choose the Inspection Lot Data tab, and the screen in Figure 10.18 appears showing the reference data of Inspection Lot 10000000662, to which this physical sample 100000019 will attach itself. Before you save your entries, release the physical sample from the top menu bar of Figure 10.17. Figure 10.18 Inspection Lot Data of Previous Goods Receipt Samples Figure 10.19 shows the physical Sample Storage tab, which shows the storage location and sample location of the reserve sample. Figure 10.19 Physical Sample Storage Access the screen in Figure 10.20 through Transaction QA02 for inspection lot 10000000662, and then, in the Sample tab, choose Physical Samples Overview (not shown). Physical sample drawing 3 now extends to incorporate the new physical sample © 493

sections.title: Physical Sample Drawing with Reference: Production Processes
sections.en: 10.4 Physical Sample Drawing with Reference: Production Processes 100000012. The remaining steps for the manually created (unplanned) physical sample are the same, such as creating its inspection lot, recording results, and making a usage decision, as we previously covered for automatic creation of physical samples. Tips and Tricks Because you created and released the physical sample manually, you can also use Trans- action QPR2 (Change Physical Sample) to directly create an inspection lot for the sample. Figure 10.20 Manually Created Physical Sample as Part of Sample Drawing 4 10.4 Physical Sample Drawing with Reference: Production Processes The business processes for goods receipt for a process or production order aren’t any dif- ferent from those for goods receipt from the procurement process. However, in the pro- duction process, an important business process is the in-process or during-production process for which you want to carry out quality inspection using sample management. Sample management integrates with all production types, such as discrete, process, and repetitive manufacturing (REM). A typical production process involves processing a material that goes through various operations and phases during the production pro- cess. During the course of its production, the material attains different physical and chemical attributes and requires physical inspections. There are two options to handle quality inspection in production processes using sam- ple management. The first option is that for planned physical sample drawings, you 10 Sample Management 494 can assign the sample-drawing procedure to the routing or master recipe, and the sys- tem creates a physical sample when it creates the inspection lot. The second option is to manually draw the physical sample on different criteria, such as drawing a physical sample after every five hours or after every 100 PC of production. In such cases, you don’t plan the drawing of physical samples in a sample-drawing procedure. You create the samples manually with reference to an inspection lot or order. In this section, we’ll show how creating a process order creates an in-process (during production) inspection lot, which you then use as a reference to create physical sam- ples.

Depending on the PP settings, the system creates the in-process inspection lot either at the time of creating a process order or on its release. sections.title: Physical Sample Drawing with Reference
sections.en: 10.4.2 Physical Sample Drawing with Reference To create a physical sample with reference to a production order, process order, or mate- rial/plant/production version combination (REM), use Transaction QPR6 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Sample Management  Physical Sample-Drawing  Create with Reference. Figure 10.22 shows the initial screen to create a new physical sample with reference to production, the process order, the in- process inspection lot, or REM’s material, plant, and production version combination. Enter the number of physical samples that you want to create. By selecting the Simulate Sample Creation checkbox, you simulate whether the system can indeed create the physical samples or whether it will lead to any warnings or errors. If there’s a warning or error message, you can first correct it before proceeding to create physical samples. In the Detailed Data for the Sample area, you can choose a sample category from the drop- down list and enter the sample quantity, together with the physical sample unit of mea- sure. In the Data for Storage area (not shown but located further down the same screen), you can enter further information about the physical samples, such as the storage loca- tion and sample location for the physical samples that you want to create, and the sys- tem automatically incorporates the information for all physical samples. Figure 10.22 Physical Sample Drawing with Reference: Initial Screen 10 Sample Management 496 Tips and Tricks It’s recommended to use the Simulate Sample Creation functionality to first simulate and see if the system will be able to successfully create the physical samples. If not, then this functionality will inform you of the missing or incomplete data or other set- tings that must first be addressed before the system can successfully create physical samples. After the system creates the physical sample, you can use Transaction QPR2 to add or change the information for a physical sample. Enter the information that you see in Figure 10.22, and choose Execute, and you’ll see that the system creates one physical sample, 200000002, as shown in Figure 10.23. The system incorporates other details, such as material, either directly from the process order or from inspection lot 30000000554. Save your entries. The remaining steps are the same, such as creating the inspection lot for the physical sample, recording results, and making a usage decision. sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.en: 10.5 Configuration Basics Configuration in sample management requires using some of the already created con- figuration objects, such as status profile or number ranges, and assigning them. Other configuration activities involve creating or changing configuration objects to meet business needs. We’ll discuss these activities in the following sections.

sections.title: Physical Sample Type Assignment to Inspection Type
sections.en: 10.5.1 Physical Sample Type Assignment to Inspection Type In this step, you assign a physical sample type to the relevant inspection type so that during automatic (planned) physical samples creation, the system is able to find the © 497 10.5 Configuration Basics relevant physical sample type. For a manual (unplanned) physical sample, you can choose the physical sample type at the time of creation. To assign a physical sample type to an inspection type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Maintain Inspec- tion Types. In Figure 10.24, for Inspection Type 01 (Goods Receipt Insp. for Purchase Order), assign Sample Type 01 Goods receipt sample, and save your entries. You have to ensure that similar settings are in place for all inspection types with which you want to integrate sample management. Figure 10.24 Physical Sample Type Assignment to Inspection Type

sections.title: Define Physical Sample Types
sections.en: 10.5.2 Define Physical Sample Types To manage physical samples, you can add new sample types for necessary inspection types. Typically, sample types that the system delivers are sufficient to meet most busi- ness needs. If you want to use your own number range for any of the sample types, you need to define it for the fiscal years you want. 10 Sample Management 498 Tips and Tricks If you don’t want to restrict number ranges of physical samples to a predefined num- ber of fiscal years, you can enter “9999” in the Year field to denote infinite use of the assigned number range to the physical sample. On the other hand, if you assign year 2023 to a number range, then the system will require you to enter a new number range when the year 2024 begins. To define a new physical sample type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Manage- ment  Quality Inspection  Sample Management  Define Physical Sample Types. In the Change View “Definition of sample types” overview screen, choose Sample Type 02 (Sample from production). You can assign a previously defined or standard number range available in the system. You can maintain the Status Profile if there’s a business need to control different functions of the physical sample through the status profile. The standard function module is available for sample label printing, which you can use along with the checkbox to initiate immediate printing (see Figure 10.25). Be sure to maintain the function module for label printing as shown so that the system is able to print labels. Figure 10.25 New Physical Sample Type

sections.title: Define Physical Sample Locations
sections.en: 10.5.4 Define Physical Sample Locations Physical sample locations uniquely identify different locations used to keep the physi- cal samples. These can be various sections or divisions of the quality control. You can create new, plant-specific physical sample storage locations (physical or virtual) with menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Sample Management  Define Physical Sample Locations. In the Determine Work Area: Entry popup that appears, enter Plant “1710”, choose New Entries, and enter the storage location code and its description. Save your entries. 10.6 Summary This chapter covered the master data that you need to set up for sample management. Then, it delved into business processes for goods receipt in procurement and how it triggers physical sample creation. The business processes for sample management for goods receipt from procurement are no different from those for goods receipt from a production order or stock transport order. While leveraging automatic (planned) phys- ical sample creation, you can also manually create the same (unplanned) samples as required to meet business needs. Similarly, you can create inspection lots for physical samples, either in a mass transaction or individually. The next chapter covers quality certificates in SAP S/4HANA. ©

sections.title: Incoming Quality Certificates
sections.en: 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates The first step toward integrating quality certificates into the procurement process begins when the person overseeing QM operations assigns a certificate type, which is needed for a procured material. A certificate type confirms the specific type of certifi- cate that the company needs from the supplier at the time of goods receipt and shows compliance with the quality standards set by the company. The next step is to put the necessary control levels in place for incoming quality certificate submission. Such con- trol levels can vary from a lenient information message to a more stringent error mes- sage that occurs if the incoming certificate doesn’t accompany the receipt of the goods. 11 Quality Certificates 502 An information message by the system simply informs the warehouse staff of the missing quality certificate. An error message doesn’t allow for a goods receipt until the supplier submits the quality certificate. Let’s get started with setting up the configuration basics.

sections.title: Configuring the Control Key
sections.en: 11.1.1 Configuring the Control Key A control key controls the allowed (or disallowed) business functions by setting the parameters or settings that the system should check during transaction processing. To define a new control key or make changes to an existing one, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Control Keys. In the screen that appears, select QM Control Key 0005 followed by choosing Details and Figure 11.1 will appear. Figure 11.1 Control Key for QM in Procurement Select at least the two checkboxes for Release Required and Certificate Required. The Release Required checkbox confirms that the user must maintain the supplier’s rela- tionship to the material before initiating any procurement activity in the system. This relationship is referred to as a quality information record, which we’ll discuss in Section 11.1.3. The Certificate Required checkbox ensures that the supplier submits an incoming © 503 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates quality certificate at the time of goods delivery. Although these are related to QM, the remaining checkboxes aren’t directly related to incoming quality certificates. Tips and Tricks You can define a new control key if the standard control keys available in SAP S/4HANA don’t fulfill your business requirements.

sections.title: Define Control Functions for Certificate Processing
sections.en: 11.1.2 Define Control Functions for Certificate Processing Just like a control key, you also assign a certificate type in the material master data and assign further control functions for incoming quality certificates. To define the control function of a specific certificate type, use Transaction V_TQ05 or follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Keys for Cer- tificate Processing. Choose Define Certificate Types. The screen that appears contains a list of the standard available certificate types. You can either use the available certificate types or define a new one. If the existing certifi- cate types meet your company’s business needs, then we suggest that you use them as is or make changes to them. For this example, we create a new Certificate Type, 0008, as shown in Figure 11.2. Figure 11.2 Detailed Screen of Certificate Type 0008 To gain a better understanding of each option in Figure 11.2, refer to Table 11.1. 11 Quality Certificates 504 The configuration for incoming certificates is now complete. The next step is to main- tain the relevant information in the material master data and create the quality infor- mation record.

sections.title: Master Data for Incoming Quality Certificates
sections.en: 11.1.3 Master Data for Incoming Quality Certificates You need to set up the QM master data for the incoming quality certificate in SAP S/4HANA before starting the procurement process. We’ll discuss the required master data in the following sections. Certificate Type Control Detail of Control Function Certificate for Each PO Item The system requires a separate certificate for each item in the purchase order. If not selected, then one certificate is suffi- cient for the entire purchase order containing multiple line items. Certificate for Each GR Item The system requires a separate certificate for each item on the goods receipt. If not selected, then one certificate is sufficient for the entire goods receipt containing multiple line items. Certificate Check Required This checkbox is generally used in business scenarios involv- ing electronic certificates and in which the user must still check the certificate to ensure that all parameters of the ordered goods are in conformity. Control Without Certificate Enforces a required action if a certificate isn’t received. The various available options include no information message, just an information message, warning message, error mes- sage, moving material, and blocked stock. Enhanced Certificate Pro- cessing Used for enhanced certificate processing. No Certificate Confirmation at GR With selection of this checkbox, as well as the Enhanced Certifcate Processing checkbox, the business user must separately record the incoming certificate instead of simply confirming certificate receipt at the time of material goods receipt. Rem. Deadline (Days) This option is maintained in number of days to create a system-generated reminder if the supplier fails to deliver the quality certificate after the delivery of goods. Escalation Deadline Also maintained in number of days, this option stipulates that the system must escalate the reminder if the supplier still fails to deliver or submit the quality certificate. Table 11.1 Certificate Type Options © 505 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates Certificate Details in the QM View in the Material Master Figure 11.3 shows the Quality Management view of the material master that was accessed by using Transaction MM02 and entering material RM129 and plant 1710. In the ensuing popup to select material views, choose the Quality Management view and press (Enter). Select the QM in Procur. Active checkbox if you need a quality informa- tion record (otherwise known as a relationship between the supplier and the material) to exist while creating a purchase order. Because this is a procurement process, we rec- ommend that you select this checkbox. Assign QM Control Key 0005 and Certificate Type 0008. These are the same two configuration objects (the QM control key and the certificate type) that you managed in the previous section. Figure 11.3 Assigning QM Control Key and Certificate Type in the Material Master Quality Management View Note Although the focus of this chapter is on quality certificates, make sure that other QM master data elements for this material (RM129)—such as the relevant inspection type activation in the material master, master inspection characteristics, inspection, and plan—are already available in the system. Quality Information Record Because you selected the QM in Procur. Active checkbox, as shown in Figure 11.3, you need to define a relationship between a material and the supplier as a part of the QM master data. To create a quality information record, use Transaction QI01 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Quality Info Record: Procurement  Create. On the initial screen that appears for the cre- ation of a quality information record, enter Material “RM129”, Supplier “17300006”, and Plant “1710”, and then press (Enter) so that the screen in Figure 11.4 appears. On this screen, choose the Inspection Control tab, and then choose Inspection Active If Supplier Not Certified in Insp. Control. This ensures that in the case of an uncertified supplier, the system checks that there is an incoming certificate for the relevant 11 Quality Certificates 506 material (RM129) procured from the supplier (17300006). Other option is here regard- less of the fact that a supplier is certified; otherwise, it will still have to go through the quality inspection and quality control process. Finally, it also has an option that a sup- plier is exempted from quality certification process for this specific material. Save the quality information record. This step completes the important QM master data you need to implement incoming certificates in procurement processes. However, to fully understand the completeness and implications of configuration and master data in procurement processes, we’ll run an end-to-end procurement cycle of creating a purchase order, posting the goods receipt of the same purchase order, and managing missing information in incoming certificates in the next sections. We’ll also explain how to enter incoming certificate details with reference to the purchase order and its line-item number, as well as gener- ate reminders to suppliers to submit missing certificates against the goods supplied. Figure 11.4 Quality Information Record

sections.title: Create a Purchase Order
sections.en: 11.1.4 Create a Purchase Order To create the purchase order, use Transaction ME21N or follow menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Purchasing  Purchase Order  Create  Supplier/Supplying Plant Known. In the screen that appears, enter Supplier “17300006”, material “RM129”, a quantity of 100 EA, and Plant “1710” and can be seen when the Item Overview tab located in the center of the screen is expanded (see Figure 11.5). Notice that QA Control Key 0005 is activated in the Delivery tab, and a certificate is required at the time of goods receipt (delivery) of the material against the purchase © 507 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates order’s line-item number. Further, the associated CertificateType is 0008 as shown here. Save the purchase order, and the system generates purchase order number 4500001824. Figure 11.5 Item Detail of Purchase Order for Procured Material

sections.title: Goods Receipt against the Purchase Order
sections.en: 11.1.5 Goods Receipt against the Purchase Order Now, you’ll record goods receipt for purchase order number 4500001824. Use Transac- tion MIGO or follow menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Inventory Manage- ment  Goods Movement  Goods Movement. In the screen that appears, enter the purchase order number previously created (“4500001824”), and press (Enter) (see Figure 11.6). Figure 11.6 Warning Message for Missing Incoming Certificate on Goods Receipt 11 Quality Certificates 508 To ensure that all information is complete on the goods receipt screen, choose Check (not shown, but located on the bottom-right side of the screen). A popup appears to inform you that a certificate of type 0008 (inspection certificate) is required. You can now confirm this warning by pressing (Enter) again to save the document. If this error message appeared on the screen in Figure 11.2, the system wouldn’t be allowed to pro- ceed until the incoming certificate was entered in the system.

sections.title: Incoming Inspection Certificate
sections.en: 11.1.6 Incoming Inspection Certificate To bring greater visibility into and improved tracking of incoming quality certificates, there are a few statuses that the warehouse supervisor can use to reflect whether the certificate is in-process or if it has been received. Some of these statuses are Certificate Is Expected, Certificate Filed and Inspected, and Certificate Is Defective. There are two additional system statuses—either a reminder or a more urgent, Escalated warning— that the system automatically sends to a supplier who hasn’t yet sent a quality certifi- cate. Create an incoming inspection certificate by using Transaction QC51 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Incoming  Create. In the screen that appears, enter the purchase order number, followed by the item number of the purchase order, and press (Enter). You’ll see a popup, as shown in Figure 11.7, to inform you that this specific purchase order has a pending incoming certificate. Choose line item 201 (the incoming quality certificate number), and then choose Continue (not shown). The screen in Figure 11.8 appears. Figure 11.7 Missing Incoming Certificate Information Here, and just for the purpose of this example, we define that the certificate is expected against the entered purchase order (see Figure 11.8). In other words, we haven’t updated the status of this certificate. With this certificate status, you can send a reminder to the supplier to expedite certificate submission. Notice that there are several other statuses of an incoming certificate that the business user can manually update, and these should be based on the actual status of the certif- icate. The system automatically updates the status when the user performs certain © 509 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates functions, such as sending a reminder to a supplier or escalating nonreceipt of a certif- icate. Save your entries. Figure 11.8 Certificate Data for Incoming Quality Certificate

sections.title: Incoming Certificate Worklist
sections.en: 11.1.7 Incoming Certificate Worklist There are instances when the company agrees with the supplier to submit the incom- ing quality certificate within an agreed-upon grace period, for example, within three days after goods delivery. This may be the case when results of a few chemical tests take longer to become available, and the supplier takes correspondingly more time to sub- mit the requisite quality certificate. If the supplier fails to submit the quality certificate within the agreed-upon grace period, the system sends a reminder message to the sup- plier about the missing quality certificate. To track the expected or missing incoming certificates you need to follow up on with suppliers, the system provides the intuitive capability to send reminders in the form of emails, as Adobe Acrobat documents, or simply by mail. To access an incoming inspection certificate’s QM worklist, use Transaction QC55 or fol- low menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Incoming  Work- list. Figure 11.9 shows the initial screen in which you enter the relevant parameters so that the system creates a worklist for further action. For this example, provide a specific 11 Quality Certificates 510 Certificate (201), and enter “1” for the status certificate receipt (Status Cert. Receipt), located on the upper half of the screen (not shown here). This status of the expected certificates enables you to send reminders to suppliers. SAP provides preconfigured output formats, such as QM_CERT_REMIND, which you can customize using ABAP resources to meet your company’s specific business needs. Choose Execute (not shown), and the system displays the screen shown in Figure 11.10, which is the QM worklist for an incoming certificate in procurement. Choose the rele- vant items, and then choose Dunning Notices to enable the system to create reminders. Figure 11.9 QM Worklist: Quality Certificates in Procurement Figure 11.10 QM Worklist for Quality Certificates in Procurement © 511 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates You’ll see a message that appears if the deadline to submit the certificate hasn’t yet been exceeded. You can still confirm the message and create the reminder by clicking the Yes button. Figure 11.11 shows the print preview of the incoming certificate receipt reminder. To bring up the print preview of the incoming certificate, select the line item from the worklist, and choose Print Preview. The incoming certificate contains all the relevant details needed to ensure that the supplier sends or submits the needed certificate as soon as possible. Notice that it contains certificate type 0008, which you had previ- ously configured. Figure 11.11 Print Preview of Certificate Receipt Reminder Once the system sends the reminder, it automatically updates the status of the certifi- cate to 3, which denotes that the reminder for the certificate is sent (refer to Figure 11.8). If the supplier still fails to submit the quality certificate after receiving a certificate sub- mission reminder, then the next logical step is to escalate it to reflect the urgency of certificate submission. The urgency exists because the warehouse supervisor is unable to issue the supplier-delivered material to production or maintenance processes, thereby disrupting the logistics, maintenance, or supply chain functions of the com- pany. As in the case of the incoming certificate reminder message, the system sends an escalation message to the defaulting supplier. The steps involved in sending escalation notices to a supplier are the same as those for sending reminders. On the initial parameters selection screen (Transaction QC55), set the Status of the certificate to “3” to denote that the supplier was previously sent the reminder; this time, the system triggers an escalation note during the dunning process. 11 Quality Certificates 512 Note You can also transfer the data of the incoming quality certificate into the inspection lot by using an intermediary document (IDoc). IDocs are beyond the scope of this book.

sections.title: Outgoing Quality Certificates
sections.en: 11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates Be it a business need or a practice to send accompanying outgoing quality certificates for every delivery of the customer’s order to enable sharing quality results for inter- company communication, it’s quick and easy to integrate outgoing quality certificates in QM. Most of the needed groundwork can be successfully undertaken by an SAP func- tional consultant or even by the client’s business users who have sufficient exposure to the SAP S/4HANA system. Outgoing quality certificates integrate with SAP S/4HANA Sales, where goods delivered to the customer are accompanied by the relevant (outgo- ing) quality certificate. A practical approach is to thoroughly assess and evaluate all the areas and processes in which different and diverse usages of outgoing quality certificates are needed and can be implemented. Upon completing this activity and gaining insight into the series of activities involved, you may treat implementing an outgoing quality certificate as a mini project or part of an ongoing business processes improvement. In the sales process, the company needs to engage the person looking after the QM operations to define the certificate type that will accompany its product as a physical document at the time of goods dispatch to the customer. The next step is to define a certificate profile in the system, consisting of the inspection results of the physical and chemical attributes of the product. The quality inspector conducts a quality inspection on the product, consisting of various tests, and eventually records the actual results in the system. The quality inspector prints these actual inspection results on the outgoing quality certificate. This printed outgoing quality certificate is the actual physical docu- ment that the company sends to its customer with each goods dispatch. Let’s now begin with the configuration steps involved in setting up outgoing quality certificates.

sections.title: Define Keys for Certificate Processing
sections.en: 11.2.1 Define Keys for Certificate Processing You have to assign a certificate type when you define a certificate profile for the out- going certificate. You can either use the standard certificate keys available in the SAP S/4HANA system or create a new key. To create a new control key for a certificate type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Certificate Profile  Define Keys for Certificate Pro- cessing. In the popup that opens, double-click Define Certificate Types. The ensuing © 513 11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates screen contains a standard list of available certificate types. As already mentioned, here you can either use an available certificate type or create a new one. In this example, use standard certificate type E23C, which is already available in the SAP S/4HANA system. This is the only configuration step you need for the outgoing quality certificate pro- cess. The next step is to create or update the QM master data that is specific to outgoing quality certificates.

sections.title: Master Data for Outgoing Quality Certificates
sections.en: 11.2.2 Master Data for Outgoing Quality Certificates We begin with QM master data you need to set up for outgoing quality certificates in the SAP S/4HANA system. The required QM master data is the certificate profile and the assignment of the certificate profile, which we’ll discuss in the following sections. Note Make sure that other QM master data elements for the material, such as the relevant inspection type activation in the material master, master inspection characteristics, and inspection plan, are already created and available in the system. Certificate Profile The first step in generating an outgoing quality certificate is to create a certificate pro- file. A certificate profile holds extensive user-defined information about what the com- pany would like to see in the printout of its outgoing quality certificate and how it should be presented. For example, the company may have five different master inspec- tion characteristics for results recording of a material but wants only two master inspection characteristics printed on the outgoing quality certificate. Similarly, you can group together several materials with the same set of master inspection character- istics in one certificate profile, thereby reducing the time and effort you put into main- taining the QM master data. To create a new certificate profile, use Transaction QC01 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Outgoing  Certificate Profile  Create. The initial screen of certificate profile creation appears; for this example, enter “QMCERT01” for the certificate profile Name, and the certificate type given is E23C (not shown). Notice that this is the same certificate type that we just covered in Section 11.2.1. Choose Header Data, enter a short description of the certificate profile (not shown), and the screen in Figure 11.12 appears. Assign an SAPscript form that the system will use as an output layout. For this example, we use the standard SAPscript that SAP delivers, which is QM_QCERT_01. You can engage an ABAP resource to configure and make available a company-specific printout (or output) of the certificate. For example, the outgoing quality certificate’s script may contain the company’s logo, as well as the offi- cial address and specific text that the company would like to appear on the certificate. 11 Quality Certificates 514 Figure 11.12 Certificate Profile Select the Accepted Lots Only checkbox, which means that the system allows printout of only outgoing quality certificates for which the usage decision is recorded as accepted. This ensures that inspection lots with rejected usage decisions are neither inadvertently printed nor circulated. You can also restrict the inspection type for which the certificate profile becomes avail- able, but this isn’t necessary or mandatory. It just provides additional control function- ality. For this example, we restrict the certificate profile Inspection Lot Origin to 89 only (not shown but located further down the same screen). Choose the Materials button to see the screen in Figure 11.13, where you assign the material (or materials) with its respective inspection origin and inspection types, which use certificate profile QMCERT01. Notice the Accptd checkbox, used to ensure that the system uses only accepted inspec- tion lots of materials with accepted usage decisions. In addition, notice that in the very last column, Min QScore, you can even control the minimum quality score an inspec- tion lot must have (after its usage decision) for the system to allow creation of an outgo- ing quality certificate. This is another control criterion that companies often use in their outgoing quality certificate processing. Here, you can enter several materials with the same master inspection characteristics and different inspection types, thus saving time and effort in the master data maintenance required for outgoing quality certificates. © 515 11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates Figure 11.13 Material Assignment to Certificate Profile For this example, assign Material “QM001” with its inspection Origin and Insp. Type as “89”, and select the Accptd checkbox. Choose Continue, which takes you back to the screen in Figure 11.12. Choose Characteristics, and this leads to the screen in Figure 11.14, which shows the characteristic overview of the certificate profile. Here, you assign all the master inspection characteristics required on printout/output of an outgoing qual- ity certificate. Enter previously created master inspection characteristics “QMHT10”, “PURITY”, and “VISINSP”, and make additional selections with respect to these master inspection characteristics. Here, you have complete control over how you would like the output of an outgoing quality certificate to look. Further, you also have the option to output the actual value of the results or its upper or lower ranges, or even average results. Scroll to the right side of the screen in Figure 11.14, and the screen in Figure 11.15 appears. Here, the system offers further controls and options for the certificate’s output, including decimal places, actual value or average value of the master inspection characteristic, and whether the master inspection characteristic description needs to be different (in the certificate’s output) than what’s maintained in the SAP S/4HANA system. 11 Quality Certificates 516 Figure 11.14 Characteristics Data of Certificate Profile After entering master inspection characteristics with the requisite details, choose Back and then Release Profile, and save the certificate profile. A released certificate profile can always be locked if there is any such business need. Choose the lock to achieve this. If the certificate profile is already released, then the icon changes to Block Profile, as shown earlier in Figure 11.12. Figure 11.15 Certification Profile Certificate Profile Assignment After certificate profile creation, you need to assign it to either a material or group of materials or to a material-customer combination. To create a new assignment for the certificate profile, use Transaction QC15 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Outgoing  Certificate Profile  Assignment  Create. Figure 11.16 shows the initial screen for the assignment of the certificate profile. The Assignment type QCA1 is standard; once you enter it, choose Key from the Edit menu © 517 11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates bar located on the top of the screen (or simply press (Enter)) to select the key combina- tion. For this example, choose Material, and press (Enter), which leads to the screen in Figure 11.17. Figure 11.16 Assignment of Certificate Profile Figure 11.17 Assignment of Materials to Certificate Profile In Figure 11.17, select the same material, QM001; the certificate profile, QMCERT01; the certificate type, E23C; and the certificate profile version, which is 1.

sections.title: Business Processes in Outgoing Quality Certificates
