Choose Save to save the scheduling details. Then, a message appears to confirm that the background job for exception Z015 has been successfully planned. This ends our discussion on how to set up EWS. The next section shows how EWS works in the system when the user performs day-to-day business functions, and how the sys- tem alerts the user who sets up EWS when an exception occurs. The business users can continue to perform and report their daily activities in the system, such as performing goods receipts against purchase orders, reporting daily production with scrap percent- age, and recording the quality results of inspection lots. 17 Early Warning System 766

sections.title: Early Warning System in Action
sections.en: 17.4 Early Warning System in Action For this example, the procurement supervisor creates a purchase order for material QM003 and for supplier 17300006. The warehouse supervisor receives the partial pur- chase order quantity of 200 PC in the system. The next step is to perform a quality inspection that includes the results recording and usage decision. The details recorded in the usage decision for the rejected material form the basis of the EWS alert. Rejected material QM003, in a quantity greater than 50 PC, causes EWS to alert the person who set it up. For this example, the alert is sent as a popup, and an email is sent to your SAP inbox. To create a new purchase order, use Transaction ME21N (see Figure 17.9 1). Enter the Material “QM003”, Plant “1710” (not shown), and Supplier “17300006”. Press (Enter). Save the purchase order, and, for this example, the system generates purchase order number 4500001818. Figure 17.9 Purchase Order and Goods Receipt The next step is to record goods receipt against the purchase order. For this, use Trans- action MIGO. Enter purchase order number “4500001818”, and press (Enter). In the Quantity field, enter the partial procurement quantity as “200” PC, and enter storage location “171A” (not shown). Save the goods receipt for purchase order number 4500001818 by pressing (Ctrl)+(S) 2. © 767 17.4 Early Warning System in Action On goods receipt, the system creates an inspection lot. Because this material (QM003) will undergo quality inspection, first record results using Transaction QE01 against the inspection lot. Finally, the last step is to undertake a usage decision using Transaction QE11 and reject the material by returning the entire quantity of 200 PC back to the supplier (see the Return Posting field in Figure 17.10, in which you enter “200” PC). On return delivery, the system opens a popup to ask for a Reason for Mvmt. (movement). A reason for movement enables the quality controller to specify the reason for rejecting or return- ing the material back to the supplier. Select 0001 to denote a defective material, enter a short text, press (Enter), and then save the usage decision. Figure 17.10 Return Delivery to Supplier for Defective Material As soon as you save the usage decision and choose Back, the system issues a popup message (see Figure 17.11) to alert you of the deviation (exception) that’s occurred. Figure 17.11 Popup Alert Issued by EWS 17 Early Warning System 768 Figure 17.11 shows that an exception (deviation) has occurred: the quantity rejected for material QM003 during the usage decision was greater than 50 PC, leading to the (popup) alert. Notice that in the popup, the system brings up the same text, Suppliers’ Rejections, that we defined during the initial stages of setting up EWS. The system also delivers the same exception message in the SAP inbox. You can use Transaction SBWP to check your inbox for unread documents that contain EWS alerts too. It’s not always possible to keep track of all the EWS popups, so it makes sense to go to the SAP inbox periodically and attend to your alerts (see Figure 17.12). Figure 17.12 SAP Inbox Tips and Tricks While maintaining scheduling to check for individual exceptions or exception group- ing, make sure to eliminate duplication of information so that the system doesn’t pres- ent the same information repeatedly—first in an individual exception and then in an exception grouping. This is achieved by adopting a well-thought-out approach prior to setting up EWS—for example, by making a list of all the important materials for which you want to monitor parameters for deviations.

sections.title: Exception Analysis
sections.en: 17.5 Exception Analysis Finally, we’ll show you how to analyze exceptions with EWS in the QM information sys- tem. Although alert monitoring is certainly a valuable EWS tool to promptly alert you about any deviations and exceptions, often you’re required to have detailed informa- tion on the exceptions. Fortunately, EWS is supported by QM, which ensures that com- prehensive details related to all exceptions are instantly available. © 769 17.5 Exception Analysis Follow menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warning System  Exception Analysis or use Transaction MCYL to get to the initial screen for exception selection. For this example, enter Exception “Z015” for analysis (see Figure 17.13). Figure 17.13 Exception Analysis Figure 17.14 Exception Analysis Report of EWS for Material QM003 17 Early Warning System 770 Choose Execute, and the system displays the selection parameter screen. Enter “QM003” for the Material field. When you execute the exception analysis report by pressing (F8) or choosing Execute (not shown), the system displays the results, as shown in Figure 17.14. This exception analysis shows the defined key figure with its data as separate columns. Further, the color is red for the entire row of the Material column, as we originally defined in Figure 17.5. As with all standard analysis reports, you can go to the menu and choose More  Extras  Inspection Lot Drilldown to view the inspection lot’s details and other key figures.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 17.6 Summary This chapter explained how quickly and easily a business process owner in any relevant area of work can set up EWS without any extensive functional or technical knowledge. EWS alerts can be modified, deleted, or updated anytime, as deemed necessary to reflect the business need. The next chapter covers QM reporting in the SAP S/4HANA system. ©

sections.title: The Basics of Reporting
sections.en: 18.1 The Basics of Reporting To take full advantage of your SAP S/4HANA system, it’s essential that you become familiar with the toolbars and other features frequently available for use in reports. Because these functions are the same in all the information systems and analyses, you’ll begin to navigate faster and be able to quickly get to your desired information or even find tips and tricks to manage the display and availability of data as needed. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 772 In the next sections, you’ll learn how to leverage the standard reports and standard analyses in QM. Then, we’ll show you how to use the QM Cockpit for Evaluations. After that, we’ll devote a significant portion of this chapter to covering SAP Fiori apps for QM. As new SAP Fiori apps are constantly added with each SAP S/4HANA release, we also cover how to find and explore them and begin taking advantage of the business bene- fits they offer.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Selection
sections.en: 18.1.1 Inspection Lot Selection When we say inspection lot selection, we’re talking about an information system that consists of the most up-to-date information about a specific object and is based on the transactions that the business user has performed as part of the business process. For example, when you execute the inspection lot selection, the system displays the cur- rent status of various inspection lots, including those for which results recording or a usage decision has happened. If you run the same report again after six hours, for example, when the business user has recorded more results or a usage decision, the system shows up-to-date (and different) information. This information helps to reflect the accurate and up-to-date status of various activities and business processes. We’ve divided the large number of available options for parameters selection into sev- eral figures in the following sections for ease of understanding and comprehension. Figure 18.1 Inspection Lot Selection © 773 18.1 The Basics of Reporting Figure 18.1 shows Transaction QA33 (Inspection Lot Selection). Here, you have several options to choose from in the Inspection Lot Selection area and in Dynamic Selections, where the system brings up far greater options to choose from. For example, in the Inspection Lot Selection area, you won’t see the option to enter the number of a pur- chase order for which you’d like to see inspection lots. For this option, choose …Pro- curement from Dynamic Selections, and the system brings up options to choose procurement-relevant parameters. The same is the case for production-related or SAP S/4HANA Sales-related inspection lots.

sections.title: Multiple Selection
sections.en: 18.1.2 Multiple Selection You may have noticed that on the selection screen of a report, an option is available to enter any parameter in a range or an interval. For example, for the Plant field in Figure 18.1, you can enter only a selection interval. But what if you want to exclude a certain plant within the plant range on the selection screen, or include two plants in addition to those given in the plant interval? All of this and several other options are available via the Multiple Selection option that’s available in all information systems and reports of all components. Choose Multiple Selection in Figure 18.1 for Material. In the resulting screen, four tabs allow you to include or exclude single values or even an entire range (see Figure 18.2). Figure 18.2 Multiple Selection 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 774 You can enter information in each of the four tabs, and the ensuing output (report) will show the desired results. You’ll also find available icons to further facilitate the busi- ness user, such as copying data from a clipboard, adding or deleting a line within the values, or using the Multiple Selection option. The Multiple Selection icon enables the user to select multiple values by selecting the requisite checkboxes.

sections.title: Maintain Selection
sections.en: 18.1.3 Maintain Selection A frequently used and available option is Define Selection Options. When you choose Define Selection Options (the leaf icon; see Figure 18.2), the Define Selection Options screen appears. To take a shortcut to this screen, double-click the relevant field of the selection screen of any report (see Figure 18.3). Figure 18.3 Define Selection Options

sections.title: Maintain Variant
sections.en: 18.1.4 Maintain Variant Maintaining a variant in SAP is similar to saving a layout, which is then available for repeated use when needed. You can also set a variant as default by managing your lay- out options. For example, say that when you use the report for quality scores history, you always use plant 1000 and the date range of 30 days from today. Instead of enter- ing these parameters every time you run the report, you can save these details as a vari- ant, which you can then subsequently select. There are two areas where you can maintain variants. The first one is on the Initial Parameters Selection screen of any report, information system, or analysis when defin- ing the selection parameters. Simply enter the information once in the parameters © 775 18.1 The Basics of Reporting selection screen, and proceed to save the variant by choosing More  Goto  Variants  Save as Variant. On the Variant Attributes screen that appears, give the variant a name and a short description, and then choose whether to make each field required, hidden, or protected from data entry. With the variant saved, the next time you need to choose More  Goto  Variants  Get the Variant. You can also delete incorrect or unwanted vari- ants. The second option to save a variant is when you’ve already executed an analysis or a report. The system displays all listed fields, and you’ve made your required changes— for example, applying any filter set, any sort of a column in ascending or descending order, or any aggregation. You can then choose More  Select Layout, and then select the Save Layout option from the dropdown. In the ensuing popup, enter the name of the layout and a short description. Here, again, you can change or delete the saved layouts if needed.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Selection Worklist
sections.en: 18.1.5 Inspection Lot Selection Worklist When you execute the report by pressing (F8) or choosing Execute, a report such as the one shown in Figure 18.4 appears, which is for the Inspection Lot Selection Worklist. In this report, you’ll explore a few important options that are available, such as aggrega- tion, setting a filter, or viewing the information in a graphical presentation. However, some of the common and obvious options, such as sorting in ascending or descending order of information and changing or displaying objects, aren’t covered. Figure 18.4 Worklist for Inspection Lots 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 776 Fields Selection Figure 18.4 displays only a limited number of columns and amount of information, whereas you can display and manipulate an enormous amount of information and even save the display layout if you routinely use it. When you choose More  Change Layout in Figure 18.4, the Change Layout screen appears, as shown in Figure 18.5 1. The columns or fields already displayed in the report are shown on the left side, whereas the fields or columns that you can display in a report are shown on the right side of the Change Layout screen. To further facilitate the user selecting fields, you can use several filters. A filter further groups together relevant fields so that it’s easier for a business user to choose and display the desired fields in the report. For this example, use the Quantities filter 2, and then only quantity-relevant fields are available for users to choose from. You can choose the relevant field in 2 and move it with the left- arrow icon so that the system displays the content in the report. Figure 18.5 Change Layout Tips and Tricks In Figure 18.4, you can place the cursor on any column and right-click to display all the available options—not just for that column, but for the entire report. © 777 18.1 The Basics of Reporting Aggregation Referring to Figure 18.4 again, you can aggregate or sum up (total) any key figure or quantity. With the Total option already in place for a key figure as shown in Figure 18.6 1, you can then use the Subtotal option to subtotal any number of characteristics and key figures 2. Figure 18.6 Aggregation In Figure 18.6 1, first use the Total option on the Unrestricted-Use Stock and Lot Qty columns by selecting them and then choosing Total. Then, select two individual columns—Material and Plant—in succession, followed by the Lot Qty column, and choose the Subtotal icon. The system displays the various summation levels with square dots on the right side. A single dot denotes the summation at the plant level, two dots for the material, and three dots for the inspection lot quantity total (and also unrestricted-use quantity). You can then also choose the individual summation level by clicking the Summation icon located at the bottom of the screen 2. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 778

sections.title: Filter Settings
sections.en: 18.1.6 Filter Settings You’ll sometimes need to filter out some information in a report so that the system dis- plays only the desired information. Refer to Figure 18.4 once again. In Figure 18.7, select the Insp. Lot Qty column, and then choose Set Filter to set the filter. Figure 18.7 Filter Settings In Figure 18.8, you can either double-click the Target Quantity field or use Define Selec- tion Options, which brings up the popup window. Select the Greater than or Equal To option, and choose Continue, which again brings up Figure 18.8. Figure 18.8 Define Selection Options to Use in Filter Settings © 779 18.1 The Basics of Reporting Enter “50” in the Inspection Lot Quantity field so that the report now shows only target quantities equal to or greater than 50, as shown in Figure 18.9. Here, you can see that the filter is in place by a little arrow pointing downward on the Insp. Lot Quantity col- umn. The red arrows (shown back in Figure 18.6) indicate that the list is sorted in descending (upward red arrow) or ascending (downward red arrow) order. Figure 18.9 Active Filter

sections.title: Download
sections.en: 18.1.7 Download When you execute a report or conduct a standard analysis, you can also download the information in one of the several available forms by right-clicking any column, fol- lowed by choosing Spreadsheet. You can also send the information as an email attach- ment or even perform an ABC analysis in the information system, although this option is also available in the standard analysis reports.

sections.title: Copy Selective Data to Microsoft Excel
sections.en: 18.1.8 Copy Selective Data to Microsoft Excel You can copy selected data if you don’t want to download the full data of your SAP S/4HANA system into Microsoft Excel or a different format. Press (Ctrl)+(Y) to select fields or con- tent within the report. This enables block selection, in which you select the block of fields you want to copy. Then, press (Ctrl)+(C) to copy the data. In Microsoft Excel or another program (e.g., Notepad or Microsoft Word), press (Ctrl)+(P) to paste the copied data.

sections.title: Print
sections.en: 18.1.9 Print To access the print option, choose the Print Preview icon within a report. It’s important to note that all parameters used in the generation of the report in the information sys- tem also become part of the printout, including filters and the like. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 780

sections.title: ABC Analysis
sections.en: 18.1.10 ABC Analysis As already mentioned earlier, you can also perform an ABC analysis in the quality inspection worklist. Access Figure 18.10 by first clicking the Inspection Lot Quantity col- umn, followed by clicking the ABC Analysis icon, located in the top menu bar shown in Figure 18.4. Figure 18.10 shows the A, B, and C divisions of inspection lot quantities based on the user-defined division criteria of 70%, 20%, and 10%, respectively. As discussed in the beginning of this chapter, while standard reports and SAP Fiori apps provide real-time information, the standard analyses are more statistical in nature. The ABC analysis we just discussed is based on real-time reporting; Section 18.2.5 will dis- cuss the ABC analysis from a statistical perspective. Figure 18.10 ABC Analysis

sections.title: Standard Analyses
sections.en: 18.2 Standard Analyses The standard analyses enable users to draw information from the available standard information (info) structures in the SAP S/4HANA system. The difference between reports such as Inspection Lot Selection and standard analyses is that in information systems, the information is dynamic and changes when the business user performs the relevant business functions. In standard analyses, the system draws from historical information to enable the business user to make better business decisions. In other words, data and information from information systems flow into analyses. © 781 18.2 Standard Analyses Note You can access standard analyses for all of the logistics areas of the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem from the central location in the Logistics Controlling node of the SAP menu via Logistics  Logistics Controlling. You can then navigate to the relevant area’s standard analyses option. The SAP S/ 4HANA areas for which the standard analyses are available are logistics, QM, inventory controlling, purchasing, sales, shop floor control, shipment, and plant maintenance (PM). In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the standard analyses of QM. We’ll also show a few features and functionalities available only in analyses and not in informa- tion systems, such as time-series analysis and ABC analysis.

With each division, there are further logical subdivisions for each analysis type, such as analysis type for inspection lot, inspection characteristics, or notifications. For example, if you want an overview of quantities of inspection characteristics of a material, you use Transaction MCXD. For this example, the characteristic is the material, and all of the key figures in Figure 18.15 are for the month of December 2023 (12/2023). You can also download the data or send it via email. sections.title: Other Info Structures
sections.en: 18.2.4 Other Info Structures You can also navigate to the Info structure screen within the standard analysis, as shown in Figure 18.16. To do so, choose the Other Info Structure icon, and in the ensuing popup, enter the name of the new info structure or use the dropdown menu to select one. If you have any self-defined info structures, then these too will be available for selection. Figure 18.16 Other Info Structures

sections.title: Standard Analysis: ABC Analysis
sections.en: 18.2.5 Standard Analysis: ABC Analysis Access Figure 18.17 for the standard analysis of suppliers using Transaction MCVD. Select the ValueOverTol (values over tolerance) key figure by clicking it and choosing Edit  ABC analysis from the menu bar. In the popup that appears, choose Total Val- ueUndTol (%) as the strategy for ABC analysis, as shown in Figure 18.18, and choose Con- tinue. © 787 18.2 Standard Analyses Figure 18.17 ABC Analysis Figure 18.18 ABC Analysis for Values under Tolerance The options in ABC analysis are as follows:  Total ValueOverTol (%) The total value of all the characteristics under or over tolerance are divided up by the defined percentage.  Number Suppliers (%) The number of suppliers is divided up by the defined percentage.  Valueover Tol (Absolute) The actual number of characteristics with values under or over the defined tolerance is divided up into A, B, or C segments.  Number Inspection Characteristic The number of master inspection characteristics is divided up into A, B, or C seg- ments. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 788 ABC analysis enables you to select the right strategy and then divides the key figures into the top three groupings. You also have the flexibility to define the percentage of a key figure to be listed in the A, B, or C segments. In Figure 18.18, you have the flexibility to overwrite the system-suggested segment sizes of A, B, or C. For this example, enter “40” for A Segment, “50” for B Segment, and “10” for C Segment (not shown). These three entries mean that the system will divide and display the Total ValueOverTol (%) in such a way that the top 40% will be catego- rized in segment A, the next 50% in segment B, and the bottom 10% in segment C, in sequential order. Choose Calculate (not shown) to open SAP Business Graphics, as shown in Figure 18.19. Figure 18.19 Graphical Representation: ABC Analysis Figure 18.19 shows the graphical representation of ABC analysis. The blue vertical bars denote the A, B, or C segment of characteristic values exceeding tolerances, and the yel- low bars represent the number of suppliers who supplied the material that exceeded the tolerance limits.

sections.title: Standard Analysis: Time Series
sections.en: 18.2.6 Standard Analysis: Time Series Access the screen in Figure 18.20 using Transaction MCVD, choose MeanVal.QScore, and then choose Time Series (not shown) to open the Time Series dialog box. A time series denotes the breakdown of a key figure of a characteristic, which in this case is Inspection Type. © 789

sections.title: QM Cockpit for Evaluations
sections.en: 18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations Figure 18.20 Time Series of Mean Value 18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations The QM Cockpit for Evaluations enables the business user to have access to all the important information and data without using different information systems or navi- gating to different reports or analyses. The QM Cockpit for Evaluations provides the required information not only in tabular form but also in graphical form. It also enables the business user to divide up the cockpit into various sections to have greater visibility of information for comparison and analysis purposes. To access the QM Cockpit for Evaluations, use Transaction QGA4 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Control  Evaluation of Original Documents  General QM Evaluations (see Figure 18.21). This screen appears blank until you make the necessary selections, for which you need to follow these steps: 1. From the dropdown menu, choose whether you want to evaluate inspection lots, components, or notifications. 2. Choose Selection  Additional Selection (or press (F7)), and the system opens a popup for you to choose whether you want inspection lots with defects or without them. You can also choose to view archived data. Choose 01 Insp. Lot Selection w/o Defects (Online). 3. In the Inspection Lot Selection screen, you can define the selection parameters, such as plant 1100 and inspection type 01. You also have to define the grouping layout, which is Standard, as well as the number of views (sections) that you want to see appear in the QM Cockpit for Evaluations. For example, if you select 3 in Views (not shown), then the system divides up the right side of the QM Cockpit for Evaluations into three sections. For this example, choose a single view, and in the Grouping Lay- out field (not shown), enter “1STANDARD”, which is the standard layout available. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 790 Figure 18.21 QM Cockpit for Evaluations 4. Choose Execute. This brings up the inspection lots that you see in Figure 18.22. 5. In Figure 18.22, under the Aggregated Objects column, you see that the highest level is Inspection Lots, followed by Characteristics, and finally Single Values (not shown). You can individually select the desired objects from the aggregated list, or choose them all. For this example, choose Select Entire Level, and then from the dropdown that appears, choose Characteristics (not shown). The system selects all characteris- tics of all inspection lots. Figure 18.22 Inspection Lots Worklist in QM Cockpit for Evaluations © 791 18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations 6. The data and information that you see on the right side of Figure 18.23 appears after you choose Create View  Table  Characteristics Table (refer to Figure 18.22 again). With data already available in the form of a table, you can leverage available data manipulation options, such as aggregation, total, subtotal, filter, and graphical pre- sentation. 7. Figure 18.24 appears after you choose Select Entire Level. This time, choose Single Values, and then choose Create View  Graphic  Histogram. Notice the large number of options available to view the graph and its associated key figures in various lay- outs and formats. These options are available when you choose Graphic Settings from the menu bar located just above the graph. Figure 18.23 Key Figures Display Figure 18.24 Graphical Representation in QM Cockpit for Evaluations 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 792

sections.title: SAP Fiori Applications
sections.en: 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the SAP Fiori apps of QM, such as Inspec- tion Lot Analytics, Quality Technician Overview, Quality Engineer Overview, Manage Control Charts, and Results History, among others.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Analytics
sections.en: 18.4.1 Inspection Lot Analytics The Inspection Lot Analytics app provides insights into several important key perfor- mance indicators (KPIs) of inspection lots for which usage decisions have already been made in the past year (365 days). The analysis can be based on time, inspection type, material, or plant. You can view the KPIs in different ways by choosing from the follow- ing options:  Rejection Rate by Time Series  Rejection Rate by Inspection Type  Rejection Rate by Material and Plant  Accepted and Rejected Lots by Time Series  Accepted and Rejected Lots by Inspection Type  Accepted and Rejected Lots by Material and Plant  Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Time Series  Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Inspection Type  Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Material and Plant  Skip Rate by Time Series  Skip Rate by Inspection Type  Skip Rate by Material and Plant Figure 18.25 shows the Inspection Lot Analytics app. The dropdown on the left side enables you to choose a specific KPI to analyze in a specific way (see preceding list). Here, along with graphical display, you can also view data a columnar form that is asso- ciated with a graph. The graphs show a 44.44% rejection rate of inspection lots that were inspected in the month of March of 2024, and five results recordings of inspection lots were skipped due to the dynamic modification rule in place. Choose Show Mini Tiles located at the top-right side of Figure 18.25, and the screen in Figure 18.26 appears. The top half of Figure 18.26 shows three mini tiles, including mean scores of inspections for a given month, as well as the frequencies with which materials are inspected. Choose any of the mini tiles to navigate to the detailed analytics of that KPI. You can also use the Jump To dropdown to jump to other associated apps, such as Inspection Lot Detailed Analysis, which we’ll cover in Section 18.4.17. © 793 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications Figure 18.25 Inspection Lot Analytics Figure 18.26 Mini Tiles Choose the filter that reads Previous 365 days in Figure 18.26, which brings up the screen in Figure 18.27. Figure 18.27 shows the options to choose a time period other than one year, which is the default time period for this app. A user-defined time period can also be created, saved, and used when needed. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 794 Figure 18.27 Filters Figure 18.28 shows the option to choose from various graph types, including heat map, as shown in this example. The option to display data in tabular or columnar form (or both) is also available. It’s also possible to navigate to other associated SAP Fiori apps, such as Inspection Lot Detailed Analytics and Manage Inspection Lots, from this screen by clicking the Jump To dropdown. Figure 18.28 Graph Options © 795 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications

sections.title: Quality Level History
sections.en: 18.4.2 Quality Level History Figure 18.29 shows the Quality Level History app, showing the various dynamic modifi- cation rules applied on various inspection lots and how they changed the inspection stages from normal to reduced or vice versa (shown in the X-axis). The KPI is displayed in the following ways (via dropdown selection):  Inspection Stages by Inspection Lots and Characteristics  Skip History: Inspection Lots and Characteristics  Inspection Severities by Inspection Lots and Characteristics  List: Inspection Lots and Characteristics Recall from Chapter 3 that dynamic modification rules were set at the inspection lot level (and not at the characteristics level); the graphs in this figure reflect that setting. Figure 18.29 Quality Level History App

sections.title: Record Inspection Results
sections.en: 18.4.3 Record Inspection Results Figure 18.30 shows the Record Inspection Results app. With this app, it’s possible to record the results of characteristics flexibly and effectively. For example, you can choose multiple inspection lots at one time and record the results centrally. On record- ing results for the inspection lots, the app automatically valuates characteristics according to valuation modes. Valuation modes define the rules for accepting or reject- ing a characteristic and are discussed in detail in Chapter 3. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 796 Figure 18.30 Record Inspection Results The Record Inspection Results app offers the following valuation modes:  Valuation mode 100 When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, the valuation occurs when an inspection plan consists of a sample size and acceptance number. The acceptance number and the number of nonconforming units are compared.  Valuation mode 400 When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, the valuation occurs when a code (selected set) is assigned to a characteristic in an inspection plan.  Valuation mode 500 When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, users can manually valuate the characteristics in the inspection plan. This valuation mode also applies to char- acteristics in inspection plans that are without sampling procedures.  Valuation mode 700 When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, the valuation occurs when the tolerance range is specified for characteristics in an inspection plan. This app also shows long-term and open characteristics from different dimensions: inspection lot, operation, sample, and master inspection characteristic. Long-term characteristic refers to a criterion for which you can also record results after comple- tion of the short-term inspection. Figure 18.31 shows the options to apply additional filters that aren’t displayed on the main screen of an app. To apply additional filters, choose Adapt Filters in Figure 18.30, and the screen in Figure 18.31 appears. The option to use additional filters is available in almost all SAP Fiori apps. © 797 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications Figure 18.31 Additional Filters

sections.title: Results History
sections.en: 18.4.4 Results History Figure 18.32 shows the Results History app. With this app, it’s possible to display the results history for an inspection plan characteristic or a master inspection characteris- tic. The valuation of a characteristic is shown as a graphic for the selected inspection lots to compare inspection results over a longer period of time. The following are some of the other features available in this app:  Only displaying the results history for quantitative characteristics is possible.  In the list, you can use the Settings to specify the grouping characteristics according to which the inspection lot results are summarized. The grouping characteristics are indicated by the suffix (Characteristic) or (Char).  The individually selected inspection lot results are summarized as one aggregated object according to whether they match the grouping characteristics. If, for example, you select only the material and the master inspection characteristic as grouping characteristics, all inspection lot results for a master inspection characteristic and material are aggregated in one row of the list. If you select the material, supplier, and master inspection characteristic as the grouping characteristic, all inspection lot results for a material-supplier combination and master inspection characteristic are aggregated in one row of the list. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 798 Figure 18.32 Results History Figure 18.33 shows the mean values of a single master inspection characteristic recorded in various inspection lots. The key figures for the selected inspection lot results are calculated at the aggregation level. The results of a row in the list are dis- played as a graphic. This is the run chart of the sample mean values with their upper and lower tolerance limits. Choose Single Values in Figure 18.33, and the screen in Figure 18.34 appears. The upper half of the screen in Figure 18.34 shows the data points in graphical form, and the lower half lists all the inspection lots that make up the data points shown in the graph. You can make a flexible selection from all selected inspection lot results, and the graphic is adapted accordingly. Figure 18.33 Mean Values of Inspection Results © 799 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications Figure 18.34 Individual Results or Single Values

sections.title: Quality Technician Overview
sections.en: 18.4.5 Quality Technician Overview Figure 18.35 shows the Quality Technician Overview app and consists of four KPIs that are displayed as cards. Information displayed as cards not only provides an overview of important KPIs but also allows a quality technician to focus on the most important tasks and to view, filter, and react to information quickly. Figure 18.35 Quality Technician Overview 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 800 The cards show the most important information ranked according to relevance. For example, on the Inspection Lots without Inspection Plan card, you can see the number of inspection lots without an inspection plan in the header—which in this example is 10 such inspection lots—followed by a list of inspection lots that are sorted based on their creation dates. It’s also possible to customize the overview page by rearranging, hiding, or showing cards via drag and drop. To hide a card, proceed as follows:  In the header bar, select the User icon, and then select Manage Cards. Use the switch control to hide or show the relevant card. Select OK.  To reset the view to the default settings, select Restore in the Manage Cards window. You can also apply a filter to the displayed information, which will affect all relevant cards. For example, you can filter the content of all cards per plant or inspection lot ori- gin. SAP delivers a standard filter variant that you can use immediately. It contains some predefined values for the filter bar. It’s also possible to make a self-defined vari- ant by selecting the Select Variant dropdown arrow. You can also customize the filter by selecting Adapt Filters. Here are some additional details about the various cards:  Inspection Lots Without Inspection Plan This card shows inspection lots without an inspection plan, sorted by creation date. Selecting the header or clicking it leads to the Manage Inspection Lots app, whereas selecting an item leads to the Change Inspection Lot screen.  Inspection Lots with Open Results Recording, No Inspection Points This card shows the total number of inspection lots for which results recording hasn’t started or is in process. Selecting the header leads to the Record Inspection Results app. The column chart shows you the number of inspection lots by end date of inspection. Selecting a column also leads to the Record Inspection Results app, but here the inspection lots are filtered based on the end date of inspection.  Inspection Lots with Open Results Recording for Inspection Points This card shows the total number of inspection lots for which results recording hasn’t started or is still in process. Selecting the header takes you to the Record Results for Inspection Points app. The column chart shows the number of inspection lots by inspection end date. Selecting a column also leads to the Record Results for Inspection Points app, but the inspection lots are now filtered based on the end date of inspection.  My Tasks Shows the quality tasks assigned to you that are in either Created or In Process Sta- tus, sorted according to the planned end date. Selecting the header takes you to the Process Quality Tasks app, whereas selecting an item takes you to the Quality Tasks screen. Quality tasks need to be created in the Manage Defects app, and these quality tasks also need to be assigned to the relevant users for them to appear in the My Tasks card. © 801 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications

sections.title: Quality Engineer Overview
sections.en: 18.4.6 Quality Engineer Overview The Quality Engineer Overview app shows the most important information and tasks related to inspection management all in a single page. Just like the Quality Technician Overview app, the information is displayed on a set of cards, thereby allowing a quality engineer to focus on the most important tasks and to view, filter, and react to informa- tion quickly. The cards show you the most important information ranked according to relevance. For example, on the Inspection Lots without Usage Decision card, you can see the num- ber of inspection lots without a usage decision in the header, followed by a donut chart that shows the percentage distribution of inspection lots based on their results record- ing status. You can then decide to make usage decisions for all inspection lots without a usage decision or for those inspection lots with a particular result recording status. You can customize the overview page by rearranging cards and by hiding or showing them. You can drag and drop cards to rearrange them. To hide a card, proceed as fol- lows: In the header bar, select the User icon and select Manage Cards. Use the switch control to hide or show the relevant card. Select OK. To reset the view to the default set- tings, select Restore in the Manage Cards window. You can also apply a filter to the dis- played information, which will affect all relevant cards. For example, you can filter the content of all cards per plant or inspection lot origin. SAP delivers a standard filter variant that can be used immediately. It contains some predefined values for the filter bar. It’s also possible to make your own variant by selecting the Select Variant dropdown arrow. You can also customize the filter by selecting Adapt Filter. Figure 18.36 and Figure 18.37 show the cards that appear in the Quality Engineer Over- view app, and Table 18.2 describes them. Figure 18.36 Quality Engineer Overview App (1/2) 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 802 Figure 18.37 Quality Engineer Overview App (2/2) Card Name Details Inspection Lots without Inspection Plan  Shows inspection lots without an inspection plan and are sorted by creation date.  Selecting the header leads to the Manage Inspection Lots app, while selecting an item takes you to the Change Inspection Lot app. Inspection Lots without Usage Deci- sion  Shows the total number of inspection lots without a usage deci- sion.  Selecting the header navigates to the Manage Usage Decisions app.  The donut chart is divided based on the results recording status.  Selecting a section of the donut chart also leads to the Manage Usage Decisions app, but the inspection lots are now filtered based on the results recording status of the selected section. The quick usage decision sets the usage deci- sion code that was previously defined as the default. Table 18.2 Quality Engineer Overview SAP Fiori App Cards © 803 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications Inspection Severity of Next Inspection Stage  Shows the number of quality levels created for inspection lots and characteristics.  The column chart shows you the number of quality levels by inspection severity.  Selecting the header leads to the Manage Quality Levels app.  Selecting a column also leads to the Manage Quality Levels app, but the quality levels for inspection lots and characteristics are now fil- tered based on inspection severity. Quality Levels for Inspection Lots  Shows the number of quality levels created for inspection lots.  The donut chart is divided based on skip status.  Selecting the header takes you to the Manage Quality Levels app.  Selecting a section of the donut chart also takes you to the Manage Quality Levels app, but the quality levels for inspection lots are now filtered based on skip status. Quality Levels for Characteristics  Shows the number of quality levels created for characteristics.  The donut chart is divided based on skip status.  Selecting the header leads to the Manage Quality Levels app.  Selecting a section of the donut chart also takes you to the Manage Quality Levels app, but the quality levels for characteristics are now filtered based on skip status. Action Limit Violations  Shows you the number of times action limits (or tolerance limits) have been violated in the past seven days.  The column chart shows the number of violations either by work center or by material.  Selecting the header takes you to the Manage Control Charts app, where all the new and active control charts with violations are dis- played.  Selecting a column also takes you to the Manage Control Charts app, but the new and active control charts with violations are now filtered based on work center or material. Quality Tasks by Planned End  Shows you the number of open quality tasks with a planned end date in the past and in the next 30 calendar days.  The column chart shows you the number of open quality tasks based on the planned end date.  Selecting the header takes you to the Manage Quality Tasks app, where all quality tasks with either the Created or In Process status and with a planned end date in the past and in the next 30 calendar days are displayed.  Selecting a column also takes you to the Manage Quality Tasks app, but the open quality tasks are now filtered based on the planned end date. sections.title: Manage Usage Decisions
sections.en: 18.4.7 Manage Usage Decisions Figure 18.38 shows the Manage Usage Decision app, wherein you can display inspection lots, as well as manage usage decisions for each inspection lot. For inspection lots for which a usage decision has been made, you can view or change that usage decision. For inspection lots for which a usage decision hasn’t been made, you can make a usage decision. Other key features of this app are as follows:  View inspection lots based on filter criteria, such as the inspection lot origin, inspec- tion lot number, results recording status, and so on.  View and change usage decisions for inspection lots with a usage decision.  Make usage decisions for inspection lots without a usage decision. For this, the fol- lowing options are available: – Make a quick usage decision for multiple inspection lots. This sets the usage deci- sion code that was previously defined as the default. – Navigate to the usage decision details screen, and select the appropriate usage decision code.  Navigate to view detailed information related to a material.  Navigate to view detailed information related to an inspection lot.  Edit the usage decision code and usage decision comments of an inspection lot.  Trigger stock posting of materials of the inspection lot stock to available stock types.  Split the inspection lot stock quantity to be posted between stock types, and choose the storage location for some stock types. You can’t use this app in the context of the following:  SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM)  Handling units  Catch weight management  Batch-managed materials Quality Tasks by Processor Assignment  Shows you the number of open quality tasks by processor assign- ment.  The donut chart is divided based on processor assignment.  Selecting the header leads to the Manage Quality Tasks app, where all quality tasks in either Created or In Process status are displayed.  Selecting a section of the donut chart also leads to the Manage Quality Tasks app, but the open quality tasks are now filtered based on the processor assignment. Card Name Details Table 18.2 Quality Engineer Overview SAP Fiori App Cards (Cont.) © 805 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications  Serial numbers  Digital signatures Choose the first inspection lot shown in Figure 18.38, and the screen in Figure 18.39 appears. Figure 18.38 Manage Usage Decisions App Figure 18.39 shows several tabs, including the Quality Score History tab. The bar chart shown here charts the quality score history of several accepted and rejected inspection lots. Figure 18.39 Quality Score History in the Manage Usage Decision App 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 806

sections.title: Manage Inspection Lots
sections.en: 18.4.8 Manage Inspection Lots Figure 18.40 shows the Manage Inspection Lots app. With this app, you not only can view detailed information related to an inspection lot but also can perform certain actions, such as changing a lot quantity or rejecting a sample calculation. Other fea- tures of this app are as follows:  View inspection lots based on filter criteria such as the inspection lot origin, inspec- tion lot number, results recording status, and so on.  Create a new inspection lot.  Select an inspection lot and perform the following actions: – Change an inspection lot. – Change lot quantity. – Move inspection stock. – Cancel sample determination.  Navigate to view detailed information related to an inspection lot.  Navigate to view detailed information related to a material. Figure 18.40 Manage Inspection Lots App

sections.title: Manage Quality Levels
sections.en: 18.4.9 Manage Quality Levels Figure 18.41 shows the Manage Quality Levels app, which is based on the dynamic modi- fication rules covered in detail in Chapter 3. With this app, it’s possible to display and manage quality levels for inspection lots and inspection characteristics. You not only can view quality level history but also tighten and reset quality levels (look for these options on the top-right side of the screen). Some other features of this app are as follows:  View quality levels for inspection lots and characteristics based on filter criteria such as material, plant, supplier, dynamic modification level, and so on. © 807 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications  View the past six inspection lots for each quality level in the form of a column micro chart.  Choose View History to navigate to the Quality Level History app.  Edit the inspection stage for the next inspection. Figure 18.41 Quality Level App

sections.title: Process Inspection Lots
sections.en: 18.4.10 Process Inspection Lots Figure 18.42 shows the SAP GUI Transaction QA32 (Inspection Lots Worklist); see Chap- ter 3 for more details. Figure 18.42 Inspection Lot Selection App 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 808 This and other transactions are available in the SAP Fiori theme to support a seamless user experience across the SAP Fiori launchpad. After entering the initial parameters in Figure 18.42, choose Execute, located at the bottom-right side of the screen, so that the screen in Figure 18.43 appears. Figure 18.43 Inspection Lot Worklist Figure 18.43 shows a selective list of inspection lots with various inspection statuses. The bottom of the screen shows the options to record results, make a usage decision, or create or change defects. The top menu bar has the same options that are available in Transaction QA32.

sections.title: Manage Control Charts
sections.en: 18.4.11 Manage Control Charts Figure 18.44 shows the Manage Control Charts app. With this app, it’s possible to display and manage control charts. Control charts graphically represent the characteristic val- ues in an inspection and help detect deviations by comparing measured values against action limits. (See Chapter 19 for more details.) sections.title: Characteristic Detailed Analytics
sections.en: 18.4.19 Characteristic Detailed Analytics Figure 18.54 shows the Characteristic Detailed Analytics app that you can use to analyze inspection characteristics for which results have already been recorded. The analysis can be based on various categories, such as accepted and rejected inspections, rejection rate, skip rate, mean value, standard deviation, cp and cpk indices, and so on, based on time, inspection characteristics, master inspection characteristics, work center, plant, material, supplier, and customer. The dropdown offers other associated characteristics analytics, such as mean values and under-tolerance and over-tolerance values of mas- ter inspection characteristics. The values of cp and cpk are the process capability indices. The first value (cp) is a mea- sure for the process dispersion (is the process controlled?)—that is, how closely a pro- cess is running to its specification limits relative to the natural variability of the process. The second value (cpk) describes the position of the mean value in relation to the tolerance limits and therefore indicates whether the process is capable. The cpk is an adjustment to the cp, affecting its noncentered distribution. In other words, cpk measures how closely the target values are consistent with normal performance. For a controlled and capable process, both values should be higher than 1.33. In many indus- tries, the minimum requirement for a process capability index is now 2.0 or higher! sections.title: Manage Batches
sections.en: 18.4.22 Manage Batches Figure 18.58 shows the Manage Batches app, which can be used to display and edit exist- ing batches or create new batches. Using one point of entry, this provides quick and easy access to batch-relevant information and activities. To enable flexible teamwork, new or changed records can be stored as draft versions in the first place. All users with the corresponding authorizations can find these draft versions using the search or fil- ter options and can either discard the draft changes or continue the work. Some of the key features of this app are as follows:  Search for existing batches: – Search for single batches using enterprise search. – Search for certain ranges of batches using selection criteria and filters in this app. – Define a default filter for the following field: Material.  Edit an existing batch or create a new batch. You can edit batch-relevant informa- tion, for example: – Batch status, such as restricted opposed to unrestricted – Overview of all dates, such as shelf life or best-before date or date of manufactur- ing 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 822 – Supplier batch information if available – Overview of the existing batch classifications – Inspection lots of the selected batch – Detailed information about the batch usage, such as shipments  Use the draft concept for changed or new batches. Figure 18.58 Manage Batches If you create a new batch or edit an existing batch, all changes are saved as a draft ver- sion as long as you don’t select Save. For 20 minutes, the draft version is available. During this period, users with authorization can resume or discard this draft version. If you want to reopen a draft version after more than 20 minutes, the system forces you to discard the draft version. This is because the draft version locks all data used in the batch entry for all users—for example, material data. To limit the time all data is locked, the draft version can only be resumed for 20 minutes. Draft versions of a batch can be found using selection criteria and filters. If you open a draft version, the system dis- plays a warning, asking if you want to resume or discard the draft version. With this app, it’s possible to trigger follow-up activities such as the following:  Transfer stock of one batch of a material to another within a plant.  Get a stock overview of a single material within a plant and a storage location.  Perform further analysis and control options such as calling up the batch master for changing and displaying master data, classification data, and the batch where-used list containing information about the lifecycle of a batch.
