sections.title: Object Links
sections.en: 20.1.4 Object Links Object links are highly useful because they make document info records visible and available in many different transactions across the SAP S/4HANA system, such as in a material master record, quality info record, or sales order item. An object link serves to © 867 20.1 Configuration Steps link or cross-link a document info record with one or more SAP objects, such as a mate- rial master, sales order item, and quality notification, among others. This means that both the data in the original document info record and the originals are available in the SAP objects. Some features and functionalities of an object link include the following:  An object link refers to the SAP table and the corresponding screen number.  A document info record can either be created directly from the object link or by using a transaction.  An object link can be restricted so that a document info record can either be assigned to only one record or multiple master records.  All versions or only the current version of an object link can be displayed.  Setting up a deletion lock can prevent deletion of a document info record if an object link is maintained.  Additional functions of an object link, such as classification, long text, and addi- tional objects, can be set for providing more details about an object link.  When creating a new version of a document info record, controls can be set if the corresponding object links are also copied automatically, or they can be ignored. It’s possible to link a single document info record to many SAP objects. One document type can have multiple object links. For example, document type QM1 can have object links to both the material master and purchase requisition item in materials manage- ment (MM), whereas DMS document type Z02 can have an object link to change num- bers only. Access Figure 20.9 by choosing Define object links from the side panel for the document Type “QM1”. Figure 20.9 shows Object MARA and Object QINF, among others, which belong to document type QM1. Let’s evaluate the available option in an object link. Figure 20.9 Object Links 20 Document Management System 868 The “MARA” object is for material master, and it can be accessed by first selecting it in Figure 20.9 and then choosing Details from the top menu bar. Figure 20.10 shows the details for Object MARA, along with the controls available for an object link, including the copy function. For example, when creating a document info record or its new version from a template or from a previously created document info record, the system prompts the user regarding whether object links should also be cop- ied. You can control whether to allow or disallow copying object links while creating a new document info record in Figure 20.10. Similarly, checking the 1:n ratio checkbox allows only one document info record to be linked to one SAP object such as a material master. If this checkbox isn’t selected, then any number of document info records can be linked to any number of SAP objects. If the Deletion block checkbox is selected, the system won’t allow deletion of a document info record for the SAP object. Selecting this checkbox, for example, will prevent deletion of design drawings (document type DRW) that are linked to a change master record table (database table AENR). Figure 20.10 Object Link Detailed Screen A large number of standard object links exist to cater to various business processes in all SAP S/4HANA functionalities. If the standard object link available in SAP S/4HANA doesn’t fulfill an organization’s business needs, then a new object link can be custom- ized. For example, a company wants to create an object link of a service entry sheet in MM to the document info record, but there’s no standard object link available for a ser- vice entry sheet. A DMS expert can collaborate with an ABAP expert to develop a new object link. Click the blue information icon shown in the top-right corner of Figure 20.10, and follow the instructions on how to create a customized object link. © 869 20.1 Configuration Steps Note If there’s a business need to link a material’s batch or batches to a document info record, maintain the following entries manually:  Batch number without plant: Object “MCH1”, Screen Number “264”  Batch number with plant: Object “MCHA”, Screen Number “265”

sections.title: Define Workstation Application
sections.en: 20.1.5 Define Workstation Application The general data configuration node of DMS primarily controls how the system will process the document info records, as well as how it will display and print the originals. Here, the most important settings are related to workstation applications that need to be carefully understood and then configured because they control the different types of files and their associated applications that can be processed within the document info records, including websites. Let’s begin with the necessary configuration within the control data node. When an original file is stored in a document info record, one of the first requirements is to asso- ciate that file to a workstation application. The workstation application controls how original files are processed. More specifically, it controls which application is started when displaying or changing an original file and how the original file is printed. During a DMS implementation project, a workstation application has to be defined for each application file type that is to be stored in DMS. For example, if a company wants to store Microsoft PowerPoint files in the document info records, a workstation appli- cation has to be defined so it can be selected when a user checks in a Microsoft Power- Point file. The selection of the workstation application is based on the extensions of the Microsoft PowerPoint file, that is, .ppt or .pptx. Further, in configuration, it can be spec- ified that the Microsoft PowerPoint application launches whenever someone changes or displays a Microsoft PowerPoint file that is associated with a document info record. We’ll show the entire configuration with an example by discussing the settings for the workstation application DOC, for Microsoft Word documents. After the necessary understanding is developed, additional workstation applications required for the DMS project can be configured. Apart from the workstation DOC, SAP provides additional standard applications in the system. To set up the workstation application and the associated configuration settings involved, follow the menu path SAP IMG  Cross-Applications Components  Document Manage- ment  General Data  Define Workstation Application. Figure 20.11 shows the initial screen that appears and shows several standard worksta- tion applications already available in the SAP S/4HANA system. Double-click on the workstation application DOC, and Figure 20.12 appears. 20 Document Management System 870 Figure 20.11 Workstation Application Note We deliberately chose this example of showing how to set up workstation applications with the extension .doc. The older version of Microsoft Word has the .doc extension, but the latest Microsoft Word application has the new extension .docx. Both extension types can be managed in DMS. The same concept of an “x” in the latest Microsoft Office applications are available, such as .pptx, .xlsx, and so on and can be managed in DMS. See Table 20.5 to gain a better understanding of the fields in Figure 20.12. Figure 20.12 Detailed Screen of a Workstation Application © 871 20.1 Configuration Steps Tips and Tricks Apart from storing originals of all types such as Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, and 2D or 3D images, often there may be a need to store web addresses that users can access for important or relevant information. Here are the necessary settings: 1. Add the workstation type “HTM” (refer to Figure 20.11). 2. Maintain relevant extensions, such as *htm.*, *html*, or *.* (refer to Figure 20.12). 3. Ensure that the Data check off checkbox isn’t selected in Figure 20.12. Refer to Figure 20.12 again, and choose Define workstation application in network from the left side panel. With the WS Application DOC selected, define how the application launches when displaying or changing an original file associated with the workstation Setting Description Value WS application The three-letter abbreviation for the workstation application. “DO1” Description A short description of the workstation application. “Microsoft Word” or “MS Word” Archive identificatio The key used to uniquely identify the archive in which the original application files processed and archived with this application are stored. “*” (You can select any of the defined archives; “A3” in this example.) File suffix for appl. The suffix added to the original files when processing. This includes the change and display processes. “doc” File format The file extensions that are relevant to the workstation application. The worksta- tion application will be suggested when an original file with the extension is stored. “*.doc, *.docx*, *.*” Delete file after check-in Specifies whether files on the local machine are deleted after secure storage has taken place. Unchecked Addnl Files If this indicator is set, additional files associated with each original file can also be stored. As a result, when checking out an original file, the additional files are also included. Unchecked Table 20.5 Important Fields in a Workstation Application 20 Document Management System 872 application. For each data carrier, following are the three application types or actions that can be configured:  Display  Change  Print Figure 20.13 1 shows the key settings on the Details screen for a specific data carrier and application type in the Application (path and program name) field. In most cases, use the value “%AUTO%” for this field to allow Microsoft Windows or the local machine to automatically locate the correct program for displaying or changing the original file. If required, you can also hard-code the path to the application that is launched 2, wherein the graphics or images (2D and 3D) with extension .JPG are going to be dis- played with SAP 3D Visual Enterprise Viewer application. Here the hard-coded informa- tion is “%VIEWER-CONTROL%%SAPPROVIS%” for changing, displaying, and printing image files with the extension .JPG. SAP 3D Visual Enterprise Viewer should be installed on the local machine of the user. The three entries and the associated AT (application type) (1, 2, and 3) denote the display, change, and print functions, respectively. Figure 20.13 Individual Settings of a Workstation Application SAP provides integration to Microsoft Office products when viewing or changing these types of files. Therefore, if using the value “%SAP-OFFICE-INTEGRATION.INPLACE%” in the Application (path and program name) field, Microsoft Word will be opened directly in the SAP GUI when processing original files associated with this workstation applica- tion (see Figure 20.14). To display the original by launching the Microsoft Word application separately, use “%SAP-OFFICE-INTEGRATION.OUTPLACE%”. Alternatively, entering the value “%AUTO%” will also serve the same purpose as the system will automatically search for the relevant application (in this case, Microsoft Word) to open the file. © 873

sections.title: Document Info Record Management
sections.en: 20.2 Document Info Record Management Figure 20.14 Microsoft Office Integration If you use “%SAP-OFFICE-INTEGRATION.MAXSIZE%”, then Microsoft Office integration is started with the largest window possible. The interface technology between SAP S/4HANA and Microsoft Office is based on the link server, and that’s why the value LINK_SERV is maintained in Figure 20.14. Selecting the Export checkbox will copy and export the original in the document info record to the Microsoft application. Tips and Tricks To maintain a default storage category so users don’t have to enter it every time while checking in an original in a document info record, add workstation applications under Determine definitions for applications, and then enter the default storage category for this application in the Storage cat field. Secondly and more importantly, at least set the Display checkbox for all maintained workstation applications to prevent the filtering behavior in Transaction CV03N. If the originals are also expected to be printed, then set the Print checkbox too. Now that we’ve covered the necessary DMS configuration, let’s move on to document info record management. 20.2 Document Info Record Management A document info record in DMS contains attributes that describe the original files being stored, document characteristics, object links, and authorization groups that were previously configured. Due to the nature of DMS and how it connects with most SAP S/4HANA functional areas, understanding and using SAP’s classification system is essential. Therefore, you should first read Chapter 9, which covers classification and supports the foundation of working with DMS in detail in this section. This section will first discuss in detail how to create a document info record, including the various tabs available as well as other features and functionalities. After you under- stand how a document info record is built, the chapter moves on to cover the powerful search or find functionality of the document info record. 20 Document Management System 874 Let’s first begin with some of the key concepts and terminology frequently used for document info records in DMS.

sections.title: Creating a Document Info Record
sections.en: 20.2.1 Creating a Document Info Record Documents created in DMS are referred to as document info records. A document info record is the master record in the SAP S/4HANA system. It manages the originals and controls workflows. An original is the actual file information retained in the document info record. An original can be a Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel file, a PDF docu- ment, a design drawing in 2D or 3D format, a website, or even a text file. The storage location of an original is also maintained in the document info record. Document info records contain all the information as well as the control functions and features. In the SAP S/4HANA system, DMS uses a document info record to link the document to an SAP object, such as a material master or equipment. Before delving into document info record creation in the SAP S/4HANA system, let’s first gain an understanding of the key concepts and terminologies that you’ll see in this section:  Document types A document type is three alphanumeric characters with number ranges (internal or external) that act as a distinguishing feature of the business process. The document type controls the major functions. An example of a document type is ZQM, which stores all documents related to a supplier’s quality certification process. When creat- ing, changing, or displaying a new document info record, it’s mandatory to enter the relevant document type.  Document part A document part is defined as part of a document info record that is maintained as a separate document. This separation may be required if the original document is large and can be divided into relevant sections. For example, a large specification document has relevant information for many materials; the specification can be divided into separate parts for each material. As an example, an individual design or an engineering drawing of a product may have several complex parts, making it practical to divide them into document parts. A document info record can have up to 999 parts.  Document version A document version describes the version number of a document info record. This number is particularly important for keeping the document current in situations where modifications may have been made to specifications, engineering drawings, and so on. A document info record can have up to 99 versions.  Document statuses All major activities and even controls in a document info record are undertaken and managed based on document statuses. Some examples of user-defined document statuses include In Process, Under Review, Released, Locked, and Archived. © 875 20.2 Document Info Record Management  Document key A document key consists of four elements: – Document number – Document type – Document part – Document version Together, these four elements make up a document key, for example, 1000050/ DRW/000/00. Let’s now discuss the document info record consisting of basic data, classification, and object link, as well as associated topics in the following sections. Basic Data To create a new document info record, use Transaction CV01N, or follow the menu path Logistics  Central Functions  Document Management System  Document  Create. Figure 20.15 shows the initial screen for maintaining a document info record. Enter the Document Type “QM1”, which is the same document type previously configured and now needs to be assigned at the time of document info record creation. There’s no need to assign a document part number or version because the system automatically assigns the initial number to the document info record. Figure 20.15 Document Info Record: Initial Screen It’s also possible to create a new document info record with reference to a previously created document info record by entering the relevant document info record’s details in the Template section. Press (Enter), and the screen shown in Figure 20.16 appears 20 Document Management System 876 displaying the details for creating the document info record of document type QM1. The header shows the document type QM1. In the Document Data tab, enter a short Description of the document info record. This description is then searchable. Next, as Document Status was configured to be a mandatory field, it must be set as “UR”. (If it were set as an optional field, there would be no need to provide a status.) Table 20.6 explains the fields in detail. Figure 20.16 Document Data Tab of the Document Info Record Field Description Description A short description of the document info record. Document Status The current status of the document info record. When config- uring a document type, an initial document status will usually be set. In this case, it’s IW (In Work). User The person responsible for the document info record. Usually, the system defaults the username of the person creating the document info record, but it can be changed, if needed. Lab/Office The office or area of the business to which the document info record belongs. Authorization Group (not shown, but located further down the same screen) The authorization group to which the document belongs. This field helps drive the access and security of a document info record. Superior Document (not shown) Helps with setting up and then determining a document hier- archy. Table 20.6 Fields in the Basic Data Tab of a Document Info Record © 877 20.2 Document Info Record Management Long Text DMS also offers a feature to incorporate long text of unlimited length that is then search- able by keywords. A user of any department of an organization can create a short (or long) description and store it in a document info record, which can then be used for search purposes. For example, the details of an entire inspection method can be incorpo- rated in long text. Similarly, a summary of a presentation or an important management report, such as a board meeting, which otherwise wouldn’t fit anywhere else, can be incorporated into long text for subsequent searches. DMS offers standard long text search capability without the need to implement or install any additional functionalities. Additionally, with this standard functionality, no search engine installation (e.g., TREX) is needed. From the screen shown in Figure 20.16 previously, choose Create Long Text to open the screen shown in Figure 20.17. In this example, first enter some text; later, we’ll search for the word “Bonn” using the search function that is covered in detail later on. Notice that standard word processing features and options available in Microsoft Office are also available here. Figure 20.17 Long Text in a Document Info Record Originals (not shown) An area to attach original files to the document info record. Originals are discussed in detail later in this chapter. Field Description Table 20.6 Fields in the Basic Data Tab of a Document Info Record (Cont.) 20 Document Management System 878 Tips and Tricks Clicking on Choose in Figure 20.16 will also bring up the option to maintain long text for a document info record. Document Statuses and Status Network When a document info record is going through several rounds of review and approval processes, it’s important that the document status be updated accordingly. For exam- ple, a new prototype of an engineering component may undergo the following docu- ment statuses before it’s released for production process: Prototype → In Review → Reviewed → Released for Production → Obsolete/Locked → Archived. Document statuses enable complete tracking and monitoring of the current state of a document info record. Additionally, document status is fully supported by respective business functions. For example, a Released status of the document info record requires you to provide a digital signature, as well as ensures that further changes to the document info record are no longer possible. Similarly, a document info record with the status of Locked is available, thereby ensuring no further inadvertent use of the document info record. Whenever a document status is changed, a complete change history is maintained. Figure 20.18 Status Network © 879 20.2 Document Info Record Management The status network of a document info record ensures that a structured and logical sequence of document statuses be maintained. It requires a predefined flow of the doc- ument info record’s statuses and acts as a document control function. For example, a Released status of a document info record can’t again get the status In Review. Simi- larly, an Archived document status can’t be given back the status Created as their status sequences are predefined in the status network. Figure 20.18 (accessed by clicking Back in the screen shown earlier in Figure 20.17) shows the status network in which three sequential statuses associated with the docu- ment type “QM1” are shown in a visual form. To access a status network of a document info record, follow the menu path Extra  Status Network from the very top menu bar located within the document info record. This section discussed the Basic Data tab of a document info record. The next section about originals is also part of the Basic Data tab, but due to its detailed features, it war- rants a separate section.

sections.title: Originals
sections.en: 20.2.2 Originals Let’s add an original file to the document info record. As already mentioned, any file in the form of a scanned copy of a physical or hard-copy document, a Microsoft Word file, a Microsoft Excel sheet, or a graphic file can be added to a document info record as an original. Adding Originals to a Document Info Record To assign or upload original files, whether a Microsoft Word document, a Microsoft Excel file, or a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation from the network or a local hard drive, scroll down the Document Data tab page shown in Figure 20.19, and choose Cre- ate Original. A popup, shown in Figure 20.20, will appear where you can assign the original files to a document info record. Enter a short Description of the original file, and then define the menu path where the original file is stored. Give a description that includes keywords because, later on, this description can also be used to search originals. Use the Original dropdown to navigate to the menu path where the original file needs to be uploaded into the document info record. In this example, it’s from the desktop. Figure 20.21 shows an original file that is now part of the document info record. This process showed adding one original file to the document info record at a time, and the process can be repeated. However, sometimes there’s a business need to add multi- ple or additional original files to a document info record. Refer to Figure 20.20 again, and this time choose the + icon (Show additional files) located at the bottom of the screen. In the screen that appears, maintain the details of additional original files in the same way as previously discussed for a single original. Choose Continue. 20 Document Management System 880 Figure 20.19 Creating Originals Figure 20.20 Adding Originals Tips and Tricks You can drag and drop files into the Originals area of a document info record and they will then be automatically uploaded into the SAP S/4HANA system. © 881 20.2 Document Info Record Management Figure 20.21 Original Document Checked In Checking In and Checking Out Originals The padlock function can be activated by first selecting the originals, then right- clicking the padlock icon, and then selecting the Check In Orig. option that follows, as shown in Figure 20.22. Figure 20.22 shows several options available for managing the originals. This includes displaying, editing, saving a local copy of the original, or even deleting an original, among other available options. Checking in ensures that the original file is now saved securely in an SAP S/4HANA system and is accessible to everyone with the relevant authorization. With several icons available for the original stored files, the functions to change, display, download, or print are all available, and we suggest exploring these functionalities. First, select all three originals shown in Figure 20.22, right-click, and then select Check In Orig.. Figure 20.22 Checking In Originals A popup appears for you to enter a short text at the time of checking in the originals. Choose Continue. The next screen that appears shows that originals are now securely checked in. Tips and Tricks Apart from the option to right-click a selected original and then choose Check In, as shown in Figure 20.22, the other option is to select originals and then click on the arrow 20 Document Management System 882 pointing upward icon (third icon from the right on the bottom of the screen in Figure 20.22). Additionally, you can first select the originals and then navigate to the menu path More  Originals from the top menu bar of a document info record, and several options related to originals are available to choose from. Changing, Displaying, Deleting, and Printing Originals The bottom of Figure 20.22 shows the options that you can leverage to manage origi- nals, such as displaying, changing, creating, printing, or deleting them. When you select an original and choose the change or display option, the system opens the original applications associated with the original, which can be, for example, Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft Word, or Microsoft PowerPoint. Similarly, depending on the configuration settings made for workstation applications, visuals or image files with file extensions, such as .jpg, .bmp, .png, and so on, can be displayed within the document info record. Figure 20.23 shows an image that can be displayed when you select the image file and then choose the Display Original option. It’s important to note that this in-line display of an image was based on the settings made earlier in configuration, in which the latest SAP S/4HANA application for visuals or images, SAP 3D Visual Enterprise Viewer, was activated. If SAP 3D Visual Enterprise Viewer isn’t installed in the SAP system, then the system tries to automatically find a suitable application that can open a graphic or an image file. Figure 20.23 shows that you can make the necessary changes, such as redlin- ing, flipping images horizontally or vertically, and so on, from the toolbar available on the far-right side of the screen. Figure 20.23 Visual Display of an Original

sections.title: Classification System and Additional Data
sections.en: 20.2.3 Classification System and Additional Data The Addnl Data tab contains attributes that help further define the document info record. The attributes appear in this tab because of the association of a default class © 883 20.2 Document Info Record Management “QM1” to the document type “QM1” made during the configuration is now available to use in this Addnl Data tab. The class is defined using the classification functionality and contains a definition for each attribute, including values and whether a specific attribute is required or optional. A good deal of effort should be put into defining what additional attributes a user will be required to use. The additional attributes are important because they are used later in the search func- tion for the document info record. One of the key goals of implementing DMS is the ability to search and locate relevant document info records quickly. Classification is a cross-application SAP functionality extensively used by all the func- tionalities for indexing and searching purposes. DMS also effectively utilizes classifica- tion. It has to be set up by a DMS functional expert as searchable tags for documents, which can then be used with any of the different search terms. Different document types need to be indexed logically for easy searching, often requiring multiple search criteria to find all the relevant SAP document info records. Figure 20.24 shows that classification has been set up for DMS for document info record indexing. All the fields will eventually be available for searching. These fields are highly customizable and require no technical knowledge to set up and use. In the Addnl Data tab of Figure 20.24, notice all the characteristics that were previously created and then assigned to class QM1 in Chapter 9 are now available for data entry. Figure 20.24 Additional Data or Classification in DMS As the classification is primarily a frontend master data maintenance activity, changes can be made at any point as deemed necessary. For example, Figure 20.24 shows four quality inspectors to choose from in the dropdown. But what if the company now has a new quality inspector, Jennifer Preston, and this inspector needs to be added to the characteristic having description Quality Inspector? To do so, simply make the neces- sary update to the relevant characteristic (Transaction CT04), and the updated informa- tion in this dropdown will be automatically available to choose from. As all the controls in Figure 20.24 are basically managed through classification, you can make changes to relevant characteristics and the class so that they appear on this screen. For example, in 20 Document Management System 884 a characteristic, it’s possible to control which fields need mandatory data input versus optional via the relevant characteristic. Similarly, Figure 20.24 shows only two of the four fields (attributes or characteristics) for data input. More fields can be added to this screen simply by first creating characteristics (Transaction CT04) and then assigning these newly created characteristics to the relevant class (Transaction CL02). In addition, the data input form shown in Figure 20.24 is user friendly where data input in all fields is entered from top to bottom (vertical), and the data output is in the form of rows (left to right). Note Using classification in DMS also offers the advantage of incorporating advanced classi- fication functions, also known as advanced variant configuration (beyond the scope of this chapter or the book), such as setting up actions and preconditions, which can ensure better data entry controls. Note The Descriptions tab in Figure 20.24 enables you to maintain multiple language- dependent descriptions for the document info record. If you log in to the SAP GUI with a different language, for example, German, the document info record description will appear in German, if it’s maintained. The previous section discussed the classification functionality available in the docu- ment info record. The next section covers the Object Links tab in the document info record.

sections.title: Object Links
sections.en: 20.2.4 Object Links Object linking ensures that all documents attached to an SAP object are automatically made available. Object links are defined for individual DMS document types. One DMS document type can have multiple object links. For example, a document type Z01 can have object links to both the material master and quality info record. Object linking ensures that all document info records attached to an object are auto- matically available. For example, the material master and the line item of a purchase requisition can be assigned to the document info record. Figure 20.25 shows that the document info record 100000 is assigned to Material FG129 in the Material Master tab. Let’s now quickly recheck to see if the same document info record (100000) is now also linked (or cross-linked) to material master FG129. © 885 20.2 Document Info Record Management Figure 20.25 Material Master as an Object Link Access Figure 20.26 through Transaction MM03, enter the Material “FG129”, and choose the Basic data 1 view. Choose Additional data located at the top menu bar of the Basic data 1 view of the material master (not shown), followed by choosing the Docu- ment data tab shown in Figure 20.26. It confirms that the document info record 100000 is now linked (or rather, cross-linked) to the SAP object, material master, for the material FG129. Figure 20.26 Document Info Record Linked to the Material Master 20 Document Management System 886 Tips and Tricks You can create an object link from a document info record, and vice versa. For example, while working on a material master, it’s possible to link an already-created document info record to a material master, thus creating a cross-link between the document info record and the linked objects. Note that to link an SAP object with a document info record, the object must already exist in the system. Similarly, to link a document info record with an SAP object, the document info record should already exist to create a cross-linking. Now that we’ve covered how to create a document info record of document type QM1, let’s also briefly discuss the change and display of document info records in the follow- ing two sections.

sections.title: Changing a Document Info Record
sections.en: 20.3 Changing a Document Info Record Using Transaction CV02N (Change Document), a previously created document info record can be changed. Actions performed when changing a document info record can include the following:  Update basic or additional attributes.  Change the document status where the status of the document info record 100000 has been changed from “IW” to “UR”.  Add additional objects links.  Create a new version of the document info record.  Change an original file.  Add another original file.  Display changes.

sections.title: Display a Document Info Record
sections.en: 20.4 Display a Document Info Record Using Transaction CV03N (Display Document), a document info record created earlier can be displayed. The document info record 100000 and the Status is set to “RL” (Released), and per the configuration made earlier, when a document info record attains an RL status, the system won’t allow any further changes to it; therefore, all fields are now grayed out or disabled to prevent any further changes to the document info record. Further, the icon next to the Status field will also turn green to denote that the document info record is released. A release date is also shown next to the green icon. The lower-right side of the screen shows the updated status network. © 887

sections.title: Version and Part Management
sections.en: 20.5 Version and Part Management Some areas to review when displaying a document info record include the following:  Original file(s)  Status network  Change history  Number of versions or parts  Display changes (see Figure 20.27) Figure 20.27 Display Changes to a Document Info Record 20.5 Version and Part Management To demonstrate another key capability of DMS, let’s now briefly discuss how to create a new version of the document info record: version 01. Version 00 will remain as it was last saved, and because it isn’t released or locked, it’s still possible to make changes to this version. The important concept to understand is that now there are two versions of the document info record. The document info records are still related to each other, but each version can have its own original files, classification, settings for attributes, and objects links. In the following sections, we’ll discuss how to create a new version of a document info record as well as its new part, and then we’ll show all the versions and parts of a document info record.

sections.title: New Version of a Document Info Record
sections.en: 20.5.1 New Version of a Document Info Record Creating a new version of a document info record with reference to an existing docu- ment info record is easier. A document info record can have up to 999 parts and 99 ver- sions. Often, creating and maintaining different versions of the same document (document info record) is useful for maintaining visibility of the changes made to the various versions of the same document info record. Quickly refer to Figure 20.15. To create a new version of a document info record, use Transaction CV01N or follow the menu path Logistics  Central Functions  Document 20 Document Management System 888 Management System  Document  Create (refer to Figure 20.15 again). For this example, enter the previously created document info record, Document “100000” and Docu- ment Type “QM1”. Because the document info record’s version 00 already exists, the system prompts for creating a new version. Choose Continue. The system prompts you to also confirm copying the originals associated with version “00” of the document info record 100000. Here, select or deselect the originals to copy into the new version of document info record 100000. Select both originals, and then choose Continue. Similarly, the system prompts you to confirm copying the object links associated with version “00” of the document info record 100000. Here, select or deselect the object links to copy into the new version of document info record 100000. For this example, select both object links, and then choose Continue. On the screen that appears, the document info record 100000 and its Version 01 at the top-right side of the screen will be shown. All functions that were available while creat- ing a document info record are also available here in the new version. Make the neces- sary changes to the new version of the document info record, such as changing the status, and save. Tips and Tricks A new version of a document info record can also be created from within the document info record. For this, choose New Version from the top menu bar, and the system will trigger the necessary prompts to copy originals and object links as discussed previ- ously. To navigate to a report that shows all the versions of a document info record, use the menu path More  Extras  Versions within a document info record.

sections.title: New Document Info Record Part
sections.en: 20.5.2 New Document Info Record Part Just as a document info record can have multiple versions, it’s possible to create multi- ple parts of the same document. To do so, use Transaction CV01N or follow menu path Logistics  Central Functions  Document Management System  Document  Create. On the screen that appears, enter the previously created document info record, that is, Document “100000”, Document Type “QM1”, Document version “00”, and Document part “001”. In contrast to the prompts that the system issues for copying originals and objects links at the time of creating a new version of a document info record, no such prompts are issued when a document part is created for a document version. Choose Continue after entering the document info record details. Notice that docu- ment info record 100000 has Part 001. © 889

sections.title: Searching Document Info Records
sections.en: 20.6 Searching Document Info Records Choose More  Extras  Parts to navigate to a report that shows all parts of a document info record. The system not only shows the parts associated with document info record 100000 but also the versions and their statuses. The previous section covered version and part management of a document info record. The next section details the search function and capabilities available in DMS for docu- ment info records. 20.6 Searching Document Info Records DMS offers a very powerful search functionality that includes many search options, including by document type, document number, document status, originals, object link, classification, and short description, among other options. Another major benefit of using this search functionality is that it not only can be used to search document info records but is also a reporting tool due to its intuitive SAP List Viewer (ALV) layout (columnar format), which we’ll show in this section. The first part of the following sections will begin with discussing the initial screen of searching document info records based on a large number of selection fields and parameters available. The next section will discuss the basic attributes of document info records and how to enhance or manipulate the available data, including showing hidden fields, setting filters, downloading, and printing data. The last section will show how to search document info records based on classification, object links, text, or long text, as well as how to use the document browser.

sections.title: Search Options
sections.en: 20.6.1 Search Options To search for document info records, use Transaction CV04N or follow menu path Logistics  Central Functions  Document Management System  Document  Find. Figure 20.28 and Figure 20.29 are part of the same initial screen to search document info records. Apart from the Document Data tab, notice the following four additional tabs for the search function that we’ll also discuss in this the following sections:  Classification  Object Links  Texts  Document Browser Let’s first get familiar with the search options available in the Document Data tab (Figure 20.28 and Figure 20.29). In the Key Fields area in Figure 20.28, document info records can be searched via individual document (Document), by Document Type, by document Status (see Figure 20.29), and so on. For example, entering “QM1” in the Doc- ument Type field will bring up all the document info records of document type QM1 when searched. 20 Document Management System 890 To reduce the processing time to search relevant document info records, the Other Selection Criteria area offers additional fields, such as searching for All Versions, Latest Versions, or All released Versions of document info records, which helps narrow down the search results. Document info records can also be searched by user, by change number, or even by document info records marked for deletion. Figure 20.28 Search Document Info Record via Document Data Figure 20.29 shows that document info records can be searched based on specific doc- ument statuses as well as the file names that have been checked in as originals. Tips and Tricks Searching document info records based on the date entries in Figure 20.29 works only in combination with a certain status of document info records. Otherwise, the system displays all document info records without mentioning the entered date range. This is due to the fact that the system searches for the documents status from the entered date until the present time. If you want to search just for documents that have a certain status at the moment, just enter it in the Status field. If you want to find document info records that had a certain status on a specific date, then enter the Date From and Date To fields. The system will bring up all document info records that had the chosen status in this time period, so the document may have a different status today because the entered status was assigned in the past and then changed to the current document status. © 891 20.6 Searching Document Info Records Figure 20.29 Search Document Info Record via Originals So far, notice that in Figure 20.28 and Figure 20.29, the option is available to enter any parameter in a range or an interval. For example, in Figure 20.28, for the Document Type field, you can enter only a single value, or in Figure 20.29, there is a provision to enter only one Document Status. But what if you want to exclude a certain value within the range on the selection screen or include more document types in addition to the document type QM1? All of this and several other options are available via the Multiple Selection icon , as shown in Figure 20.30. You can choose this icon for any parame- ter where it’s available, and in the resulting screen, four tabs allow you to include or exclude single values or even an entire range. Enter information in each of the four tabs, and the ensuing output (report) will show the desired results. The available icons also allow you to copy data from a clipboard, add or delete a line within the values, or 20 Document Management System 892 use the multiple selection icon. The multiple selection icon enables selection of multi- ple values by selecting the requisite checkboxes. Figure 20.30 shows that apart from document type QM1, the document type DRW is also included so that the ensuing report will bring up all the document info records belonging to these two document types (QM1 and DRW). Figure 20.30 Multiple Selections

sections.title: Basic Documents Attributes
sections.en: 20.6.2 Basic Documents Attributes After entering parameters on the initial screen in Figure 20.28 and Figure 20.29, exe- cute the search function by pressing (F8) or choosing Execute. An example of such an output or a report is shown in Figure 20.31 where the document info records match the search criteria. Select a document info record from the list, and then either choose Change or Display to change or display the respective document info record. From there, proceed with updating or even printing the document info record, if required. In this search report, let’s explore a few important options, such as sorting the data in ascending or descending order, setting a filter, changing the layout, downloading data, and finding specific words. © 893 20.6 Searching Document Info Records Figure 20.31 Search Document Info Records List Fields Selection Figure 20.31 shows only a limited number of columns and information, whereas you can display and manipulate an enormous amount of information and even save the display layout, if it’s routinely used. In Figure 20.32, place the cursor on any column, and right-click to display all the available options—not just for that column, but for the entire report. From the dropdown list, choose Show. Figure 20.32 Data Manipulation Options Tips and Tricks Figure 20.32 shows only limited data manipulation options. Click on More from the top menu bar for additional functionalities and options, including saving a layout variant of a report or downloading the data in Microsoft Excel. 20 Document Management System 894 In Figure 20.33, the columns or fields already displayed in the report are shown on the left side, whereas the fields or columns that can be displayed (currently hidden) in a report are shown on the right side. For this example, select the four fields Inspection Date, Quality Inspector, Inspection Sites (not shown but available by further scrolling down), and Certificate Type. Alternately, click on the relevant fields in Figure 20.33, and move them with the left arrow (Show selected fields), so that the system displays the content in the report. Figure 20.33 Display or Hide Fields Transaction CV04N (Find Documents) can be used not only for searching relevant doc- ument info records but also as a complete reporting tool, which reduces or eliminates the need for custom development. Let’s now explore some more data manipulation options available. Sorting in Ascending or Descending Order Refer to Figure 20.33, and this time choose Sort in Ascending Order from the dropdown while keeping the cursor on the Inspection Date field. In the screen that appears, the quality inspector can see the dates when the relevant inspection of a supplier’s site is due. Red arrow in the columns denote whether the list is sorted in ascending (upward red arrow) order or descending (downward red arrow). © 895 20.6 Searching Document Info Records Filters While evaluating the information in a report, sometimes it becomes important to filter out some information so that the system displays only the desired information. In Figure 20.34, the fields that were selected to be shown can be seen, including quality inspector, certificate type, inspection date, and inspection sites. Figure 20.34 Fields Selected Are Shown Downloading When executing a report, it’s also possible to download the information in one of the several available forms by clicking the download icon. You can also send the informa- tion as an email attachment or perform an ABC analysis in the report. Refer to Figure 20.32 again, and this time, choose Spreadsheet from the dropdown. Copying Selective Data to Microsoft Excel To copy selected data instead of downloading the entire data set of the SAP S/4HANA system into Microsoft Excel or a different format, press (Ctrl)+(Y) to select the fields or content within the report. This enables block selection, in which you can select the block of fields to copy. Then press (Ctrl)+(C) to copy the data. In Microsoft Excel or another program (Notepad or Microsoft Word), press (Ctrl)+(V) to paste the copied data. Printing The print option is available by clicking on the Print List button in the top menu bar within the report (refer to Figure 20.32). It’s important to note that all parameters used in the generation and printing of the report also become part of the printout, including the filters. Maintaining Variants Maintaining a variant in the SAP S/4HANA system is similar to saving a layout, which is then available for repeated use when needed. You can also set a variant as the default by managing the layout options. For example, when you use the letter of credit report, you might always use the same set of fields and layout. Instead of entering all of these parameters every time you run the report, you can save these details as a variant, which can then be subsequently selected. 20 Document Management System 896 There are two areas where you can maintain variants. The first one is on the initial parameters selection screen of the report (Transaction CV04N). The second place to maintain a variant is when the desired layout is set within the report. For the first option in Transaction CV04N, simply enter the information once in the parameters selection screen, and save the variant by choosing More  Selection Variant  Save. On the Variant Attributes screen that appears, give the variant a name and a short descrip- tion, and then choose whether to make each field required, hidden, or protected from data entry. With the variant saved, the next time, you just need to choose More  Selec- tion Variant  Choose. Incorrect or unwanted variants can also be deleted via the Admi- nistration option.

sections.title: Search Additional Attributes or Classification
sections.en: 20.6.3 Search Additional Attributes or Classification In this section, we’ll highlight the importance of the attributes maintained on the Addnl Data tab of a document info record, which is basically individual characteristics that are grouped together in a class of class type 017 (document management). Through the following example, we’ll show the benefit of using these attributes. Defin- ing and spending time figuring out which attributes should be associated with a docu- ment info record will provide greater business benefit by reducing the time users will spend searching. Figure 20.35 Search Document Info Records via Classification © 897 20.6 Searching Document Info Records For the example, use document type “QM1.” This document type has an associated default class (QM1) of Class Type 017, which in turn has associated attributes or charac- teristics. Figure 20.35 1 shows the Classification tab of Transaction CV04N. Notice and recall that four letter of credit characteristics (Quality Inspector, Certificate Type, Inspection Date, and Inspection Sites) were maintained and grouped in class “QM1”. In Figure 20.35 1, select the MEAGAN entry from the dropdown of the Quality Inspector field. Choose Execute, and the search results appear 2 that meet the search criteria as shown in the last column.

sections.title: Object Links
sections.en: 20.6.4 Object Links While creating a document info record earlier in this chapter, two object links were cre- ated: material master and purchase requisition item. It’s possible to search all docu- ment info records linked to a specific object. Once again, this search feature is very helpful because you may want to find all document info records related to a single SAP object or set of SAP objects in one search. Select the Object Links tab, and then select the Material Master tab, as shown in Figure 20.36 1. Enter the purchase requisition number “FG129” to which document info records were previously linked. Choose Execute, the search results are shown that meet the search criteria 2. In the same way, document info records associated with a quality info record can also be searched with the object link functionality. Figure 20.36 Search Document Info Records via Object Link 20 Document Management System 898

sections.title: Text or Long Text
sections.en: 20.6.5 Text or Long Text Recall from Figure 20.17 earlier in the chapter that we maintained long text to include quality inspection details from several countries, including that from Bonn. The Text tab in Figure 20.37 1 displays the keyword, *Bonn*. On this screen, it’s also possible to select either the AND or ROL operator to include multiple keywords as well as the BUT NOT operator to exclude certain keywords. You may also use “*” as a wildcard character. After entering search criteria, choose Execute to start the search. The system will dis- play the document info records matching the search criteria 2. It’s important to note that because it’s a long text, the search results won’t display the long text in Figure 20.37 2. You’ll have to navigate to the detailed screen of the document info record. Equally important to emphasize here is that giving as many relevant details and parameters as possible in the various tabs of Figure 20.37 will ensure the system brings up only the relevant results from the search function. Figure 20.37 Search Document Info Records via Long Text © 899 20.6 Searching Document Info Records

sections.title: Originals
sections.en: 20.6.6 Originals Among several search options available, one more option is to search the document info records among the originals. In Section 20.2.2 of this chapter, we maintained and then checked in several originals, including an image file. In Figure 20.38 1, maintain the relevant search parameter as shown, and choose Execute to start the search. The system will display the document info records matching the search criteria 2. Figure 20.38 Search Document Info Records in Originals

sections.title: Full Text
sections.en: 20.6.7 Full Text A full-text search on the contents of original files that are stored in the system is also possible. The use of a full-text search requires a content server to be set up and the set- tings for indexing to be complete. To execute a full-text search, enter the term you want to search on in the Srch Txt field shown previously in Figure 20.38 1. Choose Execute to execute a full-text search through the original files that have been indexed by the indexing process. After search- ing through the index, the document info records that have original files associated with the search term will be returned in the search list. 20 Document Management System 900 This brings an end to the discussion on search and reporting functionalities available for managing document info records. The next section is on the SAP Fiori app called Manage Documents available in SAP S/4HANA to manage creation, change, or display of document info records.

sections.title: Manage Documents App
sections.en: 20.7 Manage Documents App Let’s now discuss the single SAP Fiori app available to manage document info records: Manage Documents. With this app, you can manage document info records and origi- nal application files. The document info records can be viewed based on filter criteria such as status, document number, document type, document version, document part, user, and document description. This app is draft compatible, allowing you to keep unsaved changes if an editing activity is interrupted and needs to be resumed later. Warning The Manage Documents app is still in an evolution phase and doesn’t yet offer all the features and functionalities that we just discussed in this chapter. The following section discusses how to edit and create a document info record.

sections.title: Editing a Document
sections.en: 20.7.1 Editing a Document The Manage Documents app screen is shown in Figure 20.39. The documents list here has been filtered to show document info records of Document Type QM1 only, but many more filters are available to choose from. Some of the options available here to use with document info records are Download Originals, Copy, Create New Version, and Show All Items (Draft and Active). The + icon is for creating a new document info record, which we’ll discuss in the next section. Right next to the + icon is the settings icon that enables you to hide or display fields in this list. Finally, the last icon (Microsoft Excel icon with down arrow) offers the option to download the data on the local machine. After setting the desired filter, choose Go, and the lower half of the screen will show all the document info records that meet the criteria. Choose the document info record (Document Number) 100000 in Figure 20.39, and navigate to the detail screen by click- ing the > icon located at the far-right side of the screen. The detailed screen of the doc- ument info record 100046 (see Figure 20.40 1 and 2) is part of the same screen that can either be accessed by scrolling down or alternatively clicking on the relevant tabs. Because this is the display version of the document info record, it can be switched to change mode by clicking Edit on the top-right corner of the screen. The Document Data tab shows the header level details of the document info record, including document status, user, and document description. As this document info record was initially created in SAP GUI (with the SAP Fiori theme), all object links created © 901 20.7 Manage Documents App in SAP GUI are available for display here. Later, you’ll see very limited choices of object links available while creating a new document info record with the Manage Documents app. Choose the Classification tab in Figure 20.40. Figure 20.39 Manage Documents App Figure 20.40 Header and Object Links in the Manage Documents App 20 Document Management System 902 Figure 20.41 displays the classification details that were previously covered in the Addi- tional Data tab in the SAP GUI version of the document info record in Section 20.2.3. Figure 20.41 Classification and Document Versions in the Manage Documents App On the Classification tab, you can find the Originals section of the document info record. Here, the far-right side of the screen shows all the options associated with orig- inals, including Check-in, Check-out, Reset Check-out, and Add a Link, which we previ- ously discussed in Section 20.2.2. Let’s now create a document info record using the Manage Documents app in the next section.

sections.title: Creating a Document Info Record
sections.en: 20.7.2 Creating a Document Info Record Refer to Figure 20.39 once again, and choose the + icon (Create Document) to create a document info record. In the screen that appears, the fields with a red asterisk denote that it’s a mandatory entry. Choose QM1 from the dropdown, and add other details as deemed necessary; include a short Document Description. © 903 20.7 Manage Documents App Note There’s no provision to enter long text in the Manage Documents app yet that we dis- cussed in the SAP GUI version of the document info record. In the Object Links tab, only two object links are available for this app: MARA (material master) and DRAW (document info record). More object links for this app are expected to be available in future releases of SAP S/4HANA. Scroll down to see the Classification area of the document info record. In contrast to the classification functionality avail- able in the SAP GUI version of DMS that restricts only one class assignment to a docu- ment type, the Manage Documents app enables you to incorporate multiple classes to a document info record. This can be achieved by choosing the + (Add) icon located on the far-right side of the screen. After a class is selected, the associated characteristics and options for each characteristic (e.g., dropdown, etc.) are all available. The Remove Assignment option allows you to remove a particular class and its associated character- istics from the document info record that was previously assigned to it. Scroll down or choose the Originals tab and notice the options to intuitively manage originals, including uploading, download, checking-in, and checking-out, among other options. Choose Save. Figure 20.42 shows the newly created document info record 100003 of document type QM1. The Edit option will offer the same options that were previously discussed in Sec- tion 20.3. Figure 20.42 Newly Created Document Info Record in the Manage Documents App Additional Features of the Manage Documents App In addition to the two major features of the Manage Documents app that we just cov- ered, some of the key features of this app are as follows: 20 Document Management System 904  Draft enablement Drafts of document info records are saved automatically in the background when- ever you add or change information within a business entity while in edit state (auto-save). This adds features such as data-loss prevention, start-now continue- later, device-switch, locking mechanism, and collaborative editing.  Search document info record You can search for a document info record using filter criteria such as document number, document type, document version, document part, document description, user, and status.  Display document info record You can view a document info record’s details such as document data, originals, object links, document versions, descriptions, and general information.  Download originals You can download one or more original application files.  Classification The classification system allows you to use characteristics to describe documents according to criteria defined and to group similar documents together in classes. Now that we’ve discussed how DMS in SAP S/4HANA works, let’s discuss the DMS inte- gration in the QM processes in the next section.

sections.title: Document Management System Integration in QM Processes
sections.en: 20.8 Document Management System Integration in QM Processes You can integrate DMS with QM processes, such as attaching the document info record to an inspection lot that’s then available during results recording and usage decision. In this section, you’ll learn how you can integrate DMS (document info record) with the following:  Inspection lot  Results recording  Usage decision  Batch master The following steps are prerequisites to integrate DMS with QM processes: 1. To integrate DMS with inspection lot, in the Object Link field (see Section 20.1.4), enter object “QALS”, and then enter screen number “500” for the document type (QM1 in this example). You have to manually enter these values because they’re not available in the dropdown menu. This step links the inspection lot to the document info record. See Figure 20.43, where document info record document 100003 links with inspection lot 160000000008. © 905 20.8 Document Management System Integration in QM Processes Figure 20.43 Inspection Lot Assignment to Document 100003 2. Access the screen in Figure 20.44, and this time in the Documents tab, you see the same document 100003 links for the inspection lot 160000000008. Notice the available icons at the bottom of the screen. An advantage that you have here is that you can create a new document info record from inspection lot creation or change transactions. To do so, choose Create Document, and the system navigates to docu- ment info record creation (Transaction CV01N). Other options, such as changing the object link, deleting, or printing, are also available here. Figure 20.44 Object Link between Document Info Record and Inspection Lot 20 Document Management System 906 Tips and Tricks Make sure that while maintaining settings at the client level in the QM area, the check- boxes for Business Process “Inspection Master Data Processing” and Switch “Docu- ment Link to Code” are selected as Active. These checkboxes are available if you scroll down to the lower half of the screen. 3. Figure 20.45 1 shows that during results recording (Transaction QE01) for inspection lot 160000000008, the Documents tab already links the document info record doc- ument 100003. This is accessible when you click the Inspection Lot Documents icon located next to Insp. Lot. You can double-click the document info record so that the system opens the original document 2. Figure 20.45 Document Info Record Links in Results Recording and Usage Decision 4. Figure 20.46 shows the same document info record link in the Documents tab, but this time, it’s for the Display Usage Decision (Transaction QA11) screen of inspection lot 160000000008. 5. To activate the Documents tab in the batch screen, follow the menu path SPRO  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Batch Master  Activate Document Management for Batches. Apart from this, you also need to maintain the object link to the batch for the specific DMS document type. To do this, the relevant objects for objects link are object MCH1 and screen no 264, and object MCHA and screen no 265. Figure 20.47 shows the document info record link between inspection lot 160000000008 with document info record document 1000003 for batch 121, in the Documents tab. © 907 20.8 Document Management System Integration in QM Processes Figure 20.46 Document Info Record Link to a Usage Decision Figure 20.47 Document Info Record Link in Batch 20 Document Management System 908

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 20.9 Summary In this chapter, we covered DMS configuration in sufficient detail. By now, you’ve gained a good understanding of the concepts and steps necessary to configure number ranges, document types, lab offices, and several other configuration items. With the configuration complete, the necessary baseline to begin using DMS in SAP S/4HANA is in place. In terms of an actual and real-life DMS implementation project, it’s recom- mended to refer to and even revisit the DMS configuration topic throughout the lifecy- cle of the project. We also described the business processes of document info record management. Most companies have developed or are still developing strategies regarding their docu- ments. Having hard-copy documents moving around an organization can cause delays, errors, and miscommunication. Scanning documents on receipt (e.g., invoices from vendors) is one way to reduce the time between approvals and payments to ven- dors. Knowledge of DMS in SAP S/4HANA is paramount when advising clients on the best practices for purchasing and other areas where management of documents and digital assets can be an issue. As we come to the end of this book, you’ve seen that the QM area in SAP S/4HANA is quite comprehensive and offers in-depth and practical solutions for many business processes and scenarios in a diverse range of industries. Not only that, it offers options that enable you to implement and integrate QM into all your important business pro- cesses. However, the actual return on investment for the SAP S/4HANA implementa- tion can be ensured only when you strive to understand the integration of various SAP areas and functionalities with each other. To achieve flawless integration during an SAP S/4HANA system implementation, you need to maintain extensive collaboration and intense coordination among the various stakeholders of the company. ©
